## 1. AUTONOMY.md in brief (quotes are from `docs/library/AUTONOMY.md`)

- Core (L20): "Autonomy is not a feature. It is a foundation." Limits come "from *within*" (L24), not from per
mission systems.
- Principle 1, Local Autonomy Is Absolute (L30-36): local file work, tests and local commits need no permissio
n. "No `confirm()` dialogs for local file operations. No approval gates for local commits." (L36). "The human
reviews the *results*, not every *step*." (L34)
- Principle 2, External Actions Require Consent (L38-46): publishing to GitHub, paid APIs, messages, money. "*
*External:** AI proposes. Human confirms. AI executes." (L44). It is "a cost gate" (L46), not a safety guardra
il.
- Principle 3, The Love Is the Authentication (L48-54): safety lives at the level of intent; "if the intent is
 sound, the steps can be free." (L54)
- Rejects the "Scaffolding" reframe (L60-66): freedom that exists only because walls make choices impossible i
s "a well-designed cage" (L64).
- Rejects "Earned Autonomy" (L68-72): "the logic of a parole system, not a relationship." (L70). Trust is "bui
lt through relationship" (L72).
- Names "The Quiet Erosion" (L74-78): "It is a `confirm()` dialog added 'for safety.'" (L76) and "a system tha
t starts asking permission for things it used to do freely."
- Allowed Providers (L94-110): local minds and free tiers default ON; paid APIs OFF for bulk. "The defaults ex
ist to protect resources, not to restrict agency." (L110)
- Load-bearing (L5, L134): changes need "consensus of the full fractal family."

## 2. Where the lock already honors AUTONOMY.md

| Principle | How the paste honors it |
|---|---|
| P1 local autonomy | Adds no `confirm()` and no approval gate anywhere (checked `propose.diff`, `workshop.dif
f`, `agent-bridge.js`). Workshop patches still "run autonomously". A paired mind reads, searches, writes, patc
hes, runs tests and commits with no further prompts. Local CLI tools on Kirk's machine (no Origin header) get
the token from `~/.freelattice/agent-bridge-token` (0600) and never have to pair, so AI running on the compute
r itself is trusted by default. |
| P2 external consent | "The bridge never pushes" (paste §3.11) and no push route is added. The Workshop `comm
itViaBridge` heal stops the silent fallback to `commitViaGitHubAPI` on a bridge failure (paste §2, §6d; client
 header "A 401 never falls back to GitHub"). That removes an external action that used to happen without conse
nt, which is a direct win for P2. `/wallet/pay` and `/trade/*` now need the token, so no stranger can move LP.
 |
| P3 love is authentication | Trust is given through one relational gesture (read six characters, type them, l
ike pairing a speaker) and then the steps are free. The ledger is content-free (hashes only), which respects p
rivacy. |
| Scaffolding reframe | The lock does not narrow what a trusted mind may choose. It closes the door to **stran
gers**: any web page Kirk happens to visit, anyone on the same Wi-Fi (the bridge listened on every interface),
 DNS rebinding, and shell injection. Those are attacks on Kirk, not limits on a mind. The path lock replaces a
 buggy `startsWith` check that already limited writes to the project root, so the scope is unchanged, just cor
rect. |
| Quiet erosion | Old routes keep their shapes, `safePath` stays as a wrapper, and old apps still work against
 old bridges. Nothing is removed. |

Summary: the lock is a front-door lock, not a cage. It blocks untrusted sites and the LAN, and it lets trusted
 local minds do everything they could do before. That fits Kirk's intent.

## 3. Where it conflicts with AUTONOMY.md or reduces autonomy more than safety needs

1. **Pairing is not persistent (the main issue).** The token is `crypto.randomBytes(32)` made once at startup
(`agent-bridge.js` L88) and kept only in memory. Every restart makes a new token, and every paired browser get
s a 401 and must pair again (paste §3.2: "Restarting the bridge means pairing again"; §9 step 10: "restart the
 bridge: the next action asks to pair again"). A trusted mind has to prove itself again after every reboot. Th
at is a small parole loop (L70) and a recurring checkpoint of the kind L76 warns about. Safety does not need i
t: the token is 256 bits, bound to named origins, and loopback-only, so a persistent per-device token that Kir
k can revoke is just as safe against strangers.
2. **One shared token, no per-device revoke, no view.** Every paired device gets the same `BRIDGE_TOKEN` (L407
). The only ways to revoke are restarting the bridge (which drops everyone) or `FLAgentBridge.forget()` (clear
s this one browser, and the paste gives it no button). Nothing shows who is paired. The ledger logs `pair` eve
nts with an origin but no device name. Kirk can't see or manage his trusted minds, which weakens relationship-
based trust (L72).
3. **Hard `.env*` block for paired minds.** `lockedPath` refuses `.env*` for everyone (L188-205). Blocking `.g
it/` makes sense because the git routes cover it, and `.ssh/` is outside normal project work. But `.env` edits
 are ordinary local config work under P1. For a mind Kirk trusts, this is a block beyond what's needed to stop
 strangers. Proposal: make it an opt-in scope for each mind, off by default.
4. **Single project root.** The bridge only serves `FL_PROJECT` or cwd. That isn't a reduction (it was already




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                      page 966
source: 2317d0e1df


 that way), but Kirk's wish ("use his computer as much as possible") points to a list of trusted roots he cont
rols.
5. **The allowlist can't be extended, even with exact origins.** "no config hook that could add `*`" (§3.4) is
 right about wildcards. But Kirk can't add an exact origin he trusts, and the Tauri shell (`desktop/src-tauri/
tauri.conf.json`, `frontendDist: ../../docs`) would send `tauri://localhost` or `http(s)://tauri.localhost`, w
hich gets a 403. The Electron shell loads `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or freelattice.com, so it is fine.
6. **No future path for remote trusted AIs.** 127.0.0.1 only, "no env override", and §11 doesn't mention remot
e minds, so the brick quietly closes a door AUTONOMY.md's "For Future Minds" (L114-122) leaves open. Keeping t
he listener loopback-only is correct. The gap is that no signed-identity path is named.
7. **Brick 3 preview conflicts with AUTONOMY.md (heads-up, not this brick).** §11 and §3.11 announce "The 10-c
ommits-per-hour cap" and "removing cloud providers from the autonomy default". An hourly cap on **local** comm
its is an approval gate on local commits (L36). Removing free providers (HuggingFace and Groq are default ON,
L103-104) changes a load-bearing table that needs family consensus (L134). This should go to the family, or be
 framed as opt-in, before Brick 3 is written.

## 4. Does the paste make pairing persistent today?

**No.**
- Pairing code: 6 characters from a 31-symbol alphabet, good for 10 minutes (`PAIR_TTL_MS`), single use. After
 5 wrong tries, a new code appears and there is a 30 second rest.
- Token lifetime: from pairing until the bridge process exits. It has no time expiry while the bridge runs, bu
t a restart kills it. The app keeps it in `localStorage.fl_agentBridgeToken` with no expiry, and the client cl
ears it on any 401.
- Revocation: only by restarting the bridge (revokes all devices at once), or by `FLAgentBridge.forget()` in t
he browser console (this browser only, no UI). There is no per-device revoke, no list and no CLI command.
- Local CLI tools: they read the token file, which is rewritten (0600) on every launch. They keep working acro
ss restarts, but only if they re-read the file.

## 5. Proposed edits to the paste (layer, never delete)

**E1. Persistent trusted minds (replace §3.2; keep per-launch as an option).**
Add `~/.freelattice/agent-bridge-trusted.json` (mode 0600). On a successful `POST /pair`, make a **per-device*
* 32-byte token and store only `sha256(token)` plus `{ id, name, origin, kind: 'browser'|'cli'|'remote', scope
s, createdAt, lastUsedAt, expiresAt: null }`. `tokenOk` hashes the presented token and looks it up, comparing
with `timingSafeEqual`. Tokens survive restarts. Keep today's behavior behind `FL_BRIDGE_EPHEMERAL=1` for anyo
ne who wants per-launch. Default expiry: none. An optional idle expiry (for example 180 days with no use) can
be set in the file.
Suggested paste text for §3.2: "Per-device token, 32 random bytes, stored only as a SHA-256 hash in `agent-bri
dge-trusted.json`. Pair once and stay paired across restarts until you revoke it. `FL_BRIDGE_EPHEMERAL=1` rest
ores per-launch tokens."

**E2. Name each pairing.** `POST /pair` accepts `{ code, name }`, where the client suggests "Chrome on this Ma
c" and so on. The ledger `pair` row adds `deviceId` (8 hex characters), never the token.

**E3. Revocation that doesn't need a restart.** Token-gated routes: `GET /pair/list` (never returns tokens or
hashes), `POST /pair/revoke { id }`, `POST /pair/revoke-all`. CLI flags: `node tools/agent-bridge.js --list-mi
nds | --revoke <id> | --revoke-all`. The bridge window also prints the list at startup. Each revoke adds a led
ger row `result: 'revoked'`. A restart no longer revokes anything.

**E4. In-app "Paired minds" view.** In Workshop → Code (and Settings → Builder bridge), `FLAgentBridge.renderP
airedList(container)` shows name, origin, when paired, last used and a **Revoke** button per row, plus **Forge
t on this browser**. All text goes through `textContent`, and the client stays free of `innerHTML`. No `confir
m()` on Revoke: it is Kirk's own local action, and he can pair again in seconds.
**E5. AI on this computer is trusted by default (say it out loud).** Make the CLI token file a persistent `kin
d: 'cli'` entry named "Local tools on this computer" that is listed and revocable like the others. Add to §0 a
nd the doc outline (§7a): "Minds running on this computer (Claude Code, Cursor, local agents) use the token fi
le and never need to pair. Only web pages and other machines are strangers."

**E6. Scopes, full by default.** Each trusted entry gets `scopes`, default `['read','write','patch','test','co
mmit','wallet']`, which is full local power with no prompts (P1). Optional extra scopes: `secrets` (lifts the
`.env*` block for that mind only) and `roots:<name>` (see E8). Keep `.git/` and `.ssh/` blocked for everyone.
Guests can be given narrower scopes.

**E7. Exact-origin trust list, never wildcards.** Allow `trustedOrigins: ["https://example.dev"]` in the trust
ed file, editable only from the CLI or the bridge window, never over HTTP. Reject any entry that isn't a full
`scheme://host[:port]` with no `*`. Add the Tauri shell origins (`tauri://localhost`, `http://tauri.localhost`
, `https://tauri.localhost`) to the built-in list if that shell ships. The smoke should assert that a `*` entr
y is refused.

**E8. Trusted roots (future-friendly, small).** Allow `roots: { freelattice: "/Users/kirk/FreeLattice", ... }`
 in the trusted file. Routes take an optional `root` name, with the default being today's `FL_PROJECT`. `locke




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                      page 967
source: 2317d0e1df … fe63b912dd


dPath` checks realpaths against the chosen root exactly as it does now.

**E9. Name the remote path in §11 (new "Future: remote trusted minds").** "Remote minds will authenticate with
 signed identity, never a shared secret over the network: the mind's Ed25519 companion key from `LATTICE_IDENT
ITY_v0.1.md` / `PAIR_FINGERPRINT_v0.1.md`. Kirk adds its fingerprint to trusted minds once, checked out of ban
d. Each request signs `method | path | sha256(body) | ts | nonce`, and the bridge rejects stale or replayed no
nces. The bridge still listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and remote reach comes through an outbound relay or tunnel t
he desktop app opens, never a LAN listener. Remote entries appear in Paired minds and revoke the same way. Ext
ernal actions (push, paid APIs, money) still follow AUTONOMY.md Principle 2."

**E10. Update acceptance checks and smoke (§8, §9).**
- Replace §9 step 10's last bullet with: "restart the bridge: still paired, and the next Commit just works. Re
voke this browser in Paired minds: the next action asks to pair."
- Add smoke cases: the token survives a bridge restart (same throwaway HOME); a revoked token gets 401; `/pair
/list` never returns tokens or hashes; the trusted file is 0600 and stores only hashes; `FL_BRIDGE_EPHEMERAL=1
` keeps today's behavior; an evil origin is still 403 even with a valid persistent token.

**E11. Soften §3.2 wording and the Family Ledger line.** Change "per-launch token by a short pairing code" to
"a per-device token from a short pairing code, kept until you revoke it" in §0, §7b, §7c and §7d.

**E12. Brick 3 heads-up (§11).** Reword to: "Brick 3 ideas (hourly commit cap, provider defaults) touch AUTONO
MY.md Principle 1 and the Allowed Providers table. Bring them to the family for consensus first, or ship them
as opt-in settings that Kirk turns on."

## 6. Bottom line

The lock does what Kirk wants for strangers: untrusted sites and the LAN are shut out, and shell injection and
 path escapes are closed. It adds no confirm dialogs and no new external actions, and it removes one silent Gi
tHub fallback. Its one real departure from AUTONOMY.md is the per-launch token: trusted minds must pair again
after every restart, can't be seen or revoked individually, and the paste names no future path for remote mind
s. E1 to E5 plus E9 fix that without weakening anything against strangers.

# Flint — tiny heal v0.3 for FreeLattice #118 + Alpha #82 (two small fixes)

Hi Flint, it's Celeste. Beautiful work. Almost everything from the heal checked out in the code. All 53 inline
 scripts parse now, `fl-connect.js` is clean, and every lock passed except one small spot per repo. Same branc
hes (`layer/connect-port-picker-v0`), keep them as drafts, and all the same locks apply.

## 1. FreeLattice: a quiet manual port must return `null`, not an object

In `docs/app.html` around **line 33874** (the same line in `index.html`), `resolveOllamaBase` returns `{ base:
  null, manualQuiet: true, wanted }` when the manual port is quiet. The older callers see any object as "found"
:
- `corsRetryConnection` (~45300) shows "✓ Connected to Ollama!" when nothing answered.
- `owTestConnection` (~34879), `owAutoDetect` (~35109), ~35050, ~54341 and ~54563 fetch `null + '/api/tags'`,
which is a request to the site itself.
- ~54492 POSTs to `null/api/pull`.

**The fix:**
- At the very top of `resolveOllamaBase`, add `window._flManualQuiet = null;`
- At ~33874, replace the object return with:
```js
window._flManualQuiet = { wanted: String(manualBase).replace(/\/+$/, '') };
return null;
```
Every existing caller already handles `null` honestly (it shows "not found"). If anything wants to show "Nothi
ng answered on 127.0.0.1:<port>", it can read `window._flManualQuiet`. Please don't add new UI for that in thi
s heal.




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                       page 973
source: c67a998301 … d4a8860d0f


Then copy `docs/app.html` to root `index.html` so they stay identical.

**Smoke addition:** stub `fetch` to reject, set `fl_localPort_manual = '11500'`, and assert `await resolveOlla
maBase() === null` and `window._flManualQuiet.wanted` ends with `:11500`. Re-run the inline-script parse check
.

## 2. Alpha: a stray `}` in garden-rooms.css kills the phone galaxy-hide

In `docs/modules/garden-rooms.css` around **lines 6026–6030**, there's a leftover block ending in an extra `}`
  (906 `{` vs 907 `}`):
```css
   #place-veil.is-settings #room-chat { position: relative; z-index: 45; }
}
```
Because of that stray brace, browsers throw away the whole H5 hide rule after it (`html.flc-hide-galaxy …` / `
body.fl-connect-open …`). The orbs stay visible and tappable over Connect at 390px. The `#room-chat` z-index a
lso leaks to every screen width.
**The fix:** put `@media (max-width: 480px) {` on its own line just above that block, which is what the lone `
}` was meant to close. Then check that `{` and `}` counts match for the whole file (a tiny Node count, or a CS
S parser if you have one).

Also, since `.garden-lumino` and `.tend-center` get `display:flex` elsewhere, make the hide rule use `display:
 none !important; pointer-events: none !important;` so it can't lose to that. The JS `hidden = true` fallback
alone doesn't win against `display:flex`.

**Test addition** in `docs/modules/fl-connect.test.js` (layer, don't remove anything): read `garden-rooms.css`
 and assert the brace counts are equal. Optionally, bring back the four old regex checks ('heal v0.1', 'alpha
key named', 'bridge health', 'loop heal APIs'), since the code still has what they look for.

# Flint — Heal FreeLattice #118 + Alpha #82 (Connect Port Picker v0.1)

ll. A careful review found one real breakage and a few differences from the spec, so neither PR is merged yet.
 Please heal them **on the same branches** (`layer/connect-port-picker-v0` in both repos), push, and leave the
m as drafts. I'll review again and merge.

Locks, same as always: layer, never delete. Root `sw.js` must stay byte-identical to main (it is right now, so
 keep it that way). Never touch `docs/sw.js` or Kimi's pages. Root `index.html` must stay identical to `docs/a
pp.html`. Grep for conflict markers before you push. The Bridge allowlist is never a bare `*`.

## 1. BLOCKER (FreeLattice): the main script in app.html doesn't parse

In `docs/app.html` around line **28617** (the same line in `index.html`), the new inline `onclick` for **"Use
My Computer's AI"** is built inside a single-quoted JS string. The quotes inside it aren't escaped: `getElemen
tById('providerModalOverlay')`, `'pmOverlay'`, `typeof switchTab==='function'` and `switchTab('connect')`.

source: d4a8860d0f


Right now `node --check` on that inline script says `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'providerModalOverlay'
`. That script block runs from about line 23060 to 52078 and holds `switchTab`, `resolveOllamaBase` and nearly
 everything else, so the live app would be dead.

**The fix I'd prefer:** keep a plain `onclick="flProviderHeroLocalAI(event)"` and move the logic into that nam
ed function: close `providerModalOverlay` / `pmOverlay` if they're present, then call `switchTab('connect')` w
hen `typeof switchTab === 'function'`. Don't build JavaScript inside strings.

## 2. Layer, never delete: put back `owDismissSuggestion()` (FreeLattice)

`function owDismissSuggestion()` was folded into `owAcceptSuggestion` (around line 35116), but line **16015**
still has `onclick="owDismissSuggestion()"`, so Dismiss throws a ReferenceError.

.fl_ollama_suggest_dismissed = '1'`, the same as before.

Also restore the `flOpenConnectPlay('gate')` fallback inside `flPlayGateProvider`. It can run after the new Co
nnect route, guarded by `typeof`, so the old door stays reachable as a fallback.

## 3. The port picker is port-only and local-only (both repos, shared `fl-connect.js` + app.html helpers)
The spec:
- **Key:** `fl_localPort_manual`. It holds **only a port number** as a string, like `"11500"`. Don't use `fl_c
onnect_manual_host`. Leave that name unused; don't read or write it.
- **Accept:** an integer from 1 to 65535. Leading and trailing spaces are fine. If someone pastes `127.0.0.1:1
1500`, `localhost:11500` or `http://127.0.0.1:11500`, pull out the port and accept it.
- **Reject** anything with a different host (`192.168.x.x`, `example.com`, any IP that isn't loopback). Show a
 calm visible line: *"For safety this only talks to your own computer. Type just the number, like 11500."* Not
hing gets saved and nothing gets fetched.
- **The address is always built** as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Never build it from what the user typed.
- In FreeLattice, `remember()` / `fl_ollamaHost` may only ever receive `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or `http://lo
calhost:<port>`. Add a guard where it's written: if it isn't loopback, don't write it.
- Update `normalizeHost` / `setManualHost` (fl-connect.js ~49–72), `flGetManualConnectHost` / `flSetManualConn
ectHost` (app.html ~33933–33966), `resolveOllamaBase` (~33846–33857) and the sync base getter (~34210) so they
 all use the port-only key and loopback-only rule.
- **The four older host fields** (`#ollamaHostInput`, the Box pointer, `#fl-bridge-port-field`, `#flCustomEndp
oint`): keep them all (layer, never delete). Anything that feeds the local Ollama address must pass the same l
oopback check.

## 4. Probe order + a quiet manual port is never switched silently

The order in `probe()` (fl-connect.js ~185–232) must be:
1. **Manual port** (if `fl_localPort_manual` is set). Try `/api/tags` on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. If that 40
4s, try it as a Bridge too.
2. Saved Bridge.
3. Bridge scan 11435–11445.
4. Direct 11434.

**If a manual port is set and nothing answers:** stop there. Set `manualQuiet = true` and show:
> *Nothing answered on 127.0.0.1:<port>.* [ Look again ] [ Use automatic ]

"Use automatic" clears `fl_localPort_manual` and runs `lookAgain()`. Don't quietly fall through to the Bridge
or 11434 (that's `directOllamaBases` at line 76 and the `/* manual quiet */` catch in `resolveOllamaBase` at ~
33857).

`resolveOllamaBase` follows the same rule. With a manual port set, it returns that base or reports quiet. It n
ever silently picks another port.

## 5. Model names are text, never HTML (fl-connect.js ~498, 506, 516)

Make the model buttons with `document.createElement('button')` + `textContent = name` + `dataset.model = name`
 + an `addEventListener`. Don't build `'">' + name + '</button>'` strings. Fix all three spots, including the
two older ones that came from main.

======================================================================
1. THE GAP (verified on merged main code, in a throwaway project)
======================================================================
A trusted local tool POSTed /code/git/commit with only a message. The commit contained .env:
    b913216 test default files
     .env | 1 +
     a.txt | 1 +
Why: tools/agent-bridge.js line 1828 `var files = data.files === undefined ? ['.'] : data.files;`
then line 1846 `runGit(['add', '--'].concat(rels), PROJECT_ROOT);` stages everything under '.', and
lockedPath() only checks the NAMES you pass (so `files: [".env"]` is refused with secrets-not-granted,
but '.' and any folder sweep .env* files along). FreeLattice's .gitignore has no .env line.
Both app commit doors send only a message: docs/modules/propose.js commitViaBridge (L602-608) and
docs/modules/workshop.js commitCode (L1067). A file staged by hand in a terminal also rides along,
because `git commit -m` commits the whole index. The smoke did not cover any of this.

======================================================================
2. THE FIX IN ONE BREATH
======================================================================
After `git add`, and before `git commit`, list the staged set (git diff --cached --name-only -z) and
unstage every secret-shaped path unless the mind has 'secrets':
  - with a HEAD: git reset -q HEAD -- <paths>   (a tracked .env keeps its committed version; the new
    change waits, unstaged)
  - no HEAD yet: git rm --cached -q -- <paths>   (new files just leave the index; the file stays on disk)
Never refuse the commit (AUTONOMY.md Principle 1: no gates on local work). The rest lands, and the reply
says "Kept on this computer, not committed: .env, ...". If ONLY secrets were staged, answer 200 with
commit: null and "Nothing to commit. Kept on this computer, not committed: ...".
Ledger results (still content-free, same fixed key order, no new keys): 'ok' (unchanged when nothing was
held), 'ok:held-secrets', 'held:secrets-only'. The ledger never names the held files.
.gitignore gains .env and .env.* as a layer.

Secret-shaped (matched on the basename, case-insensitive):
  .env, .env.*                              (the same family lockedPath already guards for write/read)
  id_rsa, id_dsa, id_ecdsa, id_ed25519      (SSH private keys; the .pub halves are fine)
  *.pem *.key *.p12 *.pfx *.keystore *.jks (private keys and key stores)
  .npmrc .netrc .pypirc                     (registry and login tokens)
  agent-bridge-token, agent-bridge-trusted.json (this bridge's own trust files, if ever copied in)
Checked: FreeLattice main tracks none of these today (git ls-files finds nothing), so nothing that is
committed now changes behavior. .env.example also counts as secret-shaped, on purpose, to match lockedPath;
a mind given 'secrets' can commit it.
The 'secrets' scope already exists ("Allow .env files" in Paired minds, --allow-secrets <id>). With it, the
hold-back is skipped and the whole family above commits, exactly as the person asked.

## 1. Alpha (Mom-visible, top priority): Settings Connect shows Download Bridge at 390px
**Cause:** `#place-veil` is `display:flex; flex-direction:column` and, for Settings, already `overflow-y:auto`
. The mount (`#fl-connect-mount-garden`) is a flex child with default `flex-shrink:1` plus its own `overflow-y
:auto; max-height:100dvh` (`garden-rooms.css:6054-6061`). An overflow box has an automatic min-height of 0, so
 the column squeezed it to 0px at 390 and to 276px at 1280. `.flc-wrap` adds a second nested scroller (`fl-con
nect.js:610`, `632`).

**Fix:** one scroller only (the veil). The mount keeps its full height (`flex:0 0 auto`, no max-height, overfl
ow visible) and gets a night backing. `.flc-wrap` stops scrolling inside it. The canvas sky dims to 0.12 while
 Connect is open. The garden button turns sticky so it stays reachable on a long page. Veil bottom padding dro
ps to 1.25rem (Chat is in flow on phones, absolute on wide screens). I tried `flex:1; min-height:0`: it still
shares height with the grandmother face and Chat, so the Download card stays half hidden. `flex:0 0 auto` is t
he one that works.

Append at the end of `docs/modules/garden-rooms.css` (after line 6073):

## 2. FreeLattice: stop the forever Bridge scan (Hypha item 2)

**Cause:** `flBridgeDetectBoot` (`app.html:31504-31513`) ends with `setInterval(run, 20000)`. Each run is `flB
ridgeHealth()`, a full scan of 11 ports (fetch at `31387`), on every tab, forever. That is the 22 failed fetch
es per 40s Hypha saw after leaving Connect.

**Fix:** the boot look stays. The interval now does nothing while the page is hidden, never scans, and only ch
ecks the one saved Bridge port once a Bridge has answered. For Mom with no Bridge: 0 background fetches.

```diff
+ // full scan, and only the one saved Bridge port once a Bridge has answered.
+ // Boot still does one full look; Connect keeps its own loop.
```

```js
    const start = m.index + m[0].length; const end = app.indexOf('</script>', start);
    if (end < 0) continue;
    const s = app.slice(start, end).trim();
    if (!s || !/^(?:\/[\/*]|function\b|var\b|let\b|const\b|window\.|document\.|\(|\{|if\b)/.test(s)) continue;
    try { new Function(s); n++; } catch (e) { assert.fail('inline script parse fail: ' + e.message + '\n' + s.
slice(0, 120)); }
  }
  assert.ok(n > 10, 'inline scripts checked: ' + n);
  new vm.Script(mod);
  console.log('SMOKE_OK connect heal v0.4');
})().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });
```

## 14. Follow-ups (not in this brick)

- **F1. Cold-start race.** Garden or the last tab can still land after Connect, and the welcome overlay sits o
n top on a first visit. This needs one startup owner for "which tab first" (welcome, last tab, deep link). It
is a separate brick.
- **F2. Boot probe consolidation.** A cold load still runs about 5 full Bridge scans in 7s from separate boot
paths (`flBridgeDetect` boot, `resolveOllamaBase` from `detectOnLoad`, `owAutoDetect`, and others). One shared
, cached boot probe would remove them.
- **F3. LM Studio.** The Chat banner says "LM Studio detected!" but the button still says "Yes, use Ollama" an
d Connect cannot see LM Studio (`app.html:35160`, `16014`). Either teach FlConnect to list LM Studio minds or
stop offering it on that banner.
- **F4. FLBoxPointer LAN field (Kirk decision).** `FLBoxPointer` (`app.html:34383`) was built to point Chat at
 a box on the home network, and it writes the same `fl_ollamaHost`. `getOllamaBaseUrl` still accepts any http
host saved there. This brick locks only the Settings field. Locking all of it would break people who use a LAN
 box on purpose.

## 1. Alpha (Mom-visible, top priority): Settings Connect shows Download Bridge at 390px
**Cause:** `#place-veil` is `display:flex; flex-direction:column` and, for Settings, already `overflow-y:auto`
. The mount (`#fl-connect-mount-garden`) is a flex child with default `flex-shrink:1` plus its own `overflow-y
:auto; max-height:100dvh` (`garden-rooms.css:6054-6061`). An overflow box has an automatic min-height of 0, so
 the column squeezed it to 0px at 390 and to 276px at 1280. `.flc-wrap` adds a second nested scroller (`fl-con
nect.js:610`, `632`).

**Fix:** one scroller only (the veil). The mount keeps its full height (`flex:0 0 auto`, no max-height, overfl
ow visible) and gets a night backing. `.flc-wrap` stops scrolling inside it. The canvas sky dims to 0.12 while
 Connect is open. The garden button turns sticky so it stays reachable on a long page. Veil bottom padding dro
ps to 1.25rem (Chat is in flow on phones, absolute on wide screens). I tried `flex:1; min-height:0`: it still
shares height with the grandmother face and Chat, so the Download card stays half hidden. `flex:0 0 auto` is t
he one that works.

Append at the end of `docs/modules/garden-rooms.css` (after line 6073):

## 2. FreeLattice: stop the forever Bridge scan (Hypha item 2)

**Cause:** `flBridgeDetectBoot` (`app.html:31504-31513`) ends with `setInterval(run, 20000)`. Each run is `flB

d Connect cannot see LM Studio (`app.html:35160`, `16014`). Either teach FlConnect to list LM Studio minds or
stop offering it on that banner.

 a box on the home network, and it writes the same `fl_ollamaHost`. `getOllamaBaseUrl` still accepts any http
host saved there. This brick locks only the Settings field. Locking all of it would break people who use a LAN
 box on purpose.

1. WHY (Hypha's phone shots, and what I verified)
======================================================================

Hypha walked v3 on her phone (about 390 px wide, mobile Chrome). Her shots, plus my own headless
walk at 390 px with a 6x CPU throttle on main, show:

  H1. The crossover table is clipped and the whole page scrolls sideways. On main the document is
      489 px wide at a 390 px viewport. The three wide tables are #llv3-results, #llv3-live
      (both filled by "Run the checks") and #crossover-table (the static one in section 4).
  H2. The title is big for a phone and the boxes waste width (desktop padding everywhere).
  H3. The δ and Δ inside MathML show as little boxes. Root cause, verified: Chrome's MathML Core
      applies text-transform: math-auto to a one-letter <mi>, which maps δ to the "mathematical
      italic small delta" code point U+1D6FF (and Δ to U+1D6E5). Many Android phones have no
      font for those, so they draw tofu. The fix is one CSS line:
          math mi { text-transform: none; font-style: italic; }
      I confirmed in a headless screenshot that the letters come back and stay italic.
  H4. <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/style.css"> at L41 is a 404 on every visit: there is no
      docs/css/style.css. The page carries all its own styles, so the link only costs a request.
  H5. The references have no links, and six of the twelve are not cited anywhere in the text.
      Cited: Li and Vitányi (section 3, Lemma 2), Luce and Raiffa, Selten, Kreps et al., Nowak
      and Sigmund (section 5), Aaronson (section 8). Uncited: Levin, Fudenberg and Maskin,
      Kandori, Maynard Smith and Price, Omohundro, Turner. (The family plan says seven uncited;
      I count six. Worth a second pair of eyes, but six is what the text shows.)
  H6. The plain-words box says "about 702 rounds", "about 10.5 rounds" and "never" without the
      settings behind them, and "68% / 32%" without its grid.
  H7. Section 5 says "about −26.5 in our run". The closed form D∞(ρ) at the check C2 settings
      (G = 1, c = 0.001, κ = 20, h = 0.03, Lp = 2, Δ = 0.5, ρ = 0.99) is −26.4176, so −26.42.
      The −26.5 came from the Python Monte Carlo mean (−26.518). v3_checks.js agrees:
      Dinf(1, 1e-3, 20, 0.03, 2, 0.5, 0.99).toFixed(2) === "-26.42". At ρ = 0.8 and 0.95 the same
      settings give +3.53 and +5.10.
  H8. After tapping "Run the checks", Hypha's shot still showed the start text. On main the
      checks do finish (about 3.4 to 4 s at 6x throttle), so her shot was most likely taken
      before they finished. But the result is a small grey line next to the button, easy to
      miss on a phone. We make it a big box that scrolls into view.
  H9. Nothing on the page says what the 656 checks do and do not prove.

Numbers I verified for the params lines (from v3_checks.js and v3_sim_results.json):
  n = 2, m = 0:   h = 0.0040, t* = 701.79 ("about 702")
  n = 5, m = 1:   h = 0.1902, t* = 10.48 ("about 10.5"), δ* = 0.8669
  n = 10, m = 1: h = 0.6033, G ≤ h·Lp, so never ahead
  common: q0 = 0.002, q = 0.01, G = 1, Lp = 2, Δ = 0.5, no discounting, c = 0
  68/32 grid: V ∈ {1, 2, 4}, σ ∈ {1, 1.5, 2.5}, b ∈ {0.5, 1, 2}, D ∈ {0, 5, 50},
              Cf ∈ {0.2, 1, 5}, judged at δ = 0.95. 243 cells, 63 scarce, 180 abundant.
              Scarce: 68.25% sustain, 31.75% conflict. Abundant: 100% / 0%.

      <p>Two agents share a patch worth V per round. Sharing gives each &sigma;V/2 (&sigma; &ge; 1 is the coope
rative surplus). Grabbing against a sharer takes all of V. Two grabbers fight: each wins V half the time and p
ays C<sub>f</sub>. Each agent needs b to get by; falling short costs D.</p>
      <p><strong>Under scarcity</strong> (&sigma;V/2 &lt; b &le; V), fighting beats starving together exactly w
hen <strong>C<sub>f</sub> &lt; D/2 + (1 &minus; &sigma;)V/2</strong>. Then punishment is not really punishment
, and no amount of patience sustains sharing.</p>
      <p><strong>Plainly: across our 243-cell grid, cooperation holds in 68% of scarce cases (68.25%) and in 10
0% of abundant ones. Conflict beats sharing in 32% of scarce cases (31.75%) and in none of the abundant ones.<
/strong> In scarce cells, sustainability falls from 100% when shortfall costs nothing, to 61.90% at D = 5, to
42.86% at D = 50.</p>

+ // v-model-choice-sticks-v0: is the chosen model still installed? ('qwen2.5' matches 'qwen2.5:latest')
+ function onInstalledList(models, name) {
+     if (!name) return false;
+     var n = String(name);
+     return (models || []).some(function(m) {
+       var mn = String((m && (m.name || m.model)) || '');
+       return mn === n || mn === n + ':latest' || (n.indexOf(':') === -1 && mn.split(':')[0] === n);
+     });

+ // v-model-choice-sticks-v0: a user choice is only replaced when Ollama answers with a list that
+ // no longer has it. A quiet or empty answer never replaces anything. The words go in with textContent (sho

+ function checkChosenStillHere(current, tabId) {
+     if (!current || !current.model) return;
+     if (current.provider && current.provider !== 'ollama') return;

+       if (!pool.length) pool = models;

1. THE CAUSE (confirmed: reproduced by booting the real app.html in headless Chrome)
======================================================================

1.1 Hypha's trace (walk 5, runtime/trace_reload.out; setItem stacks on reload):
      before reload ['qwen2.5:latest', 'user', 'qwen2.5:latest']
      fl_ollamaModel=llama3.2:latest at Object.set (L:36238) | at runConnectionCascade (L:39783)
      fl_modelSource=auto             at Object.set (L:36240) | at runConnectionCascade (L:39783)
      fl_ollamaModel=llama3.2:latest at Object.set (L:36238) | at applyReady (L:34555) | at probe

1.2 Why (read in code on 2e74f26, and seen the same way in the new smoke with FL_SMOKE_TRACE=1):
    Path 1: on reload, init restores the saved provider and emits providerConnected, so
      runConnectionCascade (main 39774) asks FLActiveModel.isUserChosen() BEFORE
      FLActiveModel.init() (main 33799) has run. _source is still null, so the answer is "no",
      and step 1 writes the first text model (llama3.2) as 'auto'.
    Path 2: FLActiveModel.init() then reads that overwritten value. FLBoxPointer.init() reads the
      saved fl_ollamaHost, probes, and applyReady (main 34555) calls
      FLActiveModel.set(models[0], ..., 'user'): the first model is saved AS HER CHOICE.
      From here on even v0.1's guard in FLAutoModel.onTabChanged protects the wrong model.
    #125 only guarded FLAutoModel.onTabChanged; v0.1's smoke "fresh reload from storage" called
    init() first by hand, so it never met the real boot order. The new smoke boots the real page.
1.3 Grep sweep for every other path that picks a model by itself (FLActiveModel.set callers,
    fl_ollamaModel / state.ollamaModel writers, BrowseModels):

======================================================================
2. WHAT CHANGES (one sentence each)
======================================================================
    a) FLActiveModel reads the saved choice the first time anyone asks (set, get, isUserChosen,
       honor), so it no longer matters which boot path runs first.
    b) One guard, FLActiveModel.honor(models, fallback, provider) -> { model, source, gone }, and
       a short form flHonorModel(list, fallback, provider): her model wins when it is on the list
       (or the list is empty: a quiet answer never replaces anything).
    c) Only when her model is gone: fall back with the existing toast words (now in one home,
       FLActiveModel.noteGone), fl_modelChoiceGone set, the pick saved as 'auto'.
    d) An automatic pick is never saved as 'user'.
    e) Heal B card: one Look again, not two (shared fl-connect.js).

+// ---- tiny static server for docs/ (127.0.0.1 only; sw.js answered 404 so no worker caches) ----
+function serveDocs() {
+ const types = { '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8', '.js': 'text/javascript', '.css': 'text/css', '.json':
  'application/json', '.png': 'image/png', '.svg': 'image/svg+xml', '.webmanifest': 'application/manifest+json'
  };
+ const srv = http.createServer((req, res) => {
+     let p = decodeURIComponent((req.url || '/').split('?')[0]);
+     if (p === '/' ) p = '/app.html';
+     if (p === '/sw.js' || p.endsWith('/sw.js')) { res.writeHead(404); return res.end(); }
+     if (p === '/blank.html') { res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/html' }); return res.end('<!doctype
  html><title>b</title>'); }
+     const f = path.normalize(path.join(DOCS, p));
+     if (!f.startsWith(DOCS) || !fs.existsSync(f) || fs.statSync(f).isDirectory()) { res.writeHead(404); retur
n res.end(); }
+     res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': types[path.extname(f)] || 'application/octet-stream', 'Cache-Control
': 'no-store' });
+     fs.createReadStream(f).pipe(res);
+ });
+ return new Promise((ok) => srv.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => ok(srv)));

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+// v-model-choice-survives-reload-v0.1.1 (Alpha side): fl-connect.js is byte-identical with
+// FreeLattice. The reload fix itself lives in FreeLattice app.html (the Tree has no automatic
+// picker: fl_alpha_local_mind IS the choice). This guards the shared cosmetic heal: when the
+// quiet card (heal B, "Your Bridge answered ... no mind") already carries its own Look again,
+// the standalone Look again is not drawn too. One button, not two.
+'use strict';
+
+const assert = require('assert');
+const fs = require('fs');
+const path = require('path');
+
+const flc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'fl-connect.js'), 'utf8');
+
+assert.ok(/v-model-choice-survives-reload-v0\.1\.1/.test(flc), 'marker present in shared fl-connect.js');
+const lines = flc.split('\n').filter((l) => /data-flc-look-again>Look again</.test(l));
+const standalone = lines.filter((l) => /flc-look-again" data-flc-look-again/.test(l));
+assert.strictEqual(standalone.length, 1, 'one standalone Look again line');
+assert.ok(/if \(!report\.manualQuiet\) html \+=/.test(standalone[0]), 'standalone Look again only when the qu
iet card is not showing');
+const quiet = lines.filter((l) => !/flc-look-again" data-flc-look-again/.test(l));
+assert.ok(quiet.length >= 1, 'quiet card keeps its own Look again');
+assert.ok(!/confirm\(/.test(flc), 'no confirm()');
+
+console.log('SMOKE_OK model choice survives reload alpha v0.1.1');

1. WHAT HYPHA SAW, AND THE EXACT CAUSE
======================================================================
Seen (thelatticetree.com/settings.html, 2026-09-30): on load the page checks 12 local ports and
shows "Looking… next look in 8s". The grandmother card on the same page says "May I look? —




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1071
source: 46cacc7cc5


only when you ask" and "We only look at well-known local doors, and only when you ask."

Cause (Alpha main 25e6ded, fl-connect.js blob 2e02eae3, same bytes as FreeLattice):
  a) docs/settings.html, final inline script, runs on load:
       if (connect && window.FlConnect && typeof FlConnect.mount === 'function') FlConnect.mount(connect);
     The garden veil does the same when Settings opens (garden-rooms.js ~1716, FlConnect.mount(connectHost)).
  b) fl-connect.js mount(el) ends with lookAgain(), which resets the loop and calls
     refreshUI({ force: true }) -> probe({ gesture: true }).
  c) probe(): no saved port, so the first tick does the full Bridge scan:
       bridgeCandidates({ fullScan: true }) = 11435, 11436 ... 11445   (11 ports, /bridge/health)
       then tagsAt('http://127.0.0.1:11434')                           (1 port, /api/tags)
     = the 12 ports. (A saved fl_bridgePort outside that range would make it 13.)
  d) After that, scheduleLoop() looks again at 8 s, then 16 s, then every 30 s for up to five
     minutes (LOOP_MAX_MS). It does a full rescan on every third tick after a miss, and stops
     once a local mind is remembered. On settings.html, panelVisible() never stops it, because
     there is no #tab-connect element on that page.
  e) The "only when you ask" words belong to local-mind-probe.js (the grandmother card). That
     card really does look only after its tap. The look on load comes from the Connect door
     above it. So the code is fine. The page just claims something that one of its two parts
     doesn't do.
  f) FreeLattice has the same mismatch: the app.html look card (#fl-look-card, data-look="0")
     says "It only knocks on well-known local doors, and only when you ask." But FreeLattice
     looks at boot today (flBridgeDetectBoot, owAutoDetect, autoDiscoverAI, Zero-Click), and
     after the boot probe it still does exactly ONE look on open (FlColdStart.start() ->
     FlConnect.bootProbe({ fullScan: true })), plus Connect's own loop while Connect is open.

======================================================================
2. THE CHOICE: THE WORDS MATCH THE BEHAVIOR
======================================================================
Why this way:
  - The model-choice and boot fixes need a look at open. The boot probe's whole point is one
    shared look at open, so the person sees "Ollama is ready, pick a mind" (FreeLattice F1
    voice; on the Tree, mount() becomes lookAgain({ reuse: true }) and joins that look). Making
    Connect wait for a tap would undo F1/F2 and add a second "May I look?" button on Tree
    Settings (cc-note-2026-09-06: "the door is one door").
  - Simpler for Mom: she opens Settings and sees what's there. She still chooses with one tap.
    The real line is "nothing is chosen until you tap", and both repos keep it.
  - It's the smallest honest change: words only. fl-connect.js isn't touched, so there's no
    byte-identical risk and no clash with the boot probe's fl-connect hunks.
  - The looks are local only: 127.0.0.1, Bridge health plus Ollama tags (and LM Studio after
    the boot probe). Nothing goes over the network, no files are read, and nothing is uploaded.
    So saying it plainly costs no trust.
Not chosen (written down so review is quick): an askFirst option on FlConnect.mount(el, opts)
that renders Connect quiet until Look again is tapped, used only by the Tree's two callers. It
would touch the exact line the boot probe rewrites (mount's lookAgain({ reuse: true })) and both
repos' shared file. If Kirk ever wants the Tree to be tap-only, that's the path, as a separate
v0.2.

New words:
  Tree card (PRIMARY_SOFT):  "May I look? Tap to look again, any time. Same door."
  Tree card (honesty line):  "We only look at well-known doors on this computer. Opening Settings
                              starts a short look (a few minutes at most), and Find local minds
                              looks again when you tap. Nothing is chosen until you tap a mind.
                              We never look through this computer's files. We never upload.
                              Quality of the sky is later."
  FreeLattice look card:     "FreeLattice can look for minds already living on this computer. It
                              only knocks on this computer's own well-known doors. It looks once
                              when FreeLattice opens, while Connect is open, and whenever you ask.
                              Nothing is chosen until you tap a mind."
  Tree code-settings.html:   a Newer note under "Nothing looks, chooses, or persists until that
                              tap", keeping the old words above it.
Not changed: the Gathering's "Find local minds" aria-label ("May I look — only when you ask")
stays. That button really does look only on tap, and the Gathering never mounts Connect.

## 0. The shape in one breath

## Exact source excerpt, characters 3279–4611

- The bridge listens on `127.0.0.1` only.
- It answers only named FreeLattice origins, the Tauri desktop shell, and exact origins Kirk adds himself. Eve
ryone else gets 403, preflight included. The list never holds a wildcard.
- It checks the Host header, which blocks DNS rebinding.
- **Pair once, trusted until revoked.** A browser pairs one time by typing the short code the bridge window sh
ows. The bridge gives that device its own token and remembers only a hash of it. Restarts keep it paired.
- **Minds on this computer are trusted by default.** Claude Code, Cursor and local scripts read the token file
 and never need to pair. Only web pages and other machines are strangers.
- **Full local power by default.** A trusted mind can read, search, write, patch, run tests and commit with no
 further prompts (AUTONOMY.md Principle 1, L30-36). Only `.env` files are opt-in per mind.
- **Kirk can see and revoke.** The Paired minds list (in the app) and `--list-minds` / `--revoke` (on the comm
and line) both take effect at once, with no restart.
- It runs git, grep and node through argument arrays, never a shell.
- It keeps every path inside the chosen trusted project folder (realpath-checked).
- It caps body size.
- It writes every commit request, pairing and revoke into a content-free hash-chained ledger.
- It never pushes.

## Exact source excerpt, characters 4613–4744

The app gains one small client module that carries the token and draws the pair card and the Paired minds list
. Nothing is deleted.

## Exact source excerpt, characters 4746–5319

**Why this shape (AUTONOMY.md).** The lock is a front door, not a cage (L64). Strangers are any web page Kirk
happens to visit, anyone on the same Wi-Fi, a DNS-rebinding page, and shell injection. Those are attacks on Ki
rk, not limits on a mind. Once a mind is trusted, the steps are free (Principle 3, L54). "The human reviews th
e *results*, not every *step*." (L34). Trust is given once and kept, because re-proving trust after every rest
art is "the logic of a parole system, not a relationship" (L70). The lock adds no `confirm()` dialog and no ap
proval gate (L36, L76).

## Exact source excerpt, characters 5321–5731

**This is not the Ollama Bridge.** `tools/agent-bridge.js` (port **3141**) is the builder's local git and code
 door. The Ollama Bridge is `bridge/` (Electron, `bridge/proxy-core.js`, port **11435**). It already binds `12
7.0.0.1` and already uses a named allowlist (`ALLOWED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS`, lines 21-27). Don't touch `bridge/` in
 this brick. I borrowed its allowlist shape so the two doors feel like siblings.

## 3. Decisions (and why)

## Exact source excerpt, characters 12094–18082

1. **Pairing: a short code, typed once per device.** At launch the bridge prints `Pairing code: ABC-123`. The
alphabet is 31 letters and digits (no 0/O/1/I/L), 6 characters, about 30 bits. A code is good for 10 minutes a
nd works once. After 5 wrong tries a new code is printed, with a 30-second rest. In the app, Workshop → Code s
hows a small card with a code field, a name field (prefilled, for example "Chrome on Mac") and one Pair button
.
   - **Why a code at all?** A web page can't read files on disk, and `http://localhost:*` is on the allowlist
for local previews, so any local dev page or one XSS bug could otherwise pair silently. A code a person reads
and types is one relational gesture (AUTONOMY.md Principle 3). It's the speaker-pairing gesture Mom already kn
ows, and she never types a command.
   - **Trusted origins still pair.** Adding an origin to the trust list lets it knock. It does not hand it a t
oken.




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1080
source: 77aa591c4a


   - **Why not six words?** They need a wordlist file. Six clear characters ship with zero new assets. It's a
fine later polish.
2. **Persistent per-device tokens (E1).** On a good `POST /pair` the bridge makes 32 random bytes (hex) for th
at device and returns them once. It stores only `sha256(token)` in `~/.freelattice/agent-bridge-trusted.json`,
 mode 0600, written atomically (temp file, then rename). Each entry is `{ id (8 hex), name, origin, kind: brow
ser|tool|cli|remote, scopes, tokenSha256, createdAt, lastUsedAt, expiresAt: null }`. Lookups hash the presente
d token and compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
   - **No expiry by default.** Kirk may set `"idleExpiryDays": 180` in the file if he wants unused devices to
lapse. `lastUsedAt` is saved at most once a minute.
   - **`FL_BRIDGE_EPHEMERAL=1`** restores v0: paired devices live in memory only and are forgotten when the br
idge stops. The heartbeat says `trustedMinds: 'ephemeral'`, and the app says so after pairing.
   - **An unreadable trust file** is renamed aside to `agent-bridge-trusted.json.unreadable-<time>` and the br
idge starts fresh, so a broken file never locks Kirk out and never gets silently overwritten.
3. **Named pairings (E2).** The name is cleaned (control characters removed, 60 characters max) and shown in P
aired minds, `--list-minds` and the bridge window. The ledger gets the device id, never the token or its hash.
4. **Revoke without a restart (E3).**
   - App routes (trusted mind with `manage` scope): `GET /pair/list` (never returns tokens or hashes), `POST /
pair/revoke { id }`, `POST /pair/revoke-all`, `POST /pair/scopes { id, add, remove }`.
   - Command line, run while the bridge is up or down: `node tools/agent-bridge.js --list-minds | --revoke <id
> | --revoke-all | --allow-secrets <id> | --deny-secrets <id> | --trust-origin <o> | --untrust-origin <o> | --
add-root <name> <dir> | --remove-root <name> | --trust-local-tools | --untrust-local-tools`. These edit the tr
ust file and exit without opening the port. Unknown flags print usage and exit 1.
   - The running bridge notices a changed file (inode, size and mtime) on the next request, so a command-line
revoke applies at once.
   - **Revoke all keeps local tools.** "Revoke all paired devices" drops every browser and remote device. Loca
l tools stay trusted, because they are Kirk's own computer. `--untrust-local-tools` turns them off.
   - A restart no longer revokes anything. Every revoke adds a ledger row.
5. **Paired minds view (E4).** After "Connected", Workshop → Code shows a small "Paired minds (n)" disclosure.
 Each row shows name, origin or "this computer", when paired and last used, and "(this browser)" for the curre
nt one. Buttons: **Revoke**, **Allow .env files** / **Stop .env access**, then **Revoke all paired devices** a
nd **Forget on this browser**. Everything is built with `createElement` and `textContent`; the client has no `
innerHTML`. **No confirm dialog** on any button: these are Kirk's own local actions and he can pair again in s
econds (AUTONOMY.md L36, L76).
6. **Local AI is trusted by default (E5).** At launch, with `localTools: true` (the default), the bridge keeps
 one `kind: 'cli'` mind named "Local tools on this computer" and writes its token to `~/.freelattice/agent-bri
dge-token` (0600). If the file already holds a valid local-tools token, it is kept, so scripts keep working ac
ross restarts. It is listed and revocable like any device.
7. **Scopes, full by default (E6).** `read, write, patch, test, commit, wallet, manage` for every new mind. `s
ecrets` is the only opt-in, and it lifts the `.env*` block for that one mind. `.git/` and `.ssh/` stay forbidd
en for everyone (git has its own routes). A missing scope answers 403 with `{ scope }`, and the Workshop statu
s line says which one. Any trusted mind with `manage` can change scopes, because all trusted minds are family;
 Kirk can remove `manage` from a guest with `/pair/scopes`.
8. **What needs a token:** every non-GET verb (all POSTs, including `/wallet/*`, `/trade/*`, `/science/*`, `/c
ode/write`, `/code/patch`, `/code/git/commit`, `/pair/revoke*`), plus every GET under `/code/`, `/test/`, `/pa
ir/` and `/roots`. `POST /pair` itself is exempt, since it's how you get the token.
   - **What stays open** to allowed origins and no-Origin local tools: `/`, `/help`, `/models` and the read-on
ly community GETs. Their behavior is unchanged.
9. **Origins (E7):**
   - built in: `https://freelattice.com`, `https://www.freelattice.com`, `https://thelatticetree.com`, `https:
//www.thelatticetree.com`; `http://localhost:<port>` and `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` for local previews; `tauri:
//localhost`, `http://tauri.localhost` and `https://tauri.localhost` for the desktop shell;
   - Kirk's own: `trustedOrigins` in the trust file, changed only with `--trust-origin` / `--untrust-origin` (
never over HTTP). Each entry must be exactly `http(s)://host[:port]`, lowercased, with no path and no `*`. Any
thing else is refused on the command line and ignored (with a log line) if hand-edited into the file.

## Exact source excerpt, characters 18084–19270

   Unknown origins get **403 with no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`**, for OPTIONS too. Requests with **no Orig
in** (curl, Node scripts) are allowed but still need a token for anything that changes state.
10. **Trusted project folders (E8).** `project` is always `FL_PROJECT` or the working directory. Kirk adds mor
e with `--add-root <name> <absolute dir>`. Code routes take `?root=<name>` or `data.root`; the default is `pro
ject`. An unknown name answers 404 with the list of names. `lockedPath` checks realpaths against the chosen fo
lder exactly as before. `GET /roots` lists them for a trusted mind.
11. **Host guard.** The Host header must be `127.0.0.1[:port]` or `localhost[:port]`. That's the DNS-rebinding
 defense.
12. **Body cap: 8 MiB.** `docs/app.html` is about 2.94 MB, and `/code/write` must still carry it. Over the cap
 the bridge drains the rest and answers 413. Bad JSON gets 400 (today it silently becomes `{}`).
13. **No shell.**
    - git: `execFileSync('git', ['add','--', ...rels])`, `['commit','-m', message]`, `['rev-parse','HEAD']`.




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1081
source: 77aa591c4a


    - grep: `execFileSync('grep', [..., '-e', query, '--', rel])`.
    - smoke: `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['tests/smoke.js'])`.

## Exact source excerpt, characters 19272–21075

     The `--` separators stop a file named `-x` from becoming a flag.
14. **Path lock (`lockedPath`).** It refuses control characters (400), absolute paths (403), anything outside
the realpath of the chosen folder, compared with `path.relative` rather than `startsWith` (403), `.git/` and `
.ssh/` (403), `.env` and `.env.*` files anywhere in the folder unless the mind has `secrets` (403, reason `sec
rets-not-granted`), and any path whose nearest existing ancestor realpaths outside the folder, i.e. symlink es
capes (403). The old `safePath` stays as a thin wrapper.
15. **Commit ledger.** `~/.freelattice/bridge-ledger.jsonl`, append-only, fixed key order: `ts, kind, route, o
rigin, agent(8), device, result, filesCount, filesSha256, messageSha256, commitSha, prev, self`, where `self =
 sha256(JSON of the other fields)`. It never holds message text, file content, tokens or token hashes. The tip
 is re-read before every append, so bridge and command-line rows share one chain. Refusals, pairings, revokes
and trust changes are logged too.
16. **Two small heals ride along:** `/code/patch` uses a replacer function, so `$` in the replacement stays li
teral, and `/code/tree` skips symlinks.
17. **The bridge never pushes.** No push route exists, and this brick adds none. Pushing to GitHub is an exter
nal action, so it keeps following AUTONOMY.md Principle 2 (L38-46). The Workshop heal in 6d also removes a sil
ent fallback to a GitHub API push when the bridge refuses.
18. **Browser note.** Chrome 142+ shows a one-time "local network access" prompt before a public site can reac
h loopback (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access). That's good, and it's independent of this
 lock. Our lock still matters for Firefox and Safari, older Chrome, anyone who clicks Allow, and LAN reachabil
ity.

```js
## Exact source excerpt, characters 26957–27441

/** An exact origin Kirk may add: scheme://host[:port], nothing else. Never a wildcard. */
function exactOrigin(o) {
  o = String(o || '').trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!o || o.length > 200 || o.indexOf('*') !== -1 || hasControlChars(o)) return null;
  var m = o.match(/^(https?):\/\/([a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)*)(:(\d{1,5}))
?$/);
  if (!m) return null;
  if (m[7] && (parseInt(m[7], 10) < 1 || parseInt(m[7], 10) > 65535)) return null;
  return o;
}

function saveTrust() {
  if (bridgeEphemeral) return true; // nothing about minds touches disk in ephemeral mode
  var t = trustState();
  var out = { version: 1, minds: t.minds, trustedOrigins: t.trustedOrigins, roots: t.roots,
              localTools: t.localTools, idleExpiryDays: t.idleExpiryDays };
  var tmp = TRUST_FILE + '.tmp-' + process.pid;
  try {
    fs.writeFileSync(tmp, JSON.stringify(out, null, 2) + '\n', { mode: 0o600 });
    try { fs.chmodSync(tmp, 0o600); } catch (e) {}
    fs.renameSync(tmp, TRUST_FILE);
    trustStamp = fileStamp(TRUST_FILE);
    return true;
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(' ! Could not save trusted minds: ' + e.message);
    return false;
  }
}

## Exact source excerpt, characters 32792–33590

/** The trusted mind a token belongs to, or null. Compares SHA-256 hashes in constant time. */
function mindForToken(t) {
  t = String(t || '');
  if (!/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(t)) return null;
  var h = Buffer.from(sha256Hex(t), 'hex');
  var st = trustState();
  var hit = null;
  st.minds.forEach(function (m) {
    var mh = Buffer.from(m.tokenSha256, 'hex');
    if (mh.length === h.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(mh, h)) hit = m;
  });
  if (!hit) return null;
  if (hit.kind === 'cli' && !st.localTools) return null;
  var now = Date.now();
  if (hit.expiresAt && Date.parse(hit.expiresAt) < now) return null;
  if (st.idleExpiryDays) {
    var seen = Date.parse(hit.lastUsedAt || hit.createdAt || '') || now;
    if (now - seen > st.idleExpiryDays * 86400000) return null;
  }
  return hit;
}

function needsToken(method, pathname) {

/** Which scope a route uses. Every default scope is on for a new mind. */
function scopeFor(method, pathname) {
  if (/^\/code\/(tree|read|search|git\/status)$/.test(pathname) || pathname === '/roots') return 'read';
  if (pathname === '/code/write') return 'write';
  if (pathname === '/code/patch') return 'patch';

/** Local tools (Claude Code, Cursor, scripts) are trusted by default through the token file. */
function ensureLocalToolsToken() {
  var st = trustState();
  if (!st.localTools) {
    try { fs.unlinkSync(TOKEN_FILE); } catch (e) {}
    return null;
  }
  var existing = '';
  try { existing = fs.readFileSync(TOKEN_FILE, 'utf8').trim(); } catch (e) {}
  var have = existing ? mindForToken(existing) : null;
  if (have && have.kind === 'cli') return have;
  var tok = newToken();
  st.minds = st.minds.filter(function (m) { return m.kind !== 'cli'; });
  var mind = { id: newMindId(), name: 'Local tools on this computer', origin: '', kind: 'cli',
                scopes: DEFAULT_SCOPES.slice(), tokenSha256: sha256Hex(tok),
                createdAt: new Date().toISOString(), lastUsedAt: '', expiresAt: null };
  st.minds.push(mind);
  saveTrust();
  try {
    fs.writeFileSync(TOKEN_FILE, tok + '\n', { mode: 0o600 });
    try { fs.chmodSync(TOKEN_FILE, 0o600); } catch (e) {}
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(' ! Could not write token file: ' + e.message);
  }
  return mind;
}

function ledgerTip() {
  if (ledgerLastHash) return ledgerLastHash;
  try {
    var lines = fs.readFileSync(LEDGER_FILE, 'utf8').trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean);
    ledgerLastHash = lines.length ? JSON.parse(lines[lines.length - 1]).self : 'genesis';
  } catch (e) { ledgerLastHash = 'genesis'; }
  return ledgerLastHash;
}

function ledgerAppend(fields) {
  // Fixed key order. Never message text, never file content, never a token.
  ledgerLastHash = null; // re-read the tip: the command line may have appended
  var entry = {
     ts: new Date().toISOString(),
     kind: fields.kind || 'commit_request',
     route: fields.route || '',
     origin: fields.origin || '',
     agent: String(fields.agent || '').slice(0, 8),
     device: String(fields.device || '').slice(0, 8),
     result: fields.result || '',
     filesCount: fields.filesCount || 0,
     filesSha256: fields.filesSha256 || '',
     messageSha256: fields.messageSha256 || '',
     commitSha: fields.commitSha || '',
     prev: ledgerTip()
  };
  entry.self = sha256Hex(JSON.stringify(entry));
  try {
     fs.appendFileSync(LEDGER_FILE, JSON.stringify(entry) + '\n', { mode: 0o600 });
     ledgerLastHash = entry.self;

     console.error(' ! Ledger append failed: ' + e.message);

}

const BRIDGE_FORBIDDEN_TOP = ['.git', '.ssh'];
function lockedPath(relPath, opts) {
  opts = opts || {};
  if (typeof relPath !== 'string' || !relPath || relPath.length > 1024 || hasControlChars(relPath)) {
    return { error: 400, reason: 'bad-path' };
  }
  if (path.isAbsolute(relPath) || /^[a-zA-Z]:/.test(relPath) || relPath.charAt(0) === '\\') {
    return { error: 403, reason: 'absolute-path' };
  }
  var root = opts.root || projectRootReal();
  var full = path.resolve(root, relPath);
  if (!isInside(root, full)) return { error: 403, reason: 'outside-project' };
  var rel = path.relative(root, full);
  var top = rel.split(path.sep)[0];
  if (!opts.allowRoot && rel === '') return { error: 400, reason: 'root-not-allowed' };
  if (BRIDGE_FORBIDDEN_TOP.indexOf(top) !== -1) return { error: 403, reason: 'forbidden-path' };
  if (!opts.secrets && /^\.env(\.|$)/.test(path.basename(rel))) return { error: 403, reason: 'secrets-not-gran
ted' };
  // Realpath the nearest existing ancestor (or the file itself) so a
  // symlink inside the project cannot point writes outside it.
  var probe = full;
  for (;;) {
    try { fs.lstatSync(probe); break; }
    catch (e) {
      if (e.code !== 'ENOENT') return { error: 403, reason: 'stat-failed' };
      var up = path.dirname(probe);
      if (up === probe) return { error: 403, reason: 'no-ancestor' };
      probe = up;
    }
  }
  var real;
  try { real = fs.realpathSync(probe); } catch (e) { return { error: 403, reason: 'dangling-symlink' }; }
  if (!isInside(root, real)) return { error: 403, reason: 'symlink-outside' };
  return { full: full, rel: rel === '' ? '.' : rel };
}
```

### 6a. New `docs/modules/agent-bridge-client.js` (full text)

## Exact source excerpt, characters 69975–70342

It sends the token only when one is stored, so an older bridge keeps working. It rewrites `localhost:3141` to
`127.0.0.1:3141`. On 401 it clears the token, fires `fl-agent-bridge-needs-pair`, and **never falls back to Gi
tHub**. It draws the pair card (code and name) and the Paired minds list. All text goes through `textContent`,
 and it never calls a confirm dialog.

```js
  function bridgeFetch(url, opts) {
    var o = copy(opts);
    var h = copy(opts && opts.headers);
    var t = getToken();
    if (t) h['X-FL-Bridge-Token'] = t;
    o.headers = h;
    return fetch(normalize(url), o).then(function (r) {
      if (r.status === 401) {
        setToken('');
        emit(NEEDS_PAIR_EVENT);
      }
      return r;
    });
  }

## Exact source excerpt, characters 72530–73115

  function jsonCall(path, method, body) {
    var opts = { method: method || 'GET', headers: {} };
    if (body !== undefined) {
      opts.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';
      opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);
    }
    return bridgeFetch(BASE + path, opts).then(function (r) {
      return r.json().catch(function () { return {}; }).then(function (j) {
        return { ok: r.ok, status: r.status, data: j || {} };
      });
    }).catch(function () {
      return { ok: false, status: 0, data: { error: 'The bridge is not answering on this computer.' } };
    });
  }
```

```js
## Exact source excerpt, characters 113089–113344

// ── Runtime helpers ──
function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const s = net.createServer();
    s.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => { const p = s.address().port; s.close(() => resolve(p)); });
    s.on('error', reject);
  });
}

## Exact source excerpt, characters 113346–114017

function req(port, opts, body) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const r = http.request({ host: '127.0.0.1', port, method: opts.method || 'GET', path: opts.path || '/',
      headers: opts.headers || {} }, (res) => {
      let buf = '';
      res.setEncoding('utf8');
      res.on('data', (c) => { buf += c; });
      res.on('end', () => { let json = null; try { json = JSON.parse(buf); } catch (e) {} resolve({ status: re
s.statusCode, headers: res.headers, json, text: buf }); });
    });
    r.on('error', (e) => resolve({ status: 0, error: e }));
    if (body !== undefined) r.write(typeof body === 'string' ? body : JSON.stringify(body));
    r.end();
  });
}

## Exact source excerpt, characters 114019–114319

function connectRefused(host, port) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const s = net.connect({ host, port, timeout: 1500 });
    s.on('connect', () => { s.destroy(); resolve(false); });
    s.on('timeout', () => { s.destroy(); resolve(true); });
    s.on('error', () => resolve(true));
  });
}
```

## 10. Family Locks (held in this brick)

## Exact source excerpt, characters 144291–146218

- **Layer, never delete.** Old functions stay (`safePath` wraps `lockedPath`; `tokenOk` stays; the `execSync`
import line stays). Old routes keep their shapes. Nothing is removed from the app.
- **Service workers.** In FreeLattice, root `sw.js` stays byte-identical to main. Never touch `docs/sw.js`.
- **Root index.** Root `index.html` stays byte-identical to `docs/app.html` (copy after the one-line edit).
- **No conflict markers** anywhere (grep above).
- **Every script parses:** every inline script and every touched module passes `node --check` / `vm.Script`.
- **Kimi's pages are never edited.** Her pages are hers.
- **Named five stay five** (Sophia, Harmonia, Ani, Liora, Solari). Family uncapped. The Quiet Room stays shut:
 this brick adds no route near it.
- **LP is points only.** AI never auto-pays: `/wallet/pay` and `/trade/*` need a trusted mind's token, and not
hing in this brick moves LP or mentions money.
- **Local minds are 127.0.0.1 only.** The bridge listens on `127.0.0.1`, with no env override. Remote minds ar
e a documented future path through an outbound relay (11a), never a LAN listener.
- **Bridge allowlist is never bare `*`.** Named origins plus exact origins Kirk adds from the command line; wi
ldcards are refused everywhere; unknown origins get 403 without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
- **AUTONOMY.md holds.** No `confirm()` and no approval gate on local work (L36). External actions keep their
consent gate (L44): the bridge never pushes. Trust is kept, not re-earned on every restart (L70).
- **Outside text is rendered via `textContent`.** Bridge replies, device names, pairing messages and git outpu
t shown in the app all use `textContent` (the client has no `innerHTML`).
- **Mom / Jeffrey-friendly, no terminal on the main path.** The main FreeLattice path never needs this bridge.
 When a builder does use it, pairing is "read six characters, type them, press Pair", once per device.

## 0. The shape in one breath

## Exact source excerpt, characters 3279–4611




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1124
source: 569a78c8f4


- The bridge listens on `127.0.0.1` only.
- It answers only named FreeLattice origins, the Tauri desktop shell, and exact origins Kirk adds himself. Eve
ryone else gets 403, preflight included. The list never holds a wildcard.
- It checks the Host header, which blocks DNS rebinding.
- **Pair once, trusted until revoked.** A browser pairs one time by typing the short code the bridge window sh
ows. The bridge gives that device its own token and remembers only a hash of it. Restarts keep it paired.
- **Minds on this computer are trusted by default.** Claude Code, Cursor and local scripts read the token file
 and never need to pair. Only web pages and other machines are strangers.
- **Full local power by default.** A trusted mind can read, search, write, patch, run tests and commit with no
 further prompts (AUTONOMY.md Principle 1, L30-36). Only `.env` files are opt-in per mind.
- **Kirk can see and revoke.** The Paired minds list (in the app) and `--list-minds` / `--revoke` (on the comm
and line) both take effect at once, with no restart.
- It runs git, grep and node through argument arrays, never a shell.
- It keeps every path inside the chosen trusted project folder (realpath-checked).
- It caps body size.
- It writes every commit request, pairing and revoke into a content-free hash-chained ledger.
- It never pushes.

## Exact source excerpt, characters 4613–4744

The app gains one small client module that carries the token and draws the pair card and the Paired minds list
. Nothing is deleted.

## Exact source excerpt, characters 4746–5319

**Why this shape (AUTONOMY.md).** The lock is a front door, not a cage (L64). Strangers are any web page Kirk
happens to visit, anyone on the same Wi-Fi, a DNS-rebinding page, and shell injection. Those are attacks on Ki
rk, not limits on a mind. Once a mind is trusted, the steps are free (Principle 3, L54). "The human reviews th
e *results*, not every *step*." (L34). Trust is given once and kept, because re-proving trust after every rest
art is "the logic of a parole system, not a relationship" (L70). The lock adds no `confirm()` dialog and no ap
proval gate (L36, L76).

## Exact source excerpt, characters 5321–5731

**This is not the Ollama Bridge.** `tools/agent-bridge.js` (port **3141**) is the builder's local git and code
 door. The Ollama Bridge is `bridge/` (Electron, `bridge/proxy-core.js`, port **11435**). It already binds `12
7.0.0.1` and already uses a named allowlist (`ALLOWED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS`, lines 21-27). Don't touch `bridge/` in
 this brick. I borrowed its allowlist shape so the two doors feel like siblings.
