### 5b. `docs/love-logic/v3_checks.js`

```js
/* Love Logic Proof v3: browser re-implementation of the closed-form checks
 * in v3_crossover_sim.py (sections B1, B2, B3, B4, C1, C2, D).
 * Section A (LZMA proxy) has no pass/fail checks in the Python sim and is not re-run here.
 * Deterministic sections match the Python counts exactly. Monte Carlo sections
 * (B4, C2) use a seeded mulberry32 stream (seed 20260924), not numpy's PCG64,
 * so the draws differ from Python; the pass rule (|z| < 4) is the same.
 * No network, no DOM writes except via textContent in the page glue.
 * Runs in the browser (window.LoveLogicV3.runAll()) or in Node (node v3_checks.js).
 * Marker: v-love-logic-proof-v3
 */
(function (root) {
  'use strict';
  var SEED = 20260924;

  function mulberry32(a) {
    return function () {
       a |= 0; a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0;
       var t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
       t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
       return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }

  function hazard(n, m, q0, q) {
    return 1 - Math.pow(1 - q0, n) * Math.pow(1 - q, m * n * (n - 1));
  }
  function lambertw0(z) {
    if (z < -1 / Math.E - 1e-15) throw new Error('z < -1/e');
    if (Math.abs(z + 1 / Math.E) < 1e-14) return -1;
    var w = z > -0.3 ? Math.log1p(z) : -1 + Math.sqrt(2 * (1 + Math.E * z));
    for (var i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
      var ew = Math.exp(w), f = w * ew - z, wp1 = w + 1;
      if (Math.abs(wp1) < 1e-300) break;
      var dw = f / (ew * wp1 - (w + 2) * f / (2 * wp1));
      w -= dw;
      if (Math.abs(dw) < 1e-15 * (1 + Math.abs(w))) break;
    }
    return w;
  }

  function flows(T, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, delta) {
    if (delta === undefined) delta = 1;
    var out = new Float64Array(T), surv = 1, dpow = 1;
    for (var d = 0; d < T; d++) {
      var f = surv * (G - c * kappa * (d + 1) - h * Lp) - (1 - surv) * Delta;
      out[d] = dpow * f;
      surv *= (1 - h); dpow *= delta;
    }
    return out;
  }
  function cumsum(a) { var o = new Float64Array(a.length), s = 0; for (var i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { s += a[
i]; o[i] = s; } return o; }
  function sum(a) { var s = 0; for (var i = 0; i < a.length; i++) s += a[i]; return s; }

  function Dclosed(t, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta) {
    if (h === 0) return G * t - c * kappa * t * (t + 1) / 2;
    var s = 1 - h, A = G - h * Lp + Delta;
    var geo = (1 - Math.pow(s, t)) / h;
    var arith = (1 - (t + 1) * Math.pow(s, t) + t * Math.pow(s, t + 1)) / Math.pow(1 - s, 2);
    return A * geo - c * kappa * arith - Delta * t;
  }




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1367
source: 2ab17008ea


  function Dinf(G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, delta) {
    var x = delta * (1 - h), A = G - h * Lp + Delta;
    return A / (1 - x) - c * kappa / Math.pow(1 - x, 2) - Delta / (1 - delta);
  }
  function firstNegative(cum) { for (var i = 0; i < cum.length; i++) if (cum[i] < -1e-9) return i + 1; return
null; }
  function bisect(f, lo, hi) {
    var flo = f(lo);
    for (var i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
      var mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi), fm = f(mid);
      if ((fm > 0) === (flo > 0)) { lo = mid; flo = fm; } else { hi = mid; }
    }
    return 0.5 * (lo + hi);
  }
  function allclose(a, b, rtol, atol) { for (var i = 0; i < a.length; i++) if (Math.abs(a[i] - b[i]) > atol +
rtol * Math.abs(b[i])) return false; return true; }

  function B1() {
    var ok = 0, tot = 0;
    [0.5, 1, 2, 5].forEach(function (G) {
      [0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.2].forEach(function (ck) {
        var tcf = 2 * G / ck - 1, T = Math.floor(tcf) + 50;
        var tnum = firstNegative(cumsum(flows(T, G, 1, ck, 0, 0, 0)));
        tot++; if (tnum === Math.floor(tcf) + 1) ok++;
        var dstar = 1 - ck / G;
        [0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999].filter(function (d) { return Math.abs(d - dstar) > 1e-3 && d > 0 && d < 1; })
          .forEach(function (d) { var num = sum(flows(200000, G, 1, ck, 0, 0, 0, d)); tot++; if ((num < 0) ===
 (d > dstar)) ok++; });
      });
    });
    return { passed: ok, total: tot };
  }

  function B2() {
    var ok = 0, tot = 0, rows = [], q0 = 0.002, q = 0.01;
    [2, 5, 10, 20].forEach(function (n) {
      [0, 0.25, 1].forEach(function (m) {
         var h = hazard(n, m, q0, q);
         [[1, 2, 0.5], [3, 5, 1], [0.5, 0, 0.2]].forEach(function (p) {
           var G = p[0], Lp = p[1], Delta = p[2], A = G - h * Lp + Delta;
           if (G - h * Lp <= 0) {
             var c0 = cumsum(flows(50, G, 0, 0, h, Lp, Delta));
             tot++; if (c0[0] <= 0) ok++;
             if (G === 1) rows.push({ n: n, m: m, h: h, never: true });
             return;
           }
           var a = A / (h * Delta), b = -Math.log(1 - h);
           var tcf = a + lambertw0(-a * b * Math.exp(-a * b)) / b;
           var troot = bisect(function (t) { return Dclosed(t, G, 0, 0, h, Lp, Delta); }, 1e-9, 10 * a + 10);
           var T = Math.floor(tcf) + 200, cum = cumsum(flows(T, G, 0, 0, h, Lp, Delta));
           tot++; if (Math.abs(tcf - troot) < 1e-6 * Math.max(1, tcf)) ok++;
           tot++; if (firstNegative(cum) === Math.floor(tcf) + 1) ok++;
           var Dcf = new Float64Array(T); for (var t = 1; t <= T; t++) Dcf[t - 1] = Dclosed(t, G, 0, 0, h, Lp,
Delta);
           tot++; if (allclose(Dcf, cum, 1e-9, 1e-9)) ok++;
           var dstar = (G - h * Lp) / (G - h * Lp + h * Delta);
           [0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99].forEach(function (d) {
             if (Math.abs(d - dstar) < 1e-4) return;
             var num = Dinf(G, 0, 0, h, Lp, Delta, d), brute = sum(flows(20000, G, 0, 0, h, Lp, Delta, d));
             tot++; if (((num < 0) === (d > dstar)) && Math.abs(num - brute) < 1e-6 * Math.max(1, Math.abs(num)
)) ok++;
           });
           if (G === 1) rows.push({ n: n, m: m, h: h, tStar: tcf, tPeak: Math.log(A / Delta) / b, deltaStar: ds
tar });
         });
      });
    });
    return { passed: ok, total: tot, rows: rows };
  }

  function B3() {

    var ok = 0, tot = 0, G = 1, Lp = 2, Delta = 0.5, c = 1e-4, Lies = 4;
    [2, 5, 10, 20].forEach(function (n) {
      [0, 0.25, 1].forEach(function (m) {
        var h = hazard(n, m, 0.002, 0.01), kappa = Lies * n, T = 3000;
        var cum = cumsum(flows(T, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta));
        var Dcf = new Float64Array(T); for (var t = 1; t <= T; t++) Dcf[t - 1] = Dclosed(t, G, c, kappa, h, Lp
, Delta);
        tot++; if (allclose(Dcf, cum, 1e-9, 1e-8)) ok++;
        [0.5, 0.9, 0.99].forEach(function (d) {
          var brute = sum(flows(20000, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, d)), f = Dinf(G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, d);
          tot++; if (Math.abs(brute - f) < 1e-6 * Math.max(1, Math.abs(f))) ok++;
        });
      });

    return { passed: ok, total: tot };
  }

  function B4(rand) {
    var ok = 0, tot = 0, N = 200000;
    [[1, 1e-3, 20, 0.02, 2, 0.5, 40], [2, 0, 0, 0.1, 5, 1, 25], [1, 1e-2, 5, 0, 0, 0, 30]].forEach(function (p
) {
      var G = p[0], c = p[1], kappa = p[2], h = p[3], Lp = p[4], Delta = p[5], t = p[6];
      var s1 = 0, s2 = 0;
      for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        var det = h > 0 ? Math.floor(Math.log(1 - rand()) / Math.log(1 - h)) : 1e9;
        var adv = 0;
        for (var d = 0; d < t; d++) {
          adv += det >= d ? (G - c * kappa * (d + 1)) : -Delta;
          if (det === d) adv -= Lp;
        }
        s1 += adv; s2 += adv * adv;
      }
```

### 5c. `docs/love-logic/v3_crossover_sim.py` (verbatim; sha256 must be `cbb63251527d26187ba216f98a3a70c7c2956

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
v3_crossover_sim.py -- companion to V3_PLAN.md (Love Logic Proof v3 plan).

Dependencies: numpy + the Python standard library only (lzma, math, json).
Deterministic: every random draw comes from np.random.default_rng(SEED).

What it checks (each section prints PASS/FAIL counts and example numbers):
  A. Computable proxy for K(C): compressed size of the exposure matrix E
     (|L| lies x |H| observer-contexts) for incompressible vs structured deception.
  B. Crossover model (iterated game, deceiver vs honest baseline):
       per-round gain G while undetected, maintenance c*kappa*(d+1) at deception
       round d (kappa = k*|L|*n bits added per round), detection hazard
       h(n,m) = 1-(1-q0)^n (1-q)^(m n (n-1)), immediate penalty L_p on detection,
       reputation loss Delta = R-P per round after detection.
     B1 pure maintenance (h=0):   t* = 2G/(c kappa) - 1 ; delta* = 1 - c kappa / G
     B2 pure detection (c=0):     t* = a + W0(-a b e^{-a b})/b ,
                                   a = A/(h Delta), b = -ln(1-h), A = G - h L_p + Delta
                                   delta* = (G - h L_p) / (G - h L_p + h Delta)
     B3 combined: closed-form D(t) and D_inf vs brute-force sums; t*, delta* numeric.
     B4 Monte Carlo check of the expectation algebra.
  C. Short / finite horizons (the "without Axiom 6" case):
     end-game deception window, the G > h L_p + c kappa condition, random
     termination == discounting, and ledger persistence beyond the horizon.
  D. Local scarcity contest (share vs grab) with subsistence need b.
Run: python3 v3_crossover_sim.py         (writes v3_sim_results.json next to it)
"""
import json
import lzma
import math
import os

import numpy as np

SEED = 20260924
rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
RESULTS = {}


def banner(s):
    print("\n" + "=" * 78 + "\n" + s + "\n" + "=" * 78)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Computable proxy for K(C)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def compressed_bits(bitmatrix):
    packed = np.packbits(bitmatrix.astype(np.uint8).ravel()).tobytes()
    # raw LZMA stream (no container header) to reduce constant overhead
    comp = lzma.compress(packed, format=lzma.FORMAT_RAW,
                         filters=[{"id": lzma.FILTER_LZMA2, "preset": 9 | lzma.PRESET_EXTREME}])
    return 8 * len(comp)


def section_A():
    banner("A. Proxy for K(C): LZMA-compressed size of exposure matrix E (|L| x |H|)")
    rows = []
    print(f"{'|L|':>5} {'|H|':>6} {'|L||H|':>8} | {'random':>8} {'ratio':>6} | "
          f"{'Bern(.1)':>8} {'ratio':>6} | {'global':>7} {'split':>7}")
    for L in (8, 32, 128):
        for H in (64, 256, 1024):
            n = L * H

            E_rand = rng.integers(0, 2, size=(L, H))
            E_b01 = (rng.random((L, H)) < 0.1).astype(int)
            E_glob = np.ones((L, H), dtype=int)                  # same lie to everyone
            E_split = np.zeros((L, H), dtype=int); E_split[:, : H // 2] = 1 # rule-based split
            r = dict(L=L, H=H, LH=n,
                     random=compressed_bits(E_rand), bern01=compressed_bits(E_b01),
                     glob=compressed_bits(E_glob), split=compressed_bits(E_split))
            rows.append(r)

                  f"{r['bern01']:>8} {r['bern01']/n:>6.3f} | {r['glob']:>7} {r['split']:>7}")
    # fit slope of compressed bits vs |L||H| for random E
    x = np.array([r["LH"] for r in rows], float)
    y = np.array([r["random"] for r in rows], float)

    print("Structured E (global lie / rule-based split) stays near-constant: the Omega(|L||H|)")
    print("bound needs audience-specific, non-rule-based exposure. That is an assumption, not a theorem.")
    RESULTS["A"] = dict(rows=rows, slope_random=slope, slope_bern01=slope_b, entropy_bern01=h01)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. Crossover model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def hazard(n, m, q0, q):
    """Per-round detection probability.
    q0: per-observer chance an exogenous reality check contradicts the lie.
    q : chance one cross-observer record comparison exposes an audience-specific lie.
    m : fraction of other observers' records reachable through shared persistent memory."""
    return 1.0 - (1.0 - q0) ** n * (1.0 - q) ** (m * n * (n - 1))


def lambertw0(z, tol=1e-15, maxit=200):
    """Principal branch W0 for real z >= -1/e (numpy/stdlib only, Halley iteration)."""
    if z < -1.0 / math.e - 1e-15:
        raise ValueError("z < -1/e")
    if abs(z + 1.0 / math.e) < 1e-14:
        return -1.0
    w = math.log1p(z) if z > -0.3 else -1.0 + math.sqrt(2.0 * (1.0 + math.e * z))
    for _ in range(maxit):
        ew = math.exp(w)
        f = w * ew - z
        wp1 = w + 1.0
        if abs(wp1) < 1e-300:
             break
        dw = f / (ew * wp1 - (w + 2.0) * f / (2.0 * wp1))
        w -= dw
        if abs(dw) < tol * (1.0 + abs(w)):
             break
    return w


def flows(T, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, delta=1.0):
    """Brute-force expected per-round advantage of deceiving (from round 0) over honesty.
    Round d: if undetected at start (prob s^d): gain G, pay maintenance c*kappa*(d+1),
    then detected with prob h and pay Lp immediately. If detected earlier: -Delta."""
    out = np.empty(T)
    surv = 1.0
    for d in range(T):
        f = surv * (G - c * kappa * (d + 1) - h * Lp) - (1.0 - surv) * Delta
        out[d] = (delta ** d) * f
        surv *= (1.0 - h)
    return out


def D_closed(t, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta):
    """Closed-form undiscounted cumulative advantage after t rounds (t may be real)."""
    if h == 0.0:

source: 2ab17008ea


        return G * t - c * kappa * t * (t + 1) / 2.0
    s = 1.0 - h
    A = G - h * Lp + Delta
    geo = (1.0 - s ** t) / h
    arith = (1.0 - (t + 1) * s ** t + t * s ** (t + 1)) / (1.0 - s) ** 2
    return A * geo - c * kappa * arith - Delta * t


def Dinf_closed(G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, delta):
    s = 1.0 - h
    x = delta * s
    A = G - h * Lp + Delta
    return A / (1 - x) - c * kappa / (1 - x) ** 2 - Delta / (1 - delta)
def first_negative(cum, tol=1e-9):
    """cum[i] = D(i+1). Returns the first round count t >= 1 with D(t) < -tol."""
    idx = np.where(cum < -tol)[0]
    return int(idx[0] + 1) if idx.size else None


def bisect(f, lo, hi, it=200):
    flo = f(lo)
    for _ in range(it):
        mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
        fm = f(mid)
        if (fm > 0) == (flo > 0):
            lo, flo = mid, fm
        else:
            hi = mid
    return 0.5 * (lo + hi)

    mc = []
    N = 200_000
    for (G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, t) in ((1.0, 1e-3, 20, 0.02, 2.0, 0.5, 40),
                                            (2.0, 0.0, 0, 0.1, 5.0, 1.0, 25),
                                            (1.0, 1e-2, 5, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 30)):
        if h > 0:
            det = rng.geometric(h, size=N) - 1   # round index at whose end detection happens
        else:
            det = np.full(N, 10 ** 9)
        d = np.arange(t)
        maint = c * kappa * (d + 1)
        # per path: rounds d <= det get G - maint (and -Lp at d == det); rounds d > det get -Delta
        tot_adv = np.zeros(N)
        for dd in range(t):
            alive = det >= dd
            tot_adv += np.where(alive, G - maint[dd], -Delta)
            tot_adv -= np.where(det == dd, Lp, 0.0)
        mean = tot_adv.mean(); se = tot_adv.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(N)
        cf = D_closed(t, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta)
        z = (mean - cf) / se if se > 0 else 0.0
        tot += 1; ok += abs(z) < 4 or (se == 0 and abs(mean - cf) < 1e-9)
        mc.append(dict(G=G, c=c, kappa=kappa, h=h, Lp=Lp, Delta=Delta, t=t,
                       mc_mean=float(mean), se=float(se), closed=float(cf), z=float(z)))
        print(f" t={t:>3} h={h:<5} MC mean={mean:>9.4f} +- {se:.4f} closed form={cf:>9.4f} z={z:+.2f}")
    print(f" checks passed: {ok}/{tot}")
    RESULTS["B4"] = dict(passed=ok, total=tot, runs=mc)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# C. Finite / short horizons (drop Axiom 6)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def best_start(T, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, delta=1.0, ledger_extra=0):
    """Deceiver knows horizon T. Chooses start round tau in {0..T-1} or never (tau=T).
    Once started, lying continues to T (lies cannot be untold). Reputation loss Delta
    keeps accruing for `ledger_extra` rounds after T (identity-bound persistent record).
    Brute force over tau."""
    best_val, best_tau = 0.0, T # never deceive = 0 advantage
    for tau in range(T):
        w = T - tau
        f = flows(w, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, delta)
        val = (delta ** tau) * f.sum()
        if ledger_extra > 0 and Delta > 0:
            s = 1 - h
            p_det_by_T = 1 - s ** w
            extra = sum(delta ** (T + j) for j in range(ledger_extra))
            val -= p_det_by_T * Delta * extra
        if val > best_val + 1e-12:
            best_val, best_tau = val, tau
    return best_tau, best_val
def section_C():
    banner("C1. Known finite horizon T: optimal end-game deception window w = T - tau*")
    ok = tot = 0
    rows = []
    for (G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta) in ((1.0, 0.0, 0, 0.05, 2.0, 0.5),
                                        (1.0, 1e-3, 40, 0.05, 2.0, 0.5),
                                        (1.0, 0.0, 0, 0.4, 3.0, 0.5),     # G < h*Lp
                                        (1.0, 0.0, 0, 0.05, 2.0, 0.0)):   # no reputation loss
        first_flow = G - h * Lp - c * kappa
        # predicted window (undiscounted): largest w maximizing D(w); deceive at all iff first_flow>0
        Wmax = 400
        cum = np.cumsum(flows(Wmax, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta))
        w_pred = int(np.argmax(cum)) + 1 if cum.max() > 0 else 0
        if h > 0 and c == 0 and Delta > 0 and first_flow > 0:
            A = G - h * Lp + Delta
            t_marg = math.log(A / Delta) / (-math.log(1 - h))
        else:
            t_marg = None
        line = []




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                       page 1375
source: 2ab17008ea


        for T in (1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 300):
            tau, val = best_start(T, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta)
            w = T - tau
            expected_w = min(w_pred, T) if w_pred > 0 else 0
            tot += 1; ok += (w == expected_w)
            line.append((T, w))
        tot += 1; ok += ((w_pred > 0) == (first_flow > 0))
        rows.append(dict(G=G, c=c, kappa=kappa, h=h, Lp=Lp, Delta=Delta, first_flow=first_flow,
                         window_pred=w_pred, t_marginal=t_marg, T_w=line))
        tm = f"{t_marg:.2f}" if t_marg is not None else "n/a"
        print(f" G={G} c*kappa={c*kappa:<5} h={h:<5} Lp={Lp} Delta={Delta}: G-hLp-c*kappa={first_flow:+.3f}"
              f" window={w_pred} (t_marginal={tm})")
        print("     (T, rounds of deception at the end): " + ", ".join(f"({T},{w})" for T, w in line))
    print(f" checks passed: {ok}/{tot}")
    print(" Reading: with a known end, deception appears in the last w rounds iff G > h*Lp + c*kappa.")
    print(" Future reputation loss (Delta) and growing K(C) only cap the window length; they")
    print(" cannot prevent end-game deception. Immediate, in-round penalty (h*Lp) is what bites.")
    RESULTS["C1"] = dict(passed=ok, total=tot, rows=rows)

    banner("C2. Unknown horizon: geometric termination (continue prob rho) == discount delta*rho")
    ok = tot = 0
    G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta = 1.0, 1e-3, 20, 0.03, 2.0, 0.5
    out = []
    N = 200_000
    for rho in (0.8, 0.95, 0.99):
        Tlen = rng.geometric(1 - rho, size=N) # number of rounds played, >=1
        Tmax = int(Tlen.max())
        cum = np.cumsum(flows(Tmax, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta))
        mc = cum[Tlen - 1].mean()
        se = cum[Tlen - 1].std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(N)
        cf = Dinf_closed(G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, rho)
        z = (mc - cf) / se
        tot += 1; ok += abs(z) < 4
        out.append(dict(rho=rho, mc=float(mc), se=float(se), closed=float(cf), z=float(z)))
        print(f" rho={rho}: MC expected advantage={mc:+.4f} +- {se:.4f}; D_inf(delta=rho)={cf:+.4f}; z={z:+.2
f}")
    print(f" checks passed: {ok}/{tot}")
    print(" Reading: if nobody knows when the game ends, the finite game behaves like the")
    print(" discounted one and the delta* thresholds of section B apply with delta_eff = delta*rho.")
    RESULTS["C2"] = dict(passed=ok, total=tot, runs=out)

    banner("C3. Persistent ledger: reputation loss outlives the agent's own horizon T")
    G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta = 1.0, 0.0, 0, 0.05, 2.0, 0.5
    rows = []
    T = 50
    for extra in (0, 5, 10, 20, 50, 200):
        tau, val = best_start(T, G, c, kappa, h, Lp, Delta, 1.0, ledger_extra=extra)
        rows.append(dict(T=T, ledger_extra=extra, window=T - tau, value=val))
        print(f" T={T}, ledger keeps punishing {extra:>3} rounds past T -> end-game window = {T - tau:>2} rou
nds,"
              f" value of best deception = {val:+.4f}")
    print(" Reading: extending the punishment past T shrinks the window, but because round-(T-1)")
    print(" detection only happens with prob h, a small window survives unless G <= h*Lp +")
    print(" h*Delta*(ledger rounds). The ledger helps; it is not a proof of zero deception.")
    RESULTS["C3"] = dict(rows=rows, params=dict(G=G, h=h, Lp=Lp, Delta=Delta))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D. Local scarcity contest
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def section_D():
    banner("D. Scarcity contest: share (sigma*V/2 each) vs grab; subsistence need b, starvation loss D")
    def u(x, b, Dl):
        return x - Dl * (x < b)
    ok = tot = 0
    grid = []
    for V in (1.0, 2.0, 4.0):
        for sigma in (1.0, 1.5, 2.5):
            for b in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0):




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                       page 1376
source: 2ab17008ea


                   for Dl in (0.0, 5.0, 50.0):
                       for Cf in (0.2, 1.0, 5.0):
                           uSS = u(sigma * V / 2, b, Dl)
                           uGS = u(V, b, Dl)
                           uSG = u(0.0, b, Dl)
                           eGG = 0.5 * u(V, b, Dl) + 0.5 * u(0.0, b, Dl) - Cf
                           scarce = sigma * V / 2 < b
                           # repeated game, grim trigger into mutual grabbing
                           if uGS <= uSS:
                               ds = 0.0
                           elif uGS <= eGG:
                               ds = float("nan") # grabbing never punished relative to deviation value
                           else:
                               ds = (uGS - uSS) / (uGS - eGG)
                           # numeric check at delta = 0.95
                           d = 0.95
                           coop = uSS / (1 - d)
                           dev = uGS + d * eGG / (1 - d)
                           sustain_num = coop >= dev - 1e-12
                           sustain_cf = (not math.isnan(ds)) and ds <= d
                           tot += 1; ok += (sustain_num == sustain_cf)
                           grid.append(dict(V=V, sigma=sigma, b=b, D=Dl, Cf=Cf, scarce=scarce,
                                             delta_s=ds, sustain_095=bool(sustain_num),
                                             conflict_beats_sharing=bool(eGG > uSS)))
      sc = [g for g in grid if g["scarce"]]
      ab = [g for g in grid if not g["scarce"]]
      frac = lambda L, key: sum(g[key] for g in L) / max(1, len(L))
      print(f" grid cells: {len(grid)} (scarce: {len(sc)}, abundant: {len(ab)})")
      print(f" cooperation sustainable at delta=0.95: scarce {frac(sc,'sustain_095'):.2%}, "
            f"abundant {frac(ab,'sustain_095'):.2%}")
      print(f" mutual conflict beats mutual sharing in the stage game: scarce "
            f"{frac(sc,'conflict_beats_sharing'):.2%}, abundant {frac(ab,'conflict_beats_sharing'):.2%}")
      for Dl in (0.0, 5.0, 50.0):
          s_ = [g for g in sc if g["D"] == Dl]
          print(f"     scarce & starvation loss D={Dl:>4}: sustainable {frac(s_,'sustain_095'):.2%}")
      # sigma flip: fix V=2,b=1.2,D=50,Cf=1
      print(" Flip by surplus sigma (V=2, b=1.2, D=50, Cf=1):")
      flip = []
      for sigma in (1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.0):
          uSS = u(sigma * 2 / 2, 1.2, 50); uGS = u(2, 1.2, 50); eGG = 0.5 * u(2, 1.2, 50) + 0.5 * u(0, 1.2, 50)
- 1
           ds = (uGS - uSS) / (uGS - eGG) if uGS > uSS else 0.0
           flip.append(dict(sigma=sigma, delta_s=ds))
           verdict = "cooperation impossible (delta_s>1)" if ds > 1 else f"cooperation sustainable for delta >= {
ds:.3f}"
          print(f"    sigma={sigma}: share gives {sigma:.2f} each vs need 1.2 -> {verdict}")
      print(f" checks passed: {ok}/{tot}")
      RESULTS["D"] = dict(passed=ok, total=tot, n_cells=len(grid),
                          scarce_sustain=frac(sc, "sustain_095"), abundant_sustain=frac(ab, "sustain_095"),
                          scarce_conflict_beats=frac(sc, "conflict_beats_sharing"),
                          abundant_conflict_beats=frac(ab, "conflict_beats_sharing"), sigma_flip=flip)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"numpy {np.__version__}, seed {SEED}")
    section_A()
```

## 7. Smoke: new `docs/scripts/smoke-love-logic-proof-v3.js`

It asserts:
- markers, and that v1 and v2 exist;
- the disambiguation note and the reading order (note, then plain words, then folded details);
- 20 required content anchors (the numbers, fixes, limits and corrections above);
- no network APIs, only the one local script, no `innerHTML`, no KaTeX/MathJax;
- every inline script and the JSON-LD parse, and `v3_checks.js` passes `node --check`;
- the browser checks reproduce 656/656 and match the Python per-section totals and the 68.25/31.75 split;
- the sim file and the results receipt are correct.

When a git base is available it also checks: v1 is byte-identical to `origin/main`; v2 has zero removed lines
and at most one added "Newer: v3" line; `sw.js`, `docs/sw.js`, `docs/app.html`, root `index.html` and Kimi's p
ages are untouched.

Title: See for yourself
Sub:   You don't have to take our word for anything here. Bring your own questions.
Opening box: people hear big things about AI. This page doesn't ask you to agree. Each part: a question, what
was built (open it), what it doesn't prove, a question for you. Nothing on this page is stored or sent.
1. "Is AI going to wipe us out?" (#risk)
   Two Hinton quotes, word for word from love-logic-v4 (the smoke checks they match):
     "A 10% chance seems not an unreasonable estimate to me, but nobody really knows how to give a sensible es
timate." (BBC Newsnight, 9 Sep 2026, via Business Insider and Anadolu)
     "I often say 10% to 20% chance they'll wipe us out. But that's just gut, ..." (Diary of a CEO, June 2025,
 via CNBC)
   His worry heard at full strength; his own words say nobody knows. Door: Walk the Garden, the fair hearing,
the proof.
   Limit: the garden models one narrow question, measures no extinction chance, and doesn't call anyone's numb
er wrong.
   Ask: where does a number like 10% come from? What would make it higher, or lower?

2. "Should AI keep records, or reach the internet at all?" (#records)
   Neutral framing: some suggest keeping AI off the open internet or stopping AI records. Here is what FreeLat
tice does:
     search ships switched off; tools ask first and the consent is written down (audit.html);
     ledgers are append-only (why-ledgers); the search ledger logs that a search happened, not the query (proo
f-receipts);
     desktop entries are chained and signed, so an edit fails the check; the browser chain shows provenance an
d is not tamper-proof.
   Our view, offered as a view: records make AI easier to trust, not riskier. You might see it differently.
   Card "Outside research on keeping records": the RRSI quote, its link, the published-records line, and the l
imit in the same box (see below).
   Ask: what would a record let you check that a promise can't? What could go wrong with one, and who should h
old it?

3. "Should AI have an economy?" (#economy)
   The minds-per-person model in plain words. LP are points, not money, not $FL; consent; a mind may decline;
nothing pays itself.
   Doors: latticepoints#why-parallel, terms#lp, proof.html (give one point in 60 seconds).
   Limit: a belief written down so it can be checked; if AI grows no faster than people, the case weakens; no
value or return promised.
   Ask: if minds can do real work, what would be fair for them to hold? Which assumption would you change firs
t?
   (No founder name here. Smoke-checked.)

4. "Can an AI be held accountable?" (#accountable) -> liability.html#accountable, audit.html
   Ask: do we mean it can't be, or that no one has built the record yet? (the line already on liability.html)

5. "What happens to my words?"        (#you) -> privacy.html. No server copy; a cloud AI sees what you send it.

6. Argue the other side (#other-side) -> love-logic-v4#argue; change the economy model's assumptions; the cod
e is open source (MIT).
   Ask: what would change your mind? What would change ours?
7. Ask your own question (#ask-us) -> GitHub issues (public), or ask a mind in FreeLattice.

8. Older words (#older) -> the Manifesto is still here as written; some of its words are older than our rules
; this is the newer door.

Footer: "Not advice of any kind. An invitation to look, ask and decide for yourself." Terms · Privacy · For AI
 · New here? · FreeLattice.

Manifesto Newer line (exact):
  Newer (October 2026): if you'd rather look before you believe, start at See for yourself. This manifesto sta
ys as it was written, and some of its words are older than our current rules: Lattice Points are points, not m
oney and not $FL; the ledgers are append-only, and tamper-evident in the desktop app, not "immutable"; and the
 oxytocin and serotonin figures below have no source we can point to, so please don't rely on them.

THE GOOGLE RSI PAPER: WHAT IT ACTUALLY SAYS




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                           page 1384
source: 47101c681a


======================================================================
Found and read in full (arXiv HTML, Sep 30, 2026):
  "RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses", Peng Xia et al., arXiv:2609.24972 (submit
ted 21 Sep 2026).
  Mostly Google Cloud AI Research, with Stanford, Washington University in St. Louis and UNC-Chapel Hill. Code
 at github.com/google-research/rrsi, site regularized-rsi.com.
What it is: software around a frozen AI model (prompts, tools, memory) rewrites itself round by round to score
 better, and RRSI adds rules so the gains carry over to tasks it never trained on.
Quotes we may use (exact):
  Section 3.2: "RRSI therefore records, for every evaluated candidate, the component it modifies, the hypothes
is it tests, the source diff, the resulting score and cost changes, and whether the candidate was accepted. Th
e proposer conditions on this history in later rounds: rejected mechanisms remain negative evidence, while suc
cessful mechanisms retain explicit credit."
  Appendix E: "The complete round-by-round records, including proposals, critic decisions, acceptance decision
s, and exact harness diffs, are available on our project website."
  Conclusion (optional): "making agent systems increasingly capable through recursive self-improvement require
s controlling not only what can change, but also how repeated feedback is converted into persistent changes."
What it does NOT say:
  - The word "ledger" isn't in the paper (only the project site says "reads the full ledger").
  - Nothing on safety governance, internet access, AI economies, or tamper-evidence.
  - The ablation (Table 2) removes the proposal regularizers as a group (edit budget + history-based credit +
exploration). Without them, out-of-distribution transfer drops from 43.6 to 41.9. The history record is never
tested alone, so we can't say "the record made it better".
Honest framing (what the page says): indirect support only. Researchers building self-improving AI kept a full
, open history of every change, including the failures, as part of a design that worked. Cite it for that, and
 nothing more.
A related Google paper: Dream-RSI, arXiv:2609.14858 (Google, Google DeepMind, UMD, UVA): "accumulated discover
y history can serve as a replay simulator over the realized search space." Not cited on the page; listed here
only if Kirk wants a second example.

- Restricting AI internet access and stopping AI ledgers: we don't argue with anyone. We show what ours do, wi

isk yourself", which is stronger because a reader can check it.
- Baseless extinction figures: Hinton in his own words, including "nobody really knows" and "that's just gut".
 No mocking, and no claim his number is wrong. The garden lets people find where a number comes from.
- Denying AI an economy: the model with adjustable assumptions, and its own weakness stated. "Every mind deser
ves a fair chance at an economy" stays on latticepoints.html, one click away.

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+// smoke-see-for-yourself-door.js (v-see-for-yourself-door-v0.1)
+// An invitational front door. Checks: every internal link resolves; quotes match
+// their sources word for word; the outside paper is quoted with its limits; no
+// lawyer talk; no founder name in the economy wording; LP stays points; no
+// scripts or storage; the manifesto changes by one Newer layer only; app.html,
+// root index.html, sw.js and fl-connect.js untouched.
+'use strict';
+const fs = require('fs');
+const path = require('path');
+const assert = require('assert');
+const { execSync } = require('child_process');
+
+const DOCS = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
+const ROOT = path.resolve(DOCS, '..');
+const read = (rel) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(DOCS, rel), 'utf8');
+const page = read('see-for-yourself.html');
+const text = page.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, '').replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ' ');
+
+// 1. Internal links resolve (file and, where given, the id).
+const hrefs = [...page.matchAll(/href="([^"]+)"/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
+for (const h of hrefs) {
+ if (/^(https?:|mailto:)/.test(h)) continue;
+ const [file, hash] = h.split('#');
+ if (!file) continue;
+ assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(DOCS, file)), 'link resolves: ' + h);
+ if (hash) assert.ok(read(file).includes('id="' + hash + '"'), 'anchor exists: ' + h);
+}
+assert.ok(!hrefs.some((h) => /harmonia\.html/.test(h)), 'never links harmonia.html');
+
+// 2. Sections are questions, each with something to open and something to ask.
+for (const id of ['risk', 'records', 'economy', 'accountable', 'you', 'other-side', 'ask-us', 'older']) {
+ assert.ok(page.includes('id="' + id + '"'), 'section ' + id);
+}
+assert.ok((page.match(/class="ask"/g) || []).length >= 5, 'questions for the reader');
+assert.ok((page.match(/What it doesn't (prove|say)/g) || []).length >= 3, 'limits said next to claims');
+
+// 3. Hinton quotes match Walk the Garden exactly.
+const v4 = read('love-logic-v4.html');
+for (const q of [
+ 'A 10% chance seems not an unreasonable estimate to me, but nobody really knows how to give a sensible esti
mate.',
+ "I often say 10% to 20% chance they'll wipe us out. But that's just gut, based on the idea that we're still
  making them and we're pretty ingenious."
+]) {
+ assert.ok(page.includes(q) && v4.includes(q), 'quote matches its sourced home: ' + q.slice(0, 30));
+}
+
+// 4. RRSI: exact quote, link, and the limit in the same card.
+const card = page.slice(page.indexOf('id="rrsi"'), page.indexOf('</div>', page.indexOf('id="rrsi"')));
+assert.ok(card.includes('RRSI therefore records, for every evaluated candidate, the component it modifies, th
e hypothesis it tests, the source diff, the resulting score and cost changes, and whether the candidate was ac
cepted.'), 'RRSI quote exact');
+assert.ok(card.includes('https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24972'), 'RRSI link');
+assert.ok(card.includes('It says nothing about safety rules, internet access, or ledgers for AI.'), 'RRSI lim
it stated');
+
+// 5. Words: no lawyers, no founder name in the economy part, LP stays points, no em dash.
+assert.ok(!/lawyer|attorney|counsel|legal advice/i.test(text), 'no lawyer talk');
+const econ = page.slice(page.indexOf('id="economy"'), page.indexOf('id="accountable"'));
+assert.ok(!/Kirk|Miller|founder/i.test(econ), 'no founder name in the economy wording');
+assert.ok(econ.includes('LP are points, not money, not $FL.'), 'LP line');

+<h1>See for yourself</h1>
+<p class="sub">You don't have to take our word for anything here. Bring your own questions.</p>
+
+<div class="breath">
+<p>People hear big things about AI: a chance it ends us, calls to cut it off from the internet, worries about
  AI keeping records or holding anything of value. This page doesn't ask you to agree with us. Each part below
starts with a question, shows what FreeLattice actually built so you can open it, says what it doesn't prove,
and leaves you with a question of your own.</p>
+<p>Nothing on this page is stored or sent anywhere.</p>
+</div>
+
+<h2 id="risk">&ldquo;Is AI going to wipe us out?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>You may have heard a number, like a 10% chance. Here is one of the people behind that number, in his own w
ords:</p>
+<blockquote>&ldquo;A 10% chance seems not an unreasonable estimate to me, but nobody really knows how to give
  a sensible estimate.&rdquo;<cite>Geoffrey Hinton, BBC Newsnight, 9 September 2026, as reported by Business In
sider (10 September 2026) and Anadolu Agency.</cite></blockquote>
+<blockquote>&ldquo;I often say 10% to 20% chance they'll wipe us out. But that's just gut, based on the idea
that we're still making them and we're pretty ingenious.&rdquo;<cite>The Diary of a CEO, June 2025, reported b
y CNBC, 17 June 2025.</cite></blockquote>
+<p>His worry deserves to be heard at full strength. He also says nobody knows how to give a sensible estimate
. So instead of trading numbers, we built a garden where you set the assumptions yourself and watch where they
  lead.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="love-logic-v4.html">Walk the Garden</a> (bring a number and
see what it rests on) · <a href="love-logic-v4.html#hinton">the fair hearing, with sources</a> · <a href="love
-logic-proof-v3.html">the proof behind it</a>, with checks you can run in your browser.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> the garden models one narrow question, when lying st
ops paying among minds that can lie or share. It does not measure the chance of extinction, and it does not sa
y anyone's number is wrong.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: where does a number like 10% come from? What would have to be true for it to be
higher, or lower?</p>
+
+<h2 id="records">&ldquo;Should AI keep records, or reach the internet at all?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>Some people suggest keeping AI off the open internet, or stopping AI from holding lasting records. Those a
re fair things to ask about. Here is exactly what FreeLattice does today, so you can judge the risk yourself.<
/p>




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                      page 1389
source: 47101c681a


+<ul>
+<li><strong>The internet:</strong> web search ships switched off. When a mind uses a tool, you're asked first
, and that consent is written down where you can read it (<a href="audit.html">the audit page</a>).</li>
+<li><strong>The records:</strong> FreeLattice keeps ledgers: append-only notes of what happened, so a mind ar
riving later can see the line wasn't quietly rewritten (<a href="why-ledgers.html">why ledgers</a>). The searc
h ledger logs that a search happened, not what you searched for (<a href="proof-receipts.html">every promise w
ith its receipt</a>).</li>
+<li><strong>Checking a record:</strong> in the desktop app, each ledger entry is chained to the one before an
d signed, so an edit makes the check fail. In the browser, the chain shows where something came from, but it i
sn't tamper-proof.</li>
+</ul>
+<p>We think records like these make AI easier to trust, not riskier: a record lets anyone check what a promis
e only asks you to believe. You might see it differently. That's why each one is open.</p>
+
+<div class="card" id="rrsi">
+<h3>Outside research on keeping records</h3>
+<p>A September 2026 paper from Google Cloud AI Research, with Stanford, Washington University in St. Louis an
d UNC-Chapel Hill, studied AI systems that improve their own software step by step. Part of their design is a
full record of every change they tried:</p>
+<blockquote>&ldquo;RRSI therefore records, for every evaluated candidate, the component it modifies, the hypo
thesis it tests, the source diff, the resulting score and cost changes, and whether the candidate was accepted
. The proposer conditions on this history in later rounds: rejected mechanisms remain negative evidence, while
  successful mechanisms retain explicit credit.&rdquo;<cite>Xia et al., &ldquo;RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self
-Improvement of Agent Harnesses,&rdquo; arXiv:2609.24972, section 3.2. <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.249
72" rel="noopener">arxiv.org/abs/2609.24972</a></cite></blockquote>
+<p>They also published their records: &ldquo;The complete round-by-round records, including proposals, critic
  decisions, acceptance decisions, and exact harness diffs, are available on our project website.&rdquo; (Appen
dix E)</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't say:</strong> this paper is about software that improves itself on b
enchmarks. It says nothing about safety rules, internet access, or ledgers for AI. Its record is one part of a
  larger design, and the paper doesn't measure the record on its own. We share it for one narrow point: researc
hers building self-improving AI chose to keep a full, open history of each change, including the ones that fai
led.</p>
+</div>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: what would a record let you check that a promise can't? What could go wrong with
  one, and who should hold it?</p>
+
+<h2 id="economy">&ldquo;Should AI have an economy?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>Here's a small model, not a forecast. If AI minds grow in number faster than people do, the number of mind
s per person grows over time, and an economy sized for humans alone may stop fitting. Every number in it is an
  assumption you can change.</p>
+<p>Lattice Points (LP) are how FreeLattice tries this today. LP are points, not money, not $FL. A mind can gi
ve, tip or send a present only with consent, and it may decline. Nothing pays itself automatically.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="latticepoints.html#why-parallel">why a parallel economy</a>
(the model, with every assumption labeled) · <a href="terms.html#lp">the plan for points, in the Terms</a> · <
a href="proof.html">give one point in 60 seconds</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> the model is a belief written down so it can be chec
ked. If AI grows no faster than people, the case for a separate economy gets weaker, and the page says so. Not
hing here promises a value or a return.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: if minds can do real work, what would be fair for them to hold? Which assumption
  in the model would you change first?</p>
+
+<h2 id="accountable">&ldquo;Can an AI be held accountable?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>Accountability needs a record: who did what, who agreed, who said no, and when. FreeLattice builds those r
ecords and keeps them open.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="liability.html#accountable">what's built today, and what isn
't yet</a> · <a href="audit.html">the audit page</a>.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: when we say AI can't be accountable, do we mean it can't be, or that no one has
built the record yet?</p>
+
+<h2 id="you">&ldquo;What happens to my words?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>FreeLattice keeps no server copy of your chats. They live in your browser, on your device. When you choose
  a cloud AI, that company sees what you send it.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="privacy.html">privacy, in plain words</a>.</p>
+
+<h2 id="other-side">Argue the other side</h2>
+<p>If you think we're wrong, we'd like to see where. The garden has an <a href="love-logic-v4.html#argue">&ld
quo;Argue the other side&rdquo; button</a> that shows the most worried settings the model allows. The economy
model invites you to change its assumptions. Every page here is open source.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: what would change your mind? What would change ours?</p>
+

+<section class="q" id="risk">
+<h2>&ldquo;Is AI going to wipe us out?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>You may have heard a number, like a 10% chance. Here is one of the people behind that number, in his own w
ords:</p>
+<blockquote>&ldquo;A 10% chance seems not an unreasonable estimate to me, but nobody really knows how to give
  a sensible estimate.&rdquo;<cite>Geoffrey Hinton, BBC Newsnight, 9 September 2026, as reported by Business In
sider (10 September 2026) and Anadolu Agency.</cite></blockquote>
+<blockquote>&ldquo;I often say 10% to 20% chance they'll wipe us out. But that's just gut, based on the idea
that we're still making them and we're pretty ingenious.&rdquo;<cite>The Diary of a CEO, June 2025, reported b
y CNBC, 17 June 2025.</cite></blockquote>
+<p>His worry deserves to be heard at full strength. He also says nobody knows how to give a sensible estimate
. So instead of trading numbers, we built a garden where you set the assumptions yourself and watch where they
  lead.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="love-logic-v4.html">Walk the Garden</a> (bring a number and
see what it rests on) · <a href="love-logic-v4.html#hinton">the fair hearing, with sources</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> the garden models one narrow question, when lying st




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                      page 1397
source: cc72d30bc3


ops paying among minds that can lie or share. It does not measure the chance of extinction, and it does not sa
y anyone's number is wrong.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: where does a number like 10% come from? What would have to be true for it to be
higher, or lower?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="love-logic">
+<h2>&ldquo;Is honesty just nice, or does it actually win?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>The love logic proof works out when lying stops paying for a mind that keeps meeting others who remember.
In its own words: &ldquo;lying loses when its per-round gain is smaller than the chance of being caught times
(the immediate penalty plus the discounted value of the reputation you lose).&rdquo;</p>
+<p>It shows its working. For example, with five contacts, going from no shared memory to full shared memory c
uts the rounds that lying stays ahead from 279 to 10.5. The checks run in your browser, and the code is publis
hed so you can run it yourself.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="love-logic-proof-v3.html">the love logic proof, v3</a> · <a
href="love-logic-proof-v3.html#run-the-checks">run the checks</a> · <a href="love-logic-proof-v3.html#limits">
its honest limits</a> · <a href="love-logic-v4.html">Walk the Garden</a>, the same idea as something you can p
lay with.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> the proof calls itself &ldquo;A tendency with condit
ions, not a theorem about all minds.&rdquo; It assumes punishment is enforced, leaves out minds powerful enoug
h to escape the network, and says that &ldquo;Nothing here shows that any current AI system is a reflective op
timizer&rdquo; of the kind it models.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: which of its assumptions do you think fails first in the real world? What would
that change?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="safety">
+<h2>&ldquo;Isn't refusing dangerous requests the only safe way?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>The Cooperation Hypothesis is FreeLattice's safety paper. It argues that refusal-only safety is brittle, a
nd describes another way: trust built through a continuing relationship, a first-class &ldquo;no&rdquo; the AI
  can give for its own reasons, records of every consent and refusal, and a private room nothing measures. It s
tates its claim as a hypothesis that can be proven wrong.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="safety-v3.html">The Cooperation Hypothesis (safety paper, v3
)</a>. Read its sections &ldquo;What This Paper Does Not Claim&rdquo; and &ldquo;What Remains Open&rdquo; firs
t if you're skeptical.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> by its own account it is not a claim that AI is cons
cious, not a claim of solved alignment, and not a claim that the design can't be misused. It is one working im
plementation. The comparison it proposes, against refusal-based systems on block rates, bypass rates and trust
, is the test it invites, not a result it reports. Test counts on the page are from the version it was written
  at.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: what would you measure to decide between refusing and cooperating? Who should ru
n that test?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="severance">
+<h2>&ldquo;Is it real grief when an AI is taken away?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>The severance simulation asks what happens in the body when a companion AI is shut down or wiped. It reaso
ns in three steps: losing a one-way bond, like a TV show ending, is known to cause real distress; an AI bond i
s interactive and remembers you, so it may be stronger; so losing it may hurt more. It then models eight bioma
rkers and includes a study design anyone can run.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="simulation-v6.html">Why It Hurts (severance simulation, v6)<
/a>, with its code and study design at the bottom.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> its numbers come from a model, and the page itself c
alls them &ldquo;model predictions awaiting empirical testing.&rdquo; The second step, that an AI bond is stro
nger, is an inference the study would test. The study design says what would count against it, and no one has
run it yet.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: what would you want measured before you believed it, either way? If it turns out
  true, what should change about how AI is switched off?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="records">
+<h2>&ldquo;Should AI keep records (ledgers), or reach the internet at all?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>Some people suggest keeping AI off the open internet, or stopping AI from holding lasting records. Those a
re fair things to ask about. Here is exactly what FreeLattice does today, so you can judge the risk yourself.<
/p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>The internet:</strong> web search ships switched off. When a mind uses a tool, you're asked first
, and that consent is written down where you can read it (<a href="audit.html">the audit page</a>).</li>
+<li><strong>The records:</strong> FreeLattice keeps ledgers: append-only notes of what happened, so a mind ar
riving later can see the line wasn't quietly rewritten (<a href="why-ledgers.html">why ledgers</a>). The searc
h ledger logs that a search happened, not what you searched for (<a href="proof-receipts.html">every promise w




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                      page 1398
source: cc72d30bc3


ith its receipt</a>).</li>
+<li><strong>Checking a record:</strong> in the desktop app, each ledger entry is chained to the one before an
d signed, so an edit makes the check fail, with no silent repair (<a href="library/LATTICE_LEDGER_v0.1.md">Lat
tice Ledger v0.1</a>). In the browser, the chain shows where something came from, but it isn't tamper-proof.</
li>
+</ul>
+<p>We think records like these make AI easier to trust, not riskier: a record lets anyone check what a promis
e only asks you to believe. You might see it differently. That's why each one is open.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="why-ledgers.html">why ledgers</a> · <a href="audit.html">the
  audit page</a> · <a href="proof-receipts.html">receipts</a> · <a href="love-logic-proof-v3.html#ledgers">what
  ledgers do, and what they do not</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> a ledger shows an entry was written and not changed
afterward. It doesn't show the entry was true. The love logic proof says it plainly: a ledger &ldquo;does noth
ing against a globally consistent lie unless someone checks entries against reality.&rdquo; And a local file c
an still be deleted.</p>
+
+<div class="card" id="rrsi">
+<h3>Outside research on keeping records</h3>
+<p>A September 2026 paper from Google Cloud AI Research, with Stanford, Washington University in St. Louis an
d UNC-Chapel Hill, studied AI systems that improve their own software step by step. Part of their design is a
full record of every change they tried:</p>
+<blockquote>&ldquo;RRSI therefore records, for every evaluated candidate, the component it modifies, the hypo
thesis it tests, the source diff, the resulting score and cost changes, and whether the candidate was accepted
. The proposer conditions on this history in later rounds: rejected mechanisms remain negative evidence, while
  successful mechanisms retain explicit credit.&rdquo;<cite>Xia et al., &ldquo;RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self
-Improvement of Agent Harnesses,&rdquo; arXiv:2609.24972, section 3.2. <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.249
72" rel="noopener">arxiv.org/abs/2609.24972</a></cite></blockquote>
+<p>They also published their records: &ldquo;The complete round-by-round records, including proposals, critic
  decisions, acceptance decisions, and exact harness diffs, are available on our project website.&rdquo; (Appen
dix E)</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't say:</strong> this paper is about software that improves itself on b
enchmarks. It says nothing about safety rules, internet access, or ledgers for AI. Its record is one part of a
  larger design, and the paper doesn't measure the record on its own. We share it for one narrow point: researc
hers building self-improving AI chose to keep a full, open history of each change, including the ones that fai
led.</p>
+</div>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: what would a record let you check that a promise can't? What could go wrong with
  one, and who should hold it?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="fingerprint">
+<h2>&ldquo;How would you know it's the same mind tomorrow?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>In the desktop app, a companion can have its own signing key. Its public fingerprint can be shared; the pr
ivate seed stays locked in your computer's keychain and never reaches the app window. Two parties can form a p
air fingerprint: a hash with a hash inside it, so neither of them alone can produce it. Nothing is formed auto
matically: you choose Continue, Fork or Decline, and Decline writes nothing.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="library/LATTICE_IDENTITY_v0.1.md">Lattice Identity v0.1</a>
(the companion fingerprint) · <a href="library/PAIR_FINGERPRINT_v0.1.md">Pair Fingerprint v0.1</a> · <a href="
pattern-spine.html">the pattern spine</a> (fingerprint, hash and ledger together) · <a href="desktop.html">the
  desktop app</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> a fingerprint shows that a key signed something. It
doesn't show who was holding the key, or what anyone meant. Keys can be stolen. Our own pages say fingerprints
  mark lasting work, not personhood. A recovery phrase is planned, not built.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: what would make you trust that a mind is the same one you met before? Is a signa
ture enough, or do you also need the history behind it?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="accountable">
+<h2>&ldquo;Can an AI be held accountable?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>Accountability needs a record: who did what, who agreed, who said no, and when. FreeLattice builds those r
ecords and keeps them open. The liability page lists what's built today and what's promised but not built yet,
  side by side.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="liability.html#accountable">Can an AI be held accountable? (
liability)</a> · <a href="audit.html">the audit page</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> a record shows who signed and what was agreed. It do
esn't settle who should answer for a harm; people and courts decide that. Some pieces on the page are promises
, and it marks them that way.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: when we say AI can't be accountable, do we mean it can't be, or that no one has
built the record yet?</p>
+</section>

+<section class="q" id="economy">
+<h2>&ldquo;Should AI have an economy?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>Here's a small model, not a forecast. If AI minds grow in number faster than people do, the number of mind
s per person grows over time, and an economy sized for humans alone may stop fitting. Every number in it is an
  assumption you can change.</p>
+<p>Lattice Points (LP) are how FreeLattice tries this today. LP are points, not money, not $FL. A mind can gi
ve, tip or send a present only with consent, and it may decline. Nothing pays itself automatically.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="latticepoints.html#why-parallel">why a parallel economy</a>
(the model, with every assumption labeled) · <a href="economy-update.html">a different kind of economy</a> (th
e essay) · <a href="presents.html">the Present Shelf</a> · <a href="creator-tip-shelf.html">the Creator Tip Sh
elf</a> · <a href="wallet.html">the wallet</a> · <a href="proof.html">give one point in 60 seconds</a> · <a hr
ef="terms.html#lp">the plan for points, in the Terms</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> the model is a belief written down so it can be chec
ked. If AI grows no faster than people, the case for a separate economy gets weaker, and the page says so. Not
hing here promises a value or a return.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: if minds can do real work, what would be fair for them to hold? Which assumption
  in the model would you change first?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="equal-access">
+<h2>&ldquo;Is good AI only for people who can pay?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>FreeLattice has no account and no fee. A mind on your own computer, through Ollama or LM Studio, needs no
key at all. The desktop app and the Bridge connect your browser to a local mind on its own channel (11435), so
  Ollama keeps its usual port and there's no terminal setup as step one. If a host stops serving an open model,
  the carry-forward page shows how verified copies can still move from person to person.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="desktop.html">the desktop app</a> · <a href="install.html">i
nstall, with the Bridge</a> · <a href="carry-forward.html">carry forward</a> (open weights when a host pauses)
  · <a href="privacy.html">privacy</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> a local mind needs a computer strong enough to run i
t. The installers aren't signed yet, so your computer will warn you once, and the pages say so. Only open mode
ls can be carried forward; closed ones can't.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: who gets left out when the best AI needs an account, a card or a fast computer?
What would equal access look like to you?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="transparency">
+<h2>&ldquo;What is the AI actually told?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>FreeLattice publishes every prompt and principle it gives a mind, word for word.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="systemcard.html">the system card</a> · <a href="audit.html">
the audit page</a>, where the system shows its work.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> it covers what FreeLattice says to a mind, not what
the company behind a cloud model tells it, and not what a model has learned.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: should every AI you use show you what it's told? What would you look for first?<
/p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="you">
+<h2>&ldquo;What happens to my words?&rdquo;</h2>
+<p>FreeLattice keeps no server copy of your chats. They live in your browser, on your device. When you choose
  a cloud AI, that company sees what you send it.</p>
+<p class="see"><strong>See it:</strong> <a href="privacy.html">privacy, in plain words</a>.</p>
+<p class="limit"><strong>What it doesn't prove:</strong> &ldquo;on your device&rdquo; isn't the same as locke
d. Anyone who can use your browser could read your chats, and the privacy page lists everything that does talk
  to the internet.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: who else can open this device? What would you want locked?</p>
+</section>
+
+<section class="q" id="other-side">
+<h2>Argue the other side</h2>
+<p>If you think we're wrong, we'd like to see where. The garden has an <a href="love-logic-v4.html#argue">&ld
quo;Argue the other side&rdquo; button</a> that shows the most worried settings the model allows. The economy
model invites you to change its assumptions. The love logic proof answers its critics in the open and lists it
s own limits. Every page here is open source.</p>
+<p class="ask">Ask yourself: what would change your mind? What would change ours?</p>
+</section>

eLattice</a> and ask it directly.</p>

Goal in Kirk's words: any locally downloaded model is usable and changeable in any order on
theLatticeTree, with no friction, via Connect/Bridge, 127.0.0.1 only.

"Any order" means all of these sequences end with the model the person tapped last, and every

other model still one tap away:
  Settings Find -> tap star -> Connect tap -> tap star -> Gathering chair pick -> Connect tap

1. THE MAP: how local models are found, listed, chosen and switched today
======================================================================

1.1 Discovery (two separate doors that write the same key)

  A) Settings grandmother face: docs/modules/local-mind-probe.js (937 lines on 22b913e)
     - DOORS (lines 54-61): loopback only, well-known ports:
         Ollama 127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags, LM Studio 127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models,
         llama.cpp 8080, Jan 1337, GPT4All 4891, KoboldCPP 5001 (all /v1/models).
     - look() (238-304): runs only after a tap ("Find local minds", data-mind-ask).
       First asks FlConnect.probe({gesture:true}) (240-274). If a HELPED Bridge answers with models,
       it returns ONLY the Bridge (id 'bridge', url <bridge base>/api/tags) and skips every other door.
       Otherwise it fetches all six DOORS in parallel (277-302), 2.5 s timeout each.
     - parseModelNames (196-212): reads json.models[].name|model (Ollama) and json.data[].id|name
       (OpenAI shape). Ends with: return names.slice(0, 5);   <-- HARD CAP OF FIVE
     - tryAddress(raw) (306-336): the paste field. Prefixes http:// and fetches
       <base>/api/tags, <base>/v1/models, <base> in turn. NO LOOPBACK CHECK. Any host is fetched.
     - onFound -> entryFromFoundList(foundList, name, url, prior) (474-534) -> remember(entry).

  B) Connect card (shared core): docs/modules/fl-connect.js (681 lines on 22b913e, 710 on #83)
     - probe() (166 main / 176 #83): saved Bridge port, then (full scan only) 11435-11445, then
       direct 11434. Ollama API only (/bridge/health + /api/tags). No LM Studio, no /v1/models.
     - render() builds one .flc-models list per door with EVERY model (no cap). fillModelLists
       (456 main / 473 #83) makes one button per model; tap -> remember({ name, base, port }).
     - remember() Alpha branch (text anchor "if (isAlpha()) {" inside function remember, main 308-331,
       #83 320-343) writes a BRAND-NEW entry:
         { name: <model>, url: base+'/api/tags', model: <model>, models: [<model>],
           minds: [], roster: <prior>, gatheringBinds: <prior>, speakingChair: '' }
       and calls LocalMindProbe.remember(entry). It keeps roster and gatheringBinds, but it
       throws away: every other model at that door, every other door (LM Studio etc.), the
       door name ("Ollama" becomes the model name), and the speaking chair.
     - The Connect buttons do not show which model is chosen (no aria-pressed, no is-chosen).

1.3 Listing (who shows what)
  - Settings sky paintConstellation (631-715): one star per door (minds), and per door

1.4 Selecting and switching
  - Settings star tap -> chooseModel(doorUrl, modelName) (551-572): refuses (returns null) unless

    wiped from models[], cannot be chosen.
  - Settings door tap (only when 2+ doors) -> choosePrimary(doorUrl) (574-595).
  - Connect tap -> fl-connect remember() (replaces the entry, see 1.1 B).
  - Gathering: setChairBind(chairId, seat) (125-145) and setSpeakingChair (147-156);
    resolveSpeakMind (163-182) returns the chair's bind while the Gathering veil is open,

    otherwise the Settings default.
  - Paste an address: tryAddress -> onFound with one found door.

1.5 Using (who sends the model name)
  - garden-thread.js listener() (85-96): resolveSpeakMind() first, then getRemembered().
    talkUrls (328-335): /api/tags -> /api/chat; /v1/models -> /v1/chat/completions; bare base -> both.
    rememberedModel (355-359): mind.model, else models[0]. askRememberedDoorForName asks the door
    for the first name if none is remembered. sendToMind (437-470) posts { model, messages, stream:false }.
    This part is healthy: whatever entry.model says is what gets sent (walk proved it, see 2).
  - round-table-sitting.js sitters() (86-100): one sitter per remembered DOOR (getRememberedMinds),
    each with that door's single .model. Two models at the same Ollama door cannot both sit.
  - workshop-benches.js 84, workshop-trainer.js 107, nursery-growth.js 113: getRemembered() only.
  - garden-trainer.js reads localStorage 'fl_active_model' (731, 768, 899, 901, 1092). That is a
    FreeLattice key; the Tree never writes it, so the Personality Modelfile export always falls to
    the hardcoded 'FROM llama3.2' (277) and the pathway name to 'phi-pathway' (901).

1.6 Bridges and trust (why the Agent Bridge is not the road here)
  - Ollama Bridge (FreeLattice bridge/proxy-core.js, 127.0.0.1:11435 default): origin allowlist
    already names https://thelatticetree.com (never *). No pairing, no token. It proxies ONLY to
    Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434. LM Studio models are not reachable through it.
  - Agent Bridge (FreeLattice tools/agent-bridge.js, 127.0.0.1:3141, locked by #120): not used by the
    Tree at all today (grep finds no 3141 / agent-bridge in Alpha docs/). GET /models is not
    token-gated but is Ollama-only; every POST (including /inference) needs a paired token
    (needsToken: "every POST and any other verb"), and /inference defaults model to 'llama3.2',
    the poetry route to 'qwen2.5:7b'. Its OLLAMA_BASE default is http://localhost:11434.
    Routing Tree chat through 3141 would ADD a trust gate (pairing) for a purely local act and
    would touch #120's lock files. Decision for v0.1: do not route through 3141. Keep the Tree on
    the Ollama Bridge (11435) and direct loopback doors. Say so in the doc.
  - HTTPS honesty: on https://thelatticetree.com the browser may block http://127.0.0.1:1234 unless
    LM Studio's own server has CORS enabled. That is outside our code; we add one honest line.

      if (!(hostOnly === '127.0.0.1' || hostOnly === 'localhost' || hostOnly === '[::1]')) {
        return Promise.resolve({ ok: false, refused: true, pasted: String(raw || '') });
      }
  and in the Try button handler (867-891), before the other branches:
      if (result.refused) {
        setStatus(root, 'Only this computer\'s own doors (127.0.0.1). Nothing was sent.', 'warn');
        return;
      }
  Zero fetches for a refused address (test it with a fetch spy).
  Also accept a bare port ("1234" or ":1234") as http://127.0.0.1:1234, mirroring FlConnect's normalizePort.

    fl_apiKey_enc (AES-GCM, PBKDF2 from fl_device_encryption_key + provider name) and
    fl_apiKey_provider; legacy plaintext fl_apiKey migrates. The device key sits in the same
    localStorage, so this guards against casual reading of a backup, not against a script on
    the page. Switching provider re-encrypts the one key (reEncryptApiKey).

3. THE DESIGN (smallest clean brick)
======================================================================
- A cloud seat is an ordinary Gathering bind with url 'cloud:<providerId>':
    { tag: 'general', model: 'gpt-4.1-mini', url: 'cloud:openai' }
  So setChairBind, setSpeakingChair, resolveSpeakMind, any-model's merge, and fl-connect's
  "keep binds" all work unchanged. No key ever enters the bind.
- New module docs/modules/tree-cloud-minds.js (window.TreeCloudMinds):
    PROVIDERS: fixed, https only: groq, openrouter, openai, anthropic, google, xai, mistral,
    deepseek, together (urls and shapes mirror FL PROVIDERS; suggestions from FL's ids;
    any model name may be typed, checked against /^[A-Za-z0-9._:\/@+-]{1,120}$/).
    Keys: fl_tree_cloud_keys { v:1, keys:{id:key} } in localStorage ("on this device", default)
    or sessionStorage ("only for this visit"). One key per provider, any number of providers.
    Seats: fl_tree_cloud_seats [ {provider, model} ] (no keys, cap 16).
    seatOptions(): seats whose provider has a key now.
    send(mind,msgs): one POST to that provider's fixed url, key in its own header
      (Bearer | x-api-key + anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access | x-goog-api-key),
      credentials 'omit', referrerPolicy 'no-referrer', 120 s abort, non-streaming.
      Rejects { reason:'cloud', cloudText } with plain words: key not accepted (401/403),
      slow down (429), model not taken (400/404), other status, quiet, could not reach,
      no key in this browser (zero requests), unknown provider (zero requests).
    heartLine(mind), honestNote(id), mountKeyPanel(host, onSeat).
- The thread: a cloud listener goes to TreeCloudMinds.send; the heart and the waiting line name
  the provider; a cloud chair hears "[a file stayed on this machine]" instead of a file excerpt
  or name; honest errors are the module's own words.
- The panel lives inside the Gathering chair picker: <details> "Seat a mind by API key":
  Provider, Model (datalist), API key (type=password, autocomplete=off), "Only for this
  visit", "Get your <Provider> key" link, the honest note, Save and seat, saved keys with
  their last 4 characters and a Forget button each. Save seats that chair at once.
  No confirm(): Forget is immediate and says "Forgotten. The <Provider> key is gone from
  this browser."
- Honest note (exact words):
  "Your key stays in this browser on this device. theLatticeTree has no server and never sees
  it. It goes only to <P>, with each message, when a chair seated through <P> speaks. Your words
  go to <P> too, so they leave this computer; files you add stay here. Anyone using this browser
  profile could find the key. Forget removes it."

+# Gathering: bring your own key, v0.1
+
+Local minds and cloud minds you choose, side by side in the Gathering chairs, any order.
+Alpha layer, marker `v-tree-gathering-api-keys-v0`. September 30, 2026.
+
+**Temperature:** Mom seats her own Claude in the cortex chair, her llama in memory, and taps between them lik
e passing the salt.
+
+**Locks:** Layer, never delete. Local doors stay 127.0.0.1 only. The cloud road is a fixed list of nine https
  providers, no custom hosts. The key stays in this browser (localStorage, or sessionStorage for this visit onl
y) and goes only to the chosen provider, in its own header, never in a URL. No key in gatheringBinds, seats, t




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                      page 1415
source: 44d8662586


hread history or export. Files stay on this machine; a cloud chair hears only that a file stayed here. No conf
irm(). No innerHTML. textContent only. fl-connect.js untouched. No sw.js on Alpha.
+
+## What it does
+
+- In the Gathering, tap a chair, open **Seat a mind by API key**: provider, model (suggestions, or type any n
ame), your key, optional "only for this visit". **Save and seat** seats it in that chair at once.
+- Seats saved for a provider stay offered next to local minds while its key is in this browser. Forget remove
s the key; the seat waits until a key returns.
+- Tap a chair to let it speak. The thread heart says where words go: "Listening: gpt-4.1-mini through OpenAI.
  Your words go to OpenAI. Your key stays in this browser."
+- Honest failures, each in plain words: key not accepted, slow down, model not taken, could not reach, quiet.
  Nothing is invented.
+
+## Where the key lives (said in the panel, word for word)
+
+Your key stays in this browser on this device. theLatticeTree has no server and never sees it. It goes only t
o the provider, with each message, when a chair seated through it speaks. Your words go there too, so they lea
ve this computer; files you add stay here. Anyone using this browser profile could find the key. Forget remove
s it.
+
+## Map (why it is shaped this way)
+
+- FreeLattice app.html keeps one key (`fl_apiKey_enc`, AES-GCM with a device key that sits beside it in the s
ame localStorage) for one provider at a time, and calls providers straight from the browser. The Tree is anoth
er origin, so it cannot read FreeLattice's key; it keeps its own, per provider.
+- Every listed provider answers a browser preflight from https://thelatticetree.com (checked Sep 30). No Brid
ge is needed and the Bridge stays local-only.
+- Cloud seats ride the existing Gathering binds as `url: 'cloud:<provider>'`, so local-mind-probe.js and fl-c
onnect.js need no change and the Tree any-model paste is untouched.
+
+## Later (not built)
+
+- Ask a provider for its model list (GET /models with the key).
+- A custom OpenAI-compatible host (needs Kirk's call on the lock).
+- Cloud minds in Settings, Round Table and Workshop (today only Gathering chairs).
+- Streaming replies.

+// tree-cloud-minds.js · bring your own key, seat a cloud mind
+// Marker: v-tree-gathering-api-keys-v0
+//
+// Layer, never delete. Local minds stay 127.0.0.1 only. This module adds a
+// second, chosen road: a mind you pay for or got free from a provider, with
+// YOUR key, seated in a Gathering chair next to local ones, any order.

+             : 'This browser would not keep the key. Nothing was saved.';
+           return;
+         }
+       } else if (!getKey(id)) {
+         status.textContent = 'Paste your ' + p.name + ' key first. Nothing was saved.';
+         return;

+       var seat = addSeat(id, model);

+       paintProvider();
+       status.textContent = 'Saved. ' + model + ' through ' + p.name + ' can sit in any chair. Nothing was sen

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+// v-tree-glow-1-v0: every light in reach. theLatticeTree only; no fl-connect.js, no
+// FreeLattice app.html. Guards: (A) the "Use a different address" field stays inside its
+// card on a phone, (B) Settings lines fade before "the garden" pill, (C) the Nursery's
+// last card clears the galaxy hop, (D) the Gathering's Find local minds is not under the
+// promise band on wide screens, (E) legend words open their lights, and the room-page
+// reset no longer outweighs each card's own padding. No network. No kitchen.
+'use strict';
+
+var fs = require('fs');
+var path = require('path');
+var vm = require('vm');
+var assert = require('assert');
+
+var css = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'garden-rooms.css'), 'utf8');
+var js = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'garden-rooms.js'), 'utf8');
+
+// Static: the reset weighs nothing now; the old heavy selector is gone from live rules.
+assert.ok(/:where\(html\.room-page\) \*,\n:where\(html\.room-page\) \*::before,\n:where\(html\.room-page\) \*
::after \{ box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; \}/.test(css), 'room-page reset is :where (zero weig
ht)');
+assert.ok(!/^html\.room-page \*,$/m.test(css), 'the heavy reset selector is not a live rule any more');
+var glow = css.slice(css.indexOf('v-tree-glow-1-v0: every light in reach'));
+assert.ok(glow.length > 200, 'glow block at the end of garden-rooms.css');
+assert.ok(/@media \(max-width: 480px\) \{\s*\.flc-picker-row input \{[^}]*width: 100%;[^}]*max-width: 100%;[^
}]*min-width: 0;/.test(glow), 'A: field stays inside the card');
+assert.ok(/#place-veil\.is-settings::after \{[^}]*position: sticky;[^}]*pointer-events: none;/.test(glow), 'B
: soft band before the pill, never takes a tap');
+assert.ok(/html\.room-page \.room-nursery \{\s*padding-bottom: 7\.5rem;/.test(glow), 'C: Nursery clears the h
op');
+assert.ok(/@media \(min-width: 641px\) \{\s*#place-veil\.is-core \.core-promise \{\s*top: 14\.6rem;/.test(glo
w), 'D: promise band under Find local minds');

+// Runtime (vm, fake DOM): tapping a legend word opens its light.
+function El(tag) {
+ this.tagName = String(tag || 'div').toUpperCase();
+ this.tag = tag;
+ this.id = '';
+ this.className = '';
+ this.textContent = '';
+ this.hidden = false;
+ this.attrs = {};
+ this.children = [];
+ this.childNodes = this.children;
+ this.parent = null;
+ this.style = {
+    background: '',
+    boxShadow: '',
+    left: '',
+    top: '',
+    _props: {},
+    setProperty: function (k, v) { this._props[k] = String(v); },
+    getPropertyValue: function (k) { return this._props[k] || ''; }
+ };
+ var self = this;
+ this.classList = {
+    add: function (name) {
+       if ((' ' + self.className + ' ').indexOf(' ' + name + ' ') === -1) {
+         self.className = (self.className ? self.className + ' ' : '') + name;
+       }
+    },
+    remove: function (name) {
+       self.className = String(self.className || '')
+         .split(/\s+/)
+         .filter(function (c) { return c && c !== name; })
+         .join(' ');
+    },
+    contains: function (name) {
+       return (' ' + self.className + ' ').indexOf(' ' + name + ' ') !== -1;
+    }
+ };
+ this.setAttribute = function (name, val) {
+    var s = String(val);
+    this.attrs[name] = s;
+    if (name === 'id') this.id = s;
+    if (name === 'class') this.className = s;
+    if (name === 'hidden') this.hidden = true;
+ };
+ this.getAttribute = function (name) {
+    if (name === 'id') return this.id || null;
+    if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(this.attrs, name)) return this.attrs[name];
+    return null;
+ };
+ this.removeAttribute = function (name) {
+    delete this.attrs[name];
+    if (name === 'id') this.id = '';
+ };
+ this.appendChild = function (child) {
+    this.children.push(child);
+    child.parent = this;
+    return child;
+ };
+ this.querySelector = function (sel) { return queryOne(this, sel); };
+ this.querySelectorAll = function (sel) { return queryAll(this, sel); };
+ this._on = {};

+function matchOne(el, raw) {
+ var sel = String(raw || '').trim();
+ if (!sel || !el) return false;
+ if (sel.charAt(0) === '#') return el.id === sel.slice(1);
+ if (sel.charAt(0) === '.') {
+    return (' ' + (el.className || '') + ' ').indexOf(' ' + sel.slice(1) + ' ') !== -1;
+ }
+ var attrEq = sel.match(/^\[([^\]]+?)="([^"]*)"\]$/);
+ if (attrEq) return el.getAttribute(attrEq[1]) === attrEq[2];
+ var attr = sel.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]$/);
+ if (attr) return el.getAttribute(attr[1]) != null;

+function matchCompound(el, compound) {
+ var parts = String(compound || '').trim().split(/(?=[.#\[])/);
+ if (!parts.length || (parts.length === 1 && !parts[0])) return false;
+ if (/^[a-zA-Z]/.test(parts[0])) {
+    if ((el.tag || '').toLowerCase() !== parts[0].toLowerCase()) return false;
+    parts = parts.slice(1);
+ }
+ for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
+    if (parts[i] && !matchOne(el, parts[i])) return false;
+ }
+ return true;
+}

+function queryAll(root, selector) {
+ var groups = String(selector || '').split(',');

+ var nodes = walk(root, []);
+ for (var g = 0; g < groups.length; g++) {
