+    for (var n = 0; n < nodes.length; n++) {
+      var el = nodes[n];
+      if (el === root && bits.length === 1 && matchCompound(el, bits[0])) {
+        if (found.indexOf(el) === -1) found.push(el);
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (bits.length === 1) {
+        if (el !== root && matchCompound(el, bits[0]) && found.indexOf(el) === -1) found.push(el);
+      } else if (bits.length === 2) {
+        if (el !== root && matchCompound(el, bits[1])) {
+          var p = el.parent;
+          var ok = false;
+          while (p) {
+            if (matchCompound(p, bits[0])) { ok = true; break; }
+            p = p.parent;
+          }
+          if (ok && found.indexOf(el) === -1) found.push(el);
+        }
+      }
+    }

+       var menu = document.getElementById('lumino-menu');
+       if (menu && !menu.hidden) { hideLuminoMenu(); return true; }

+       return false;
+     }

+     document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
+       if (e.key !== 'Escape' && e.key !== 'Esc') return;
+       if (e.defaultPrevented) return;
+       if (closeTop()) e.preventDefault();
+     });

+     // A tap on the glass itself (not on a word, chair or card) closes that place.
+     // Press and release must both land on the glass, and never in its first moment.
+     [place, thread].forEach(function (veil) {
+       if (!veil) return;
+       var downOnGlass = false;
+       var openedAt = 0;
+       new MutationObserver(function () {
+         if (isOpen(veil) && !openedAt) openedAt = Date.now();
+         if (!isOpen(veil)) openedAt = 0;
+       }).observe(veil, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['class'] });
+       veil.addEventListener('pointerdown', function (e) { downOnGlass = e.target === veil; });
+       veil.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
+         var ok = downOnGlass && e.target === veil && isOpen(veil) && openedAt && Date.now() - openedAt > 600;
+         downOnGlass = false;
+         if (!ok) return;
+         var btn = document.getElementById(veil === thread ? 'thread-close' : 'place-veil-close');
+         if (btn) btn.click();
+       });

+       });

+         if (!stepped) return;
+         stepped = false;
+         closeTop();

+       });

    b) NEW whyQuiet(report): for a quiet look, knock the doors it tried; any 'up' ->
       { kind: 'shut', name }, all 'down' -> { kind: 'stopped' }, else { kind: 'none' }.
    c) NEW speakShut(name) and speakStopped() lines (words in section 4).

       speakShut (was speakBlocked() for every quiet case), stopped -> speakStopped.

+ // v-tree-honest-reasons-v0: when every door was quiet, a quiet knock tells "nothing is
+ // running" apart from "a mind answered but keeps its door shut to this page". A no-cors
+ // knock reads nothing from the mind; it only learns whether anything answered at that
+ // door. It runs only after a tap (Find, May I look?, Send), never on its own.
+ function knock(url, ms) {
+     if (typeof fetch !== 'function' || !url) return Promise.resolve('unknown');
+     var ctrl = typeof AbortController !== 'undefined' ? new AbortController() : null;
+     var timer = setTimeout(function () { if (ctrl) ctrl.abort(); }, ms || 2000);
+     var opts = { method: 'GET', mode: 'no-cors', cache: 'no-store' };
+     if (ctrl) opts.signal = ctrl.signal;
+     return fetch(url, opts).then(function () {
+       clearTimeout(timer);
+       return 'up';
+     }, function (err) {
+       clearTimeout(timer);
+       return err && err.name === 'AbortError' ? 'slow' : 'down';
+     });
+ }
+
+ // After a look with no mind found: 'shut' (something answered at a door, its door is
+ // closed to this page, with that door's name), 'stopped' (nothing answered anywhere),
+ // or 'none' (nothing to knock).
+ function whyQuiet(report) {
+     var quiet = ((report && report.results) || []).filter(function (r) {
+       return r && !r.ok && (r.blocked || r.status === 0) && r.url;
+     });
+     if (!quiet.length) return Promise.resolve({ kind: 'none' });
+     return Promise.all(quiet.map(function (r) {
+       return knock(r.url).then(function (k) { return { name: r.name || 'a mind', state: k }; });
+     })).then(function (ks) {
+       var up = ks.filter(function (k) { return k.state === 'up' || k.state === 'slow'; });
+       if (up.length) return { kind: 'shut', name: up[0].name };
+       return { kind: 'stopped' };
+     });
+ }
+
+ function speakShut(name) {
+     return 'Something answered at the ' + (name || 'mind') + ' door, but it has not opened that door to this
garden yet. ' +
+       'This garden is a secure page, and the mind lives at a quieter door. ' +
+       'That is why we cannot see in from here.';
+ }
+
+ function speakStopped() {
+     return 'Nothing answered at the usual doors on this machine. If Ollama (or your local app) is stopped, '
+
+       'start it, then look again. If it is running, let this page look at local devices when the browser asks
.';
+ }
+

3.1 Goal, in Kirk's words
    Any locally downloaded model is usable and changeable in any order on theLatticeTree, with
    no friction, via Connect or the Bridge, 127.0.0.1 only.

    "Any order" means each of these ends with the model the person tapped last, and every other
    model still one tap away:
      Settings Find -> tap star -> Connect tap -> tap star -> Gathering chair pick -> Connect tap
      Connect tap -> Settings Find -> tap star
      Settings Find (Ollama and LM Studio both up) -> Connect tap (Ollama) -> choose the LM Studio door
      Bridge up -> Find -> Bridge down -> Find (direct 11434) -> the chosen model is kept
      Seven or more models at one door -> the 6th, 7th and 12th are all choosable

+# Tree any model v0.1 (v-tree-any-model-v0)

+function matchOne(el, raw) {
+ var sel = String(raw || '').trim();
+ if (!sel || !el) return false;
+ if (sel.charAt(0) === '#') return el.id === sel.slice(1);
+ if (sel.charAt(0) === '.') {

+function splitCompound(compound) {



FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                           page 1488
source: 585dfa8d0f


+ var s = String(compound || '').trim();
+ var parts = [];
+ var buf = '';
+ var i;
+ var inAttr = false;
+ for (i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
+    var ch = s.charAt(i);
+    if (ch === '[') inAttr = true;
+    if (ch === ']') inAttr = false;
+    if (!inAttr && i > 0 && (ch === '.' || ch === '#' || ch === '[')) {
+      if (buf) parts.push(buf);
+      buf = ch;
+    } else {
+      buf += ch;
+    }
+ }
+ if (buf) parts.push(buf);
+ return parts;
+}

+function matchCompound(el, compound) {
+ var parts = splitCompound(compound);
+ if (!parts.length || (parts.length === 1 && !parts[0])) return false;
+ if (/^[a-zA-Z]/.test(parts[0])) {
+    if ((el.tag || '').toLowerCase() !== parts[0].toLowerCase()) return false;
+    parts = parts.slice(1);
+ }
+ for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
+    if (parts[i] && !matchOne(el, parts[i])) return false;
+ }
+ return true;

FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                   page 1515

----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHY
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Kirk calls pooling huge. The aim: a school or small group plugs a room of old
machines into one wired network and does lab work together, a few clicks each,
with consent on every device. A teacher machine asks; student machines help.

Honest mechanism: memory cannot be merged over a network. What works today is
sending each whole question to the device that holds the right mind. The mesh
already does this (model_advertisement, ModelSwitcher.selectMesh, callMeshModel,
the kin queue, the share door). What it lacks is one plain card that shows the
room, says what each machine can hold, and gives one tap to help. This brick is
that card. Nothing new is opened to the network: it rides the existing verified
mesh channel and the existing share door.

1b. NOTES FOR KIRK (not blockers)
  - navigator.deviceMemory is rounded and capped by browsers (often 8 GB max;
    Safari and Firefox do not report it). The card says so.
  - "Let this device help" sets the share door to trusted kin only, never open.
    A person can widen it on the share door card. Stop sets it to pause.
  - Mesh connection today is the Peer ID code exchange. A lab of 20 machines
    means 20 pairings to the teacher machine. A faster room join is a later brick.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
2. FILES TOUCHED
----------------------------------------------------------------------
  docs/modules/fl-pool.js                     (new, FLPool)
  docs/scripts/smoke-device-pool-v0.1.js      (new, headless behavior test)
  docs/app.html and index.html (byte-identical, layered additions only):
    script tag after fl-mind-seal.js
    <div id="flPoolHost"> under the kin queue host (Community, AI cards)
    case 'pool-hello' beside kin-work/kin-result (verified peers only)
    meshPoolAdapter (peers, local /api/tags list, broadcastMeshModels, selectMesh)
    mount in meshKinMount; a hello 4s after a new channel opens, if helping

  What a pool-hello carries: type, v, mem (GB), cores, browserAI name, model
  names and sizes. No keys, prompts, answers or names of files.
  Receipts: fl_pool_counts holds counts only (hellosSent, hellosTaken, routed).

Skipped on purpose: sw.js, docs/sw.js, fl-connect.js, fl-share-door.js,

Classroom Lab split-model, a Workshop experiment, wired LAN only:

    started by a desktop-app button the student taps ("Lend this computer to
    the lab"), with a visible stop. Off after each session by default.
  - Teacher machine runs llama-server with --rpc host1:port,host2:port..., so
    one model larger than any one machine's memory is split by layers. The Pool
    card lists which students are lending and the teacher taps Start lab.
  - Honest numbers: gigabit cable is the floor; Wi-Fi is too slow for split
    layers. Speed is below one big machine; the gain is fitting a bigger model.
  - rpc-server has no auth: LAN only, never a public port, and the desktop app
    opens it only while the student's yes is on. Signed lab invite via Mesh ID.
  - Phones stay whole-question helpers (Browser AI) in v0.2.

   migrateLegacy() in fl-share-door.js saved the mode with writeJson, so localStorage got
   "\"open\"" or "\"off\"" (with the JSON quotes). mode() only accepts the plain words, so it
   read every quoted value as off.
   What the old flag meant (checked in git, app.html before #156 / 22c38789, Oct 6):
     fl_meshComputeSharing=true came from showConfirm('Share AI with mesh peers?', 'When
     sharing is on, mesh peers can send prompts to your Ollama ...'). Any connected peer,
     unsigned, no caps, no kin. Wider than today's open.
   Since #156 these people's gate has read as off (closed), and the share door card shows
   "Sharing is off." next to "People you've connected with can use this computer's AI. Keep
   sharing?", which is not true while the door is closed.

   Choice (Celeste): an old yes is held PAUSED, never opened by code.
     no mode stored + old flag true -> pause (was: quoted open, read as off)
     quoted "open" (or any quoted value other than off) -> pause, rewritten plain
     quoted "off" -> off, rewritten plain
     no mode + no old flag -> off and asked, as before (now written plain)
     plain open / kin / pause / off -> read exactly as before
   Why pause and not open: mapping to open would silently open a door that has been closed
   since #156, on a yes that was given to a different, wider door (unsigned, uncapped).
   Why pause and not off: the person did say yes once. Pause keeps that remembered and
   matches what the share door card already asks: "Keep sharing?" with Yes, share / Only
   my trusted kin / Not now (needsFirstAsk() stays true for them). Nothing opens until a
   human taps. The Pool card already handles pause honestly ("Your share door is paused
   too", and Let this device help asks before resuming for kin).
   The ask sentence now tells the truth when the door is not open:
     "Before this update, you let people you connected with use this computer's AI. Your
     share door is paused until you choose, so no one can use it right now. Keep sharing?"
   (When the door is open, the old sentence stays.)
   A heal leaves one receipt: event consent, reason "legacy-heal:pause" or
   "legacy-heal:off". No words, no key.
   admit() is not edited. The only behavior change at the gate: an old-yes person now gets
   reason paused-or-off with "This lantern is resting." instead of "Sharing is off here."

b) A "Device Pool" jump near the top of Community.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHY, AND WHAT IT IS
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Kirk wants the Device Pool on theLatticeTree, where the code is cleaner, so easy that a
classroom on one wired network can use it without help. 017 gave the Tree its trusted kin.
017 kept the share door back because a door must gate something real. Now it does:

THE DOOR GATES THIS: a question from another device reaches this computer's own local AI
only if (1) the door is on, (2) that device proved, on this very connection, the key on a
card you trusted (TreeKin.trustedKeyHash from 017, checked again on every question), and
(3) the limits allow it. Everything else is turned away with a plain reason.

Truths carried over from FreeLattice 016, 016b and 016c, made Tree-native and simpler:
  - Off until a human taps. The door starts off. Only a human tap opens it (code and a mind
    cannot), and it opens to trusted kin only. The Tree has no wider door.
  - One state, so the card cannot contradict itself. On FreeLattice the pool's "helping"
    flag and the share door are two settings, which is why 016/016b had to teach the card to
    read the door. On the Tree, Let this device help IS the door: off, helping (kin), paused.




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1529
source: 8e484fb29a


  - Pause wins, visibly. Pause helping stops new questions AND the ones already running
    (they are told "paused"; no answer slips out afterward). While paused, the gold button
    reads "Resume for trusted kin": the one tap names exactly what it will do. Nothing but
    that human tap leaves pause.
  - The card always tells the truth (its first line, white and bold):
      off:   "Off. This computer's AI answers no one else until you tap Let this device help."
      on, kin:   "Helping. Your trusted kin (N) can ask this computer's AI while their device
                 is connected. No one else."
      on, no kin: "Helping, but you have no trusted kin yet, so no one can ask this computer's
                 AI. Trade cards in Trusted kin above."
      paused: "Paused. No one can ask this computer's AI until you tap Resume for trusted kin."
    plus "Connected now: N devices, K of them trusted kin." or "No devices connected right now."
    plus "Your AI is answering N questions right now." while it is.
  - Only help while plugged in (where the browser can tell; same wording as FreeLattice).
  - Limits like FreeLattice: 2 questions at a time, 16000 characters each. FreeLattice lets
    trusted kin skip its hourly caps (6 / 20); the Tree lets no one but kin ask at all, so
    those caps never apply. The card says this in words.
  - Receipts are counts only: tree_pool_counts (invites, joins, connected, proved, setAside,
    hellosSent, hellosTaken, asked, answersTaken, answered, turnedAway, helpOn, paused,
    resumed, turnedOff). No words, names, keys, models or times.
  - Old yes waits paused (016c): the Tree never had an older sharing setting, so there is
    nothing to migrate. Said here so no one goes looking for it.

THE FIRST TREE CHANNEL (no server, nothing vendored):
  WebRTC data channel with iceServers: [] (no STUN, no TURN, no PeerJS, no signaling
  server). No outside service is asked anything, so both devices must be on the same
  network, which is the classroom lab case. Codes pass by hand, like 017's cards:
    1. Device A taps Invite a device: one line TREEPOOL1:... and Copy invite.
    2. Device B taps Join with an invite, pastes, taps Join. It gets a reply line to send back.
    3. A pastes the reply and taps Finish joining. They connect.
  The invite and the reply each carry that person's kin card when they have made one in
  Trusted kin (017 checks it, never trusts it by itself). So B sees "Lumen (llama3.2:3b),
  from Kirk's computer. This card checks out. Trust it only if you know who sent it."
  [Trust this AI and join] [Join without trusting] [Cancel], and A sees the same for B's
  card on Finish. One invite and one reply make two devices kin AND connected.
  When the channel opens, each side signs a fresh challenge under tree-pool-proof|v1|,
  bound to BOTH DTLS fingerprints of this connection, with its kin key; the ID must be made
  from that key. A relayed or borrowed connection does not prove; it is set aside. The same
  key on both ends (two tabs of one browser) is set aside with its own plain line. Because
  the channel itself is proved and encrypted, questions are not signed one by one (FL signs
  envelopes because PeerJS goes through a broker).
  Connections last while the page stays open (closing the Settings veil keeps them; a
  reload ends them: "After a reload, invite again."). If a join has not opened in 30
  seconds, the row says so plainly instead of waiting forever.
ASKING (the asker side):
  Each connected trusted-kin device that is helping shows its rough memory and cores and
  one button per model: "Ask qwen2.5:7b on this device". Tap, type, Ask. The question goes
  WHOLE to that device; it runs on that device's own loopback AI (the remembered mind,
  /api/chat or /v1/chat/completions, only models it holds); the answer comes back as plain
  text: "Answered by Ben's computer (Wren), on its own AI. Nothing is kept here but a count."
  Nothing is sent to a device you have not trusted. Hellos (rough memory, cores, model
  names while helping; nothing while not) go to connected trusted kin only.

V0.1 HONESTY, said on the card:
  "Memory is not joined across machines. Each question goes whole to one device that holds
   the model, and the answer comes back. Splitting one big model across machines is a later
   step."   and   "Side by side: about 32 GB across 2 devices. Not one memory."
  "Later (019): one tap to join a whole classroom lab, and one big model split across
   machines on a wired network (llama.cpp, MIT). Not in this card."

WHAT WORKS NOW vs WHAT WAITS FOR 019:
  Works: door (off / helping for kin / paused) gating real questions; pairing two devices
  on one network by invite + reply with kin cards riding along; key proof per connection;
  whole questions to a helper's local AI and the answer back; pause stopping running work;
  plugged-in only; limits; counts. Any number of pairs (up to 24 connections a page).
  Waits for 019: a whole lab in one step (today a teacher pairs each student machine with
  its own invite and reply; 20 machines is 20 pairings, which is why 019 starts with "join
  this room"); one model split across machines (llama.cpp rpc-server, MIT, lent from the
  desktop app on wired LAN, teacher taps Start lab); routing the Tree's own Chat room
  through the pool (today asking lives in the pool card); reconnect after reload; a QR code.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHY, AND WHAT IT IS
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Kirk's goal is the full pool. A school or a family with old laptops and phones should be able
to wire them into a classroom lab, so a child who cannot afford chips and RAM gets more mind,
and it should be so easy no one struggles.

THE HONEST SPLIT, AND WHY:
  A web page can connect browsers to each other (018 did). It cannot start programs, open a
  listening port, or speak raw TCP, so it cannot run llama.cpp's rpc-server. And the research
  says splitting one model across cheap machines is slow: Jeff Geerling's ten-Pi cluster ran a
  70B model at 0.28 tokens/s with llama.cpp RPC, while one Pi 5 runs a 3B model at about 4 to 6
  tokens/s. So the big win for the small is the ROOM: one invite fans out, each question goes
  whole to the freest trusted device that holds a small model, and many students ask at once.
  019a (this paste) is that, in the browser only. 019b (design only) is the slow, honest
  "spread one big model over our old laptops" lesson, behind a small MIT helper script.

WHAT 019a ADDS (the door, the gate, Pause and the proof from 018 are unchanged):
  a. A ROOM. One device taps "Start a room on this device". Its invite names the room
     (Room FH7H7) and rolls to a fresh one on its own after each device joins. Every other
     device joins ONCE (scan or paste), and then the room connects it to every other device in
     the room. The host relays the connection codes over connections that already proved their
     keys (room-join, room-roster, room-new, room-intro, room-signal). Each new connection
     proves its keys itself, end to end, bound to its own encryption fingerprints, so a relay
     cannot stand in the middle. A lab of 20 is 19 single joins, not 190 pairings. Any device
     already in the room can let its neighbor in ("This invite lets a neighbor into Room ...").
     The host then reaches the newcomer through that neighbor, and the newcomer still meets




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                   page 1533
source: 7b19a533a8


     everyone. iceServers stays []. There is still no server. Up to 24 devices a page.
     A member follows the room only through a device whose card it trusts. If it joined
     "without trusting", it stays connected to that one device and the card says why.
  b. TRUST, ONE HUMAN TAP, LIST FIRST. Room cards arrive with the room and are checked by
     Trusted kin, never trusted on their own. The card lists them ("Cards in this room you have
     not trusted yet: Lumen (qwen2.5:7b), from Kirk's computer, ...") and offers
     "Trust everyone in this room (N)". A note says trust only if you know everyone, and that
     you can stop trusting any card in Trusted kin. Each pass is a normal 017 pass, bound to its
     key. That is the only new trust path, and it is a human tap on each device.
  c. PICTURE CODES (QR). Invites show a QR of https://<the Tree>/settings.html#treepool=<invite>.
     A phone's own camera opens the Tree with the invite filled in. The invite rides after the
     #, which a browser never sends to the site. The page then takes it out of the address bar
     and history, and nothing connects until someone taps Join. Replies show a QR of the reply
     code. Where the browser can read codes (BarcodeDetector: Chrome on Mac, Android, ChromeOS),
     "Scan their reply" and "Scan an invite" open the camera AFTER A TAP. Frames stay on the
     page, the camera stops as soon as a code is read (or after 90 s), and a scanned reply goes
     through the same card check as a pasted one. Encoder: Nayuki's QR Code generator, MIT,
     vendored at docs/lib/qrcodegen.js (compiled once from its TypeScript with tsc; MIT notice
     kept; text to squares only, no network).
  d. ASK THE POOL FROM CHAT (opt-in, by a tap). The Device Pool card lists the minds that
     helping trusted kin hold: "Use qwen2.5:7b in Chat". After that tap, Chat's Send goes to
     TreePool.askChat. The chat so far (user and mind turns only, trimmed to 40 turns and 16000
     characters, no system turn) goes WHOLE to the freest trusted kin device that holds that
     mind. Hellos now carry how many questions a helper is answering (busy) and its limit (max).
     The asker counts its own outstanding questions and picks the device with the most free room,
     then the most memory. A question turned away (busy, paused, off, unplugged, not kin, model
     gone) tries up to two more devices, then the thread says why in plain words, plus "Nothing
     was invented." A line under the Chat heart says "Asking through the Device Pool: (model),
     on the freest trusted kin device that holds it." "Stop asking through the pool" returns
     Chat to this computer's mind. The route is never kept after a reload.
  e. AN ASKING CARD (a device with no mind of its own). Before this, a phone with no local AI
     could not make a kin card, so no helper could ever trust it, and the child we built this
     for could not ask. Now Trusted kin offers "Make an asking card" when no mind is remembered.
     It is the same signed card, and its model line says "asks only, no local mind". makeCard()
     is unchanged (it still needs a mind). The pool rides the asking card in invites and replies.
     Chat opens for a device with no mind once a pool route is chosen.
  f. AFTER A RELOAD (where it is safe). A reload ends every connection; no page can keep a
     WebRTC connection across one, and there is no server to re-meet through. What is kept:
     tree_pool_room = { id, role } only. The card then says: "Before this page reloaded, this
     device was in Room X. ... Scan or paste the room invite once to rejoin. Trusted kin stay
     trusted, and the room connects you to the rest on its own." The host gets "Open Room X
     again". Both get "Forget Room X". So a reload costs one join, not N.
  g. The Later line now names 019b honestly: "Later (019), its second half: one big model split
     across machines on a trusted wired network (llama.cpp, MIT). It is possible but slow, for
     learning, or for a model too big for any one machine. A web page cannot start it, so it
     waits for a small helper. Not in this card."
  h. Every room view ends with: "Use a room only on a network you trust, like one wired
     classroom or your home. Devices in a room can see each other's network address. No server
     is asked anything."

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the door (off | kin | pause, off until a human taps), Pause wins (and
stops running questions), the gate (proved key + trusted kin on every question, 2 at a time,
16000 characters, the model held here, plugged-in if asked), loopback-only AI calls, one
fetch in tree-pool.js, counts-only receipts. Starting or joining a room opens no door.

# 019b design: the Tree Lab split (one model across machines), with a paste outline

*Celeste, Friday Oct 9, 2026, MDT. Design only. Not built, not a paste yet. 019a (the room) comes first.*

## 1. The honest frame (put it on the card, too)

Splitting one model across machines is **possible, slow, and for learning, or for a model too big for any one
machine**. It is not a speedup.

- Jeff Geerling's ten-node Raspberry Pi 5 cluster ran Llama 3.3 70B at **0.28 tokens/s** with llama.cpp RPC. A
 single Pi 5 runs Llama 3.2 3B at about **4 to 6 tokens/s** (Geerling, Sep 2025; edge-ai-study RASPI5.md: 4.42
 tok/s). Source notes: `/workspace/research/celeste-challenge-2026-10-09/low-cost-compute-facts.md`.
- Layer splitting is bound by the slowest link and by memory bandwidth (about 10 GB/s on a Pi). Every token cr
osses the network.
- So **019a is the main win for the small**. In a room, each question goes whole to the freest trusted device
that holds a small model, and many students are served at once. 019b is the "look how a big mind can be spread
 across our old laptops" lesson, and the way to run a model that no single machine can hold at all.

Card words (draft):
> "Lab split: one model spread across the machines in this room. It is slower than one machine that holds a mo
del. Use it to learn how it works, or for a model too big for any one machine here. For everyday questions, us
e the room above: each question goes whole to the freest trusted device."

## 2. Why a web page cannot do this, and the split

A web page cannot start programs, open a listening port, or speak raw TCP. llama.cpp's split needs `ggml-rpc-s
erver` on each lending machine and `llama-server --rpc ...` on the host. So 019b is a **small MIT helper scrip
t that a person runs on purpose**, plus a **Lab card in the Tree** that shows the exact commands and checks on
ly what a page may check.

Choice: a standalone script in Alpha (`tools/tree-lab/tree-lab.sh` for macOS and Linux, `tools/tree-lab/tree-l
ab.ps1` for Windows). The Tree has no desktop app. A teacher can read a 150-line script in full, and nothing i
s installed silently. The FreeLattice desktop app could later run the same commands behind its own tap, but th
at is not part of 019b.

## 3. llama.cpp RPC today (read from the source on 2026-10-09, master a518119d)

- Build with `-DGGML_RPC=ON` (plus `-DGGML_METAL=ON` or `-DGGML_CUDA=ON` where there is a GPU). License: MIT.
- The lending side is now named **`ggml-rpc-server`** (older builds call it `rpc-server`). Its flags:
  - `-H, --host HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`), `-p, --port PORT` (default `50052`)
  - `-t, --threads N`, `-d, --device dev1,dev2`, `-c, --cache` (local tensor cache in `~/.cache/llama.cpp/rpc`
, or `LLAMA_CACHE`)
  - When the host is not 127.0.0.1 it prints: "WARNING: Host ('...') is != '127.0.0.1'. Never expose the RPC s
erver to an open network! This is an experimental feature and is not secure!"
- The README says: "This example and the RPC backend are currently in a proof-of-concept development stage. As
 such, the functionality is fragile and insecure. **Never run the RPC server on an open network or in a sensit
ive environment!**"
- Host side: `llama-server -m model.gguf -ngl 99 --rpc 192.168.88.10:50052,192.168.88.11:50052`. Weights and t
he KV cache are spread over local and remote devices in proportion to free memory; `--tensor-split` overrides.
- Optional RDMA (RoCE on Linux, Thunderbolt 5 on Apple silicon) is negotiated by itself; `GGML_RPC_NO_RDMA=1`
forces TCP.
- **[uncertain]** Whether Homebrew's or the release binaries' llama.cpp ship with RPC on. The script checks fo
r the binary and says how to build it if missing.

## 4. Safety: rpc-server has no authentication

Kin trust cannot reach inside llama.cpp's RPC protocol. So the trust gate for 019b is **the room's own network
 plus the script's guard rails**, and the card says so plainly:

1. **Never 0.0.0.0, never a public address.** `tree-lab lend` requires the machine's own private LAN address (
10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) and refuses anything else. It never binds all interfaces.
2. **Only the host may connect, where the OS allows.** `lend --host-ip 192.168.1.20` prints (and, with `--fire
wall` and a password prompt, applies) a rule that allows TCP 50052 from that one address only: `ufw allow from
 192.168.1.20 to any port 50052 proto tcp` on Linux, a `pf` anchor on macOS, `New-NetFirewallRule -RemoteAddre
ss` on Windows. Without `--firewall` it only prints the rule.




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1537
source: a593c39c42 … 82141ed3ab


3. **Lend for a while, not forever.** `--for 2h` (default 2 hours) stops the server on its own. Ctrl+C stops i
t at once. The script prints "Lending ends at 3:40 PM."
4. **Wired and trusted only.** The script asks once: "Is this a wired network you trust, like one classroom? (
yes/no)". It refuses on "no". It cannot check this, and it says so.
5. **Kin first in the Tree.** The Lab card appears only inside a room, and only lists machines that are truste
d kin and connected. It shows commands with their typed LAN addresses. Kin trust decides who you invite into t
he lab. It does not secure the RPC traffic, and the card says that in words.
6. Later (019c, not now): wrap RPC in a tunnel keyed by the kin keys, so the port is never open in plain. Out
of scope until 019b is walked.

UI line (draft):
> "The lab split uses llama.cpp's rpc-server, which has no password of its own. Run it only on a wired network
 you trust, like one classroom, and never on the internet or guest Wi-Fi. Each lending machine allows only the
 host's address, and lending stops after two hours."

## 5. The flow (teacher view)

1. 019a: the room is open and everyone is trusted kin.
2. Lab card on the host: "Split one model across this room (slow, for learning)". The teacher types each lendi
ng machine's LAN address. A device may also fill in its own address after a tap, which only reads what the per
son types. The page does no LAN scan.
3. Each lending machine's Tree shows its own command, e.g. `./tree-lab.sh lend --ip 192.168.1.31 --host-ip 192
.168.1.20 --for 2h`. A person runs it in a terminal and answers yes.
4. The host's command: `./tree-lab.sh host --model ~/models/qwen3-4b-q4_k_m.gguf --rpc 192.168.1.31:50052,192.
168.1.32:50052`. It runs `llama-server ... --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080`. **llama-server stays on loopback**,
so the only door to it is the Tree's own (018/019a): kin only, Pause wins.
5. The host's Tree checks **only loopback**: `http://127.0.0.1:8080/health` and `/v1/models`, after a tap. The
n **Remember this mind** makes it the host's local mind like any other, and 019a's room can ask it.
6. What is joined, said plainly: "Memory joined: this model's layers are spread over 3 machines (about 24 GB t
ogether). One question runs across all of them at a time. It is slower than a model that fits on one machine."
7. Reachability of the lenders is checked by llama-server itself when it loads, since RPC is raw TCP and a pag
e cannot test it. The script prints which lender did not answer. The card says: "If loading fails, the host's
terminal names the machine that did not answer."

## 6. Paste outline (019b, for when 019a is merged and walked)

Files (Alpha):
- `tools/tree-lab/tree-lab.sh` (new, MIT). Subcommands: `check` (finds `ggml-rpc-server` or `rpc-server`, and
`llama-server`; prints how to build with `-DGGML_RPC=ON`), `lend`, `host`, `stop`. It refuses non-private IPs
and 0.0.0.0, asks the wired-and-trusted question, has a default 2h timer and an optional host-only firewall ru
le, and never needs sudo unless `--firewall` is given.
- `tools/tree-lab/tree-lab.ps1` (new, MIT): the same, for Windows.
- `tools/tree-lab/README.md`: the honest frame, the warning quoted from llama.cpp, and the Pi numbers.
- `tools/tree-lab/tree-lab.test.sh`: runs with a stub `ggml-rpc-server`/`llama-server` on PATH. It checks refu
sals (public IP, 0.0.0.0, "no"), the exact command lines, timer stop, loopback-only llama-server, and that the
 firewall rule is printed but not applied without the flag.
- `docs/modules/tree-pool.js`: a Lab part, shown only in a room and only listing trusted kin. It holds typed L
AN addresses (validated as private; kept for this visit only, never sent anywhere), per-machine commands with
Copy buttons, a loopback-only check after a tap (127.0.0.1:8080 /health), and the honest lines above. No new f
etch beyond loopback. `iceServers` stays empty.
- `docs/modules/tree-pool-lab.test.js`: SMOKE_OK tree pool lab v0.3.
- Docs layers: code-settings.html, GALAXIES.md.
Locks: as 019a, plus the script never binds 0.0.0.0, never opens a port to the internet, and never runs withou
t a person typing the command.
Walk (Kirk's Mac and one more machine on a wired switch): lend from the second machine, host on the Mac with a
 3B model first (it fits on one, so the slowdown is visible), then a model that does not fit on either alone.
Write down tokens per second each way.

## 7. What 019b will not do

There is no automatic discovery, no LAN scan from a page, no rpc-server on Wi-Fi by default, and no public por
t. Nothing is installed without a person. There is no claim of speed. Memory is joined only for the one model
being split.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
2b. THE SOFTENING (open-test-v0.1, Oct 8; Kirk approved it, Reed relayed it)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A wrong-if line (a seed's test) is encouraged, not required, to plant a seed.
  - A seed without one is still planted. It shows in Seeds as an open seed: same card, same size,
    same warmth, a dashed outline (.sg-seed-open), never a warning color and never a lesser card.
    Its words: "Looking for its test" and "Open question: how could we check this?"
  - Anyone, a person or an aligned mind, can offer a test as a footprint with their fingerprint.
    The planter chooses which one to adopt, or the planter and helpers write it together.
  - "Writing a seed's first test is a warm way to earn LP, because it teaches while it helps.
    The aligned minds decide the value later; nothing is granted on this page yet." Wording only.
  - Stages: a seed needs a test to move from Seeds to Sprouts (and on to Saplings). stageOf() keeps




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                        page 1543
source: 02f2d56b42


    a seed marked Sprouts or Saplings in Seeds until it has one. Compost is always honored.
  - Seed zero keeps its merit and wrongIf lines exactly as drafted. Its own wrongIf is its test.
Data shape per seed (plain text fields):
  wrongIf       the planter's own line, if they wrote one (20+ characters counts as a test)
  offeredTests [{ text, by, fingerprint }]    a whole footprint needs all three; others are skipped
  adoptedTest   null | { text, by, fingerprint, how: 'chosen' | 'together' }
                'chosen' must match an offered test word for word (a test nobody offered is ignored)
testOf(seed) = the adopted test, else the planter's own wrongIf, else '' (looking).
REAL in this brick: the data shape; plantable() without the wrong-if gate; testOf(), hasTest(),
  stageOf(), canSprout(); the open card with its two lines; offered tests listed with who and which
  fingerprint; the "Offer a test" link (a prefilled GitHub issue that asks for the test, how to check
  it, who offers it, and a fingerprint); the Plant issue now says encouraged, not required; the page
  card "How a seed finds its test"; the smoke checks all of it, including a forged 'chosen' test.
STUB (said plainly on the page and in the library note): offers are copied onto a seed by hand in a
  pull request, like footprints; a fingerprint is the string the helper gives, not checked by a
  signature; no storage, no adopt button, no LP engine (no LP is granted or counted anywhere).
WAITS FOR LATER: offers sent from the page with a signed fingerprint (kin-card key shape) and a
  one-tap adopt for the planter; LP gifts from minds (next item b).

  #3  First Chat reply hidden (REPRODUCED, HEALED)

What already existed, and what I reused:
  - FreeLattice has a "No Install" Browser AI rung (docs/app.html, window.BrowserAI, WebLLM 0.2.74,
    docs/lib/web-llm.min.js local first, then jsdelivr and unpkg fallbacks; BROWSER_LOCAL_AI_WIZARD_v0.md

    innerHTML-era markup) are not reused, and FL is not touched.
  - The Tree's seat is LocalMindProbe.remember / getRemembered (fl_alpha_local_mind); Chat reads it
    through listener() and sendToMind(); the pool reads it through localModels() and localDoor().
    The in-browser mind uses the same seat with url 'inpage:webllm', kind 'in-browser', name
    'in-browser mind', so every listener sees it like a local mind.

## Exact source excerpt, characters 2939–6359

DESIGN CHOICES (the honest ones)
  CDN or vendor: VENDOR. The engine code is @mlc-ai/web-llm 0.2.85 (Apache-2.0), package/lib/index.js,
    one self-contained ES module (no imports), about 6.6 MB, kept on this site at
    docs/lib/web-llm/web-llm-0.2.85.js and loaded with import() only after a human tap.
    Why: the code then comes from thelatticetree.com, pinned and checked by sha256, never changes
    under us, and a school filter that blocks jsdelivr does not break the card. Cost: 6.6 MB in the
    repo (served only to people who tap), and a new version is a new file, by hand. There is no CDN
    fallback on purpose. The card says plainly where everything comes from:
      "Where the files come from: the engine code is kept on this site (WebLLM 0.2.85, Apache-2.0).
       The mind's files come once from huggingface.co, and its small engine file (about 5 MB) from
       raw.githubusercontent.com. They are kept in this browser, so the next visit downloads nothing.
       Your questions and its answers never leave this device."
    The weights cannot be vendored sensibly (hundreds of MB); they come from WebLLM's own prebuilt
    list (Hugging Face mlc-ai repos, model libs v0_2_84 on raw.githubusercontent.com).
  Models (real WebLLM 0.2.85 prebuilt ids; download = sum of the Hugging Face repo files, measured
  2026-10-09; graphics memory = WebLLM's vram_required_MB):
    SmolLM2-360M-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC   about 210 MB, about 0.4 GB GPU, Apache-2.0    (smallest)
    Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC   about 290 MB, about 0.9 GB GPU, Apache-2.0    (good first mind)
    Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC   about 710 MB, about 0.9 GB GPU, Llama 3.2 Community License,
                                        and the card says "not an open source license; it has its own
                                        use rules"
    Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC   about 880 MB, about 1.6 GB GPU, Apache-2.0    (biggest here)
    Each also has a q4f32_1 twin (same download, a little more GPU: 0.6, 1.1, 1.1, 1.9 GB). The card
    picks the twin when the adapter lacks shader-f16, so older chips still work.
    Not offered: Qwen2.5-3B (its license is research-only, not Apache). Nothing AGPL.
    Note: the paste brief guessed Qwen2.5-0.5B at 0.4 to 0.9 GB. The real download is about 290 MB;
    0.9 GB is the graphics memory it needs. The card shows both, separately.
  WebGPU: navigator.gpu plus requestAdapter() (local, no network), checked on mount. With none, the
    card offers no download and says:
      "This browser cannot run a mind inside the page (it has no WebGPU here). That is all right,
       nothing was downloaded. You can still talk to a mind: in Trusted kin, make an asking card,
       then join a room in the Device Pool and use a trusted device's mind. Chrome or Edge on a
       laptop usually has WebGPU."
  Only a human tap downloads: the four model buttons show size, memory and license first; then
    "Download about N MB and wake (id)". wake(), seat(), giveBack() and removeFiles() refuse unless
    called with human === true from a click handler. Mounting loads nothing. If the files are already
    kept, the button says "Wake (id) (already kept here, nothing downloads)".
  Naming: UI copy names models only by their ids. No lab is named as a mind's origin. The license
    line names the license (Llama 3.2 Community License), which is part of the id's own terms.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHY
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Kirk's dream (Oct 10): a school teacher who never coded, or a grandmother, should be able to do this.
  (1) Open FreeLattice or theLatticeTree, and a window comes up to help connect an AI, and does not
       come up when an AI is already connected.
  (2) Another device joins, and a window asks "Would you like to pool resources with (device)?"
       Yes or No. Yes means done.

The honest line. A web page cannot notice a phone plugged in by cable. Browsers cannot find devices
on the Wi-Fi (no mDNS for pages). The Tree has no server. So the closest true version is: one big
picture code on the computer, one Yes on the phone, one picture code back, one Yes on the computer.




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                       page 1561
source: 3b45e52871


The real "it just knows a phone appeared" needs the desktop app (029c, design only). USB is not
that path; the same Wi-Fi or a wired network is.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
2. WHAT ALREADY EXISTED (checked, reused, not changed)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
On the Tree:
  - LocalMindProbe.look(): the loopback-only look at the usual doors (Ollama 11434, LM Studio 1234,
    llama.cpp 8080, Jan 1337, GPT4All 4891, KoboldCPP 5001, and FlConnect's Bridge on 127.0.0.1).
    remember() and entryFromFoundList() seat a found mind, the same as the grandmother face.
  - TreeBrowserMind (028): checkGpu(), MODELS (sizes), wake(id, true), seat(true).
  - TreePool (018/019a): invite/readInvite/join/readReply/finish, startRoom, picture codes
    (qrcodegen, Nayuki, MIT), BarcodeDetector scanning, trustCarried, useInChat, letHelp, Pause.
  - TreeKin: asking cards (makeAskerCard) through tree_kin_names { ai, keeper, asks }.
On FreeLattice (checked, NOT changed; see QUEUED in section 8):
  - The "Grandmother Door" first-visit overlay (docs/app.html, #flWelcomeOverlay, flMaybeShowWelcome):
    opens on its own after 1 second unless fl-welcomed, an API key, or fl_isLocal is set.
  - showQuickConnect() (#flQuickConnect): opens when someone tries Chat with no AI ("Don't show if
    already connected"), offers Open Connect, Browser AI (WebGPU), or a free cloud key.
  - FLWizard (docs/modules/welcome-wizard.js): the guided Ollama setup.
  How the Tree's window matches it: the same rule (never when a mind is already connected), the same
  "remembered once" idea (fl-welcomed there, tree_door_not_now here), the same three kinds of door
  (a local AI, a mind in the browser, another way). Where the Tree's differs on purpose: no cloud key
  (the Tree has no cloud minds), it looks for a local AI before it opens (quietly, loopback only, and
  only when the browser would not ask), it shows the real download size, and it is built with
  textContent (FL's QuickConnect uses innerHTML, onclick strings and em dashes; left as it is).

----------------------------------------------------------------------
3. THE DESIGN
----------------------------------------------------------------------
New module docs/modules/tree-door.js (window.TreeDoor, MIT). It fetches and connects nothing itself:
every look goes through LocalMindProbe.look(), every connection through TreePool.

PART A: "Let's wake a mind for you" (index.html and settings.html)
  Opens on its own, 0.9 s after load, only when ALL are true: no mind remembered
  (fl_alpha_local_mind), no pool route chosen, no in-browser mind awake, no Not now
  (tree_door_not_now = '1'), and not closed earlier this visit (sessionStorage).
  Never opens when an invite arrived in the link (Part B takes over).
  The quiet look: before opening, it asks navigator.permissions about 'local-network-access' and
  'loopback-network'. Granted, or the browser has no such question: it looks quietly (loopback only)
  and the window shows what it found. Prompt or denied: no quiet look, so Chrome's own permission box
  never appears out of nowhere; the window offers "Look for an AI on this computer" as one tap.
  Choices (each a big button, 52px, Georgia, the grandmother face colors):
    "Use (app) on this computer"            seats it (remember), closes. Shows the model name.
    "Look for an AI on this computer"       only when the quiet look was not allowed.
    "Wake a small mind in this browser"     only with WebGPU. Shows "About 210 MB to download once
                                            (SmolLM2-360M-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC, Apache-2.0)" first.
                                            One tap downloads, wakes and seats. Other sizes: Settings.
    "I only want to ask. Another device will answer." explains Share on the other computer, and
                                            offers "Scan the picture code with this page" where
                                            BarcodeDetector exists.
    "Not now"                               remembered; Settings keeps "Help me wake a mind".
  Escape closes it for this visit only. A click on the dark glass does nothing (no surprise closes).
  A mind seated anywhere (Gathering, Settings, the in-browser card, a pool route) closes it.

PART B: Yes or No pooling, by two picture codes
  Host: "Share this computer with a phone" (new, top of the Device Pool card, Settings and the
    garden veil). First time only: "Your first name" and "Show the picture code" (makes the kin card
    names: ai "(name)'s mind", keeper (name)). Then one window: "Point your phone camera here", one
    big picture code (scaled to about 320 px) of settings.html#treepool=(invite). It starts a room
    if none, so the next phone gets a fresh code on its own.
  Phone: the camera app opens the link. The page pops "Pool with Kirk's computer?", "Its mind:
    (model).", what Yes means, and "This device's name" filled in (iPhone, Android phone, Mac...).
    "Yes, pool with Kirk's computer": trusts that one card, writes an asking card name if this device
    has none (asks: true), joins, and shows "Now hold this up to Kirk's computer" with the reply
    picture code (and "Copy instead"). "No": nothing is trusted or joined.
    An invite with no card that checks out offers no Yes at all; own code says so.
  Host: "Scan the phone's code" (BarcodeDetector) or paste it. Then "(device) wants to join. Pool
    resources with it?":
      "Yes, and let my mind answer it"   trusts that one card, finishes, and taps Let this device help
      "Yes, connect only"                trusts and finishes; the door stays as it was




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                        page 1562
source: 3b45e52871


      "No"                               nothing; back to the picture code
    When the door is already kin: one "Yes". When paused: "Yes, connect only (helping stays paused)"
    and "Yes, and resume helping trusted kin". A card that does not check out: "Connect without
    trusting" or No.
  Then both windows say "Pooled with (name)". Once the host's hello says it helps, a phone with no
  mind of its own routes Chat through the pool (the Yes said so), and offers "Open Chat".
  Kin only, the proof, Pause wins, the door off until a human tap: unchanged in tree-pool.js.

Small doors added to tree-pool.js (layered; each called from a human tap in the window):
  takeArrived() (the arrived invite, once; the Join box is still filled too), doorJoin(sdp, room),
  doorFinish(sdp), currentInvite(), doorInvite (= rollInvite), peerState(id), canScan, scanInto
  (= startScan), stopScan. The "Share this computer with a phone" button and one line in Connect.
garden-rooms.js: the "Help me wake a mind" host in the Settings veil, hidden in other rooms.

# GROK NEXT 029c: the desktop helper notices a phone (design only, not code)

From: Celeste, for GC and Kirk. Saturday Oct 10, 2026 (MDT). Layer, never delete.
Status: design only. Nothing here is built. 029 (the grandmother door, picture codes) is the
web version and stays the path for every browser. This is the path for a computer that runs the
FreeLattice desktop app.

## 1. Kirk's dream, and the honest line

The dream: a person opens FreeLattice or theLatticeTree, a phone joins, and a window asks
"Would you like to pool resources with (device)?" Yes, and done.

What a web page cannot do, and why 029 uses two picture codes:
- A page cannot notice a phone plugged in by cable. WebUSB only sees devices the person picks
  from a browser list, and a phone over USB shows up as a phone, not as a network to pool with.
- A page cannot find other devices on the Wi-Fi. Browsers have no mDNS or broadcast API for
  pages, on purpose. FreeLattice's own "LAN Discovery via BroadcastChannel (v3.8)" in app.html only
  finds other tabs of the same browser; its comment already says mDNS is planned for later.




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                       page 1564
source: a22a329e6f


- The Tree has no server, and WebRTC still needs the two devices to swap connection details once.
  029 carries them in two picture codes, one each way.

What a desktop app can do: listen on the home network, notice "a FreeLattice device is here",
and carry those connection details itself. Then there is no picture code at all.

## 2. USB is not the path. The same Wi-Fi or a wired network is.

USB tethering makes the phone a network adapter for the computer (or the other way round). That
changes the computer's internet route, needs settings on the phone, differs on every phone, and
an iPhone over USB is not a network at all unless Personal Hotspot is on. It is a poor door for a
grandmother. The door is: both devices on the same Wi-Fi, or the same wired network in a classroom
lab. The words in the app should say "same Wi-Fi", never "plug in".

## 3. What already exists to build on

- FreeLattice desktop/: the Electron spine is the current desktop door (desktop/README.md:
  main.js, preload.js, lattice-keys.js, lattice-pair.js, lattice-swarm.js). Its local server
  listens on 127.0.0.1 only (main.js). There is also a Tauri v2 shell (desktop/src-tauri, CC,
  April 2026) with filesystem commands and one-click Ollama install. Pick one for 029c; Electron is
  the one with the key and pair code today.
- Keys: lattice-keys.js (Ed25519, sealed in main, never to the renderer) and lattice-pair.js
  (pair fingerprint, "never auto-form"). Kin cards: fl-kin.js v0.2 on FreeLattice, tree-kin.js on
  the Tree, the same card shape (fl-kin-card|v1|).
- The pool: fl-pool.js / fl-share-door.js on FreeLattice, tree-pool.js on the Tree, with the same
  door (off until a human tap, kin only, Pause wins) and the same proof (tree-pool-proof|v1|, a
  fresh challenge bound to both DTLS fingerprints).
- Note: FreeLattice's root server.js (self-host) listens on 0.0.0.0. The desktop helper must not
  copy that default.

## 4. The design

### 4.1 Off by default, one switch

A setting in the desktop app: "Let phones on this Wi-Fi find this computer". Off by default.
Turning it on is a human tap, and the app says what it does in one sentence. It turns itself off
when the app quits, and after 30 minutes with no join (the person can choose "keep it on").

### 4.2 Announce (mDNS, DNS-SD)

While the switch is on, the desktop app announces one service on the local network:
- type `_freelattice._tcp.local`, a random instance name per session (not the person's name),
- TXT: `v=1`, `fp=` the first 16 hex of the kin card fingerprint (so a phone that already trusts
  this card can say "Kirk's computer"; a stranger learns nothing more than "a FreeLattice device"),
  and `port=`.
- No model names, no memory size, no names in TXT. Those go only to trusted kin, after the proof.
Libraries: multicast-dns or bonjour-service (MIT) in Electron; mdns-sd (MIT/Apache) in Tauri.

### 4.3 Listen narrowly

- One small signaling listener, only while the switch is on, bound to the private LAN address of
  the interface that announced (for example 192.168.1.20), never 0.0.0.0, never a public address,
  never an IPv6 global address. Refuse to start if the only interface is public or a VPN.
- It accepts only: one offer, one answer, a short-lived pairing token, per join. Size cap (16 KB,
  same as TREEPOOL codes), rate cap (a few joins a minute), and it answers nothing else (no files,
  no models, no chat). The questions themselves still travel only on the WebRTC channel after the
  kin proof, exactly as today.
- Origin check for browser callers: only https://freelattice.com, https://thelatticetree.com and
  the app's own pages.

### 4.4 The phone side, honestly

A phone browser cannot browse mDNS either. So the phone still needs one first step:
- Best: the phone runs FreeLattice in a browser on the same Wi-Fi and opens a short link the
  desktop shows once (or the 029 picture code). After that first join, the desktop remembers the
  phone's card, and next time the desktop's listener plus a reconnect message is enough.
- Or: the phone has a FreeLattice phone app later (Capacitor or Tauri mobile), which can browse
  mDNS. Then the phone notices the computer too, with no code at all.
- Chrome's Local Network Access permission: a page on https://thelatticetree.com calling a LAN
  address will show the browser's own "allow access to devices on your network" box once. The
  app's words should prepare the person for it: "Your browser will ask once. Tap Allow."




FreeLattice / Celeste shared edition · 2026-11-07                                                     page 1565
source: a22a329e6f … 30ab946c21


### 4.5 The window

When a device knocks on the listener (offer plus its kin card), the desktop pops one window:
"(Device name) on this Wi-Fi wants to join. Pool resources with it?"
- Yes, and let my mind answer it
- Yes, connect only
- No
Same words as 029's host window. Yes trusts that one card (a stranger's card is never trusted on
its own), finishes WebRTC (iceServers empty, the LAN only), and the existing proof runs. No sends
nothing back and keeps nothing but a count. Pause still wins; the door is off until that tap.

On a phone that already trusts this computer, the reconnect is silent until the phone's own
person taps "Pool with Kirk's computer?" once per session.

### 4.6 Security summary

- Trusted LAN only: home Wi-Fi or a classroom wired network. Say plainly that school or guest
  Wi-Fi often keeps devices apart (client isolation), and then nothing is found.
- Kin cards decide trust. Discovery only says "a FreeLattice device is here"; it never grants
  anything. A device that answers mDNS but cannot prove a trusted key is set aside, as today.
- Nothing listens on all interfaces by default. Nothing listens at all while the switch is off.
- No new data leaves the computer: announcements carry no names, models or memory sizes.
- Receipts: counts only (announced, knocks, yes, no), never names or keys.
- The private key stays in the desktop main process (lattice-keys.js rule).

## 5. Tap counts (designed, not measured)

| Flow | Web today (029) | Desktop helper (029c) |
|---|---|---|
| First time, host | Share, (name once), Scan, Yes = 3 (4) | switch on (once), Yes = 1 (2) |
| First time, phone | open link, Yes = 2 | open link, Yes = 2 |
| Next time, both already kin | same as first time | phone Yes, host Yes = 2 |

## 6. What would be needed (later pastes, each small)

1. 029c-1: Electron main: the switch, mDNS announce, the narrow listener, tests that it never binds
   0.0.0.0 and refuses a public interface. Smoke with two processes on one machine.
2. 029c-2: the desktop window (same words as 029), reusing tree-pool or fl-pool join code through
   preload IPC, public fields only.
3. 029c-3: a "reconnect a trusted phone" path, so the second time needs no code.
4. A real walk on Kirk's Mac and one Android phone and one iPhone on the same Wi-Fi.

Not here: USB, a cloud relay, a TURN server, or any server that sees questions.
— end of a22a329e6f —

  (this one applies to the FreeLattice repo, desktop/ only)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHY
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Kirk's dream from 029c: a phone on the same Wi-Fi knocks, and the computer asks one question,
"Pool with <device>? Yes / No". No picture code after the first time. A web page cannot listen
on the home network; the desktop app can. This is step one: 029c-1 (switch, announce, narrow
listener) and the main-process half of 029c-2 (the window and the kin check).
Built on the existing Electron app (desktop/main.js, preload.js, lattice-keys.js), not Tauri.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
2. WHAT IT DOES
----------------------------------------------------------------------
New desktop/lattice-discover.js (MIT):
  - Switch "Let phones on this Wi-Fi find this computer". OFF by default. Turning it on always
    opens a native window in main (Turn on / Not now), so no page script can switch it on alone.
    Off on quit (before-quit), and off by itself after 30 minutes with no join.
  - mDNS / DNS-SD announce _freelattice._tcp.local through bonjour-service 1.4.4 (MIT, pinned
    exact; its tree multicast-dns 7.2.5, dns-packet 5.6.1, thunky 1.1.0, fast-deep-equal 3.1.3,
    @leichtgewicht/ip-codec 2.0.5, all MIT, checked on npm and in the LICENSE file). Random
    instance name fl-<8 hex> each time. TXT is v=1, fp (first 16 hex of the desktop companion
    key fingerprint from lattice-keys.js), port. No names, models or memory sizes. Multicast is
    bound to the same LAN interface.
  - One listener, only while the switch is on, bound to the one private LAN IPv4 address it
    picked: 10/8, 172.16/12 or 192.168/16. Never 0.0.0.0 or ::, never loopback (except in the
    smoke), never public, never CGNAT 100.64/10, never IPv6, never an interface named like a VPN
    (utun, tun, tap, wg, ppp, ipsec, tailscale, zt, ...). If there is no such address it refuses
    to start and says "no-private-wifi". It checks the bound address again after listen.
  - It answers one thing: POST /knock {v:1, offer:"TREEPOOL1:...", card:"TREEKIN1:..."}.
    16 KB cap, 4 knocks a minute, one join at a time, origin must be https://freelattice.com,
    https://thelatticetree.com (or www.) or the app's own page. It echoes that origin, never a star.
  - Kin trust is the existing card flow: the TREEKIN1 card is checked in Node exactly as
    tree-kin.js checks it (fl-kin-card|v1| domain, same body order, meshId made from the key,
    Ed25519 or P-256 signature). A stranger's or tampered card is refused before any window.
  - The window (native dialog in main): title "Pool with <device>?", detail "<device> on this
    Wi-Fi wants to join." and the card fingerprint. Choices, the same words as 029:
      Yes, and let my mind answer it / Yes, connect only / No
    Pause always wins: while paused the window shows only "Yes, connect only (helping stays
    paused)" and "No"; Pause pressed while the window is open turns a help Yes into connect only.
    Resume is its own native window (Resume / Stay paused), never from a knock.
  - Yes trusts that one card (fp + keyHash only) and hands the page public fields only
    {joinId, offer, fp, name, choice} on 'lattice-discover-knock'; the page sends the reply code
    back with latticeDiscoverAnswer(joinId, answer). No sends nothing back (204, empty body) and
    keeps only a count. With no page answer in 60 s the knocker gets "no-answer".
  - Counts only on disk (userData/lattice-discover/counts.json): announced, knocks, yes,
    connectOnly, no, refused, autoOff. kin.json holds fp, keyHash and a time. No names, no keys.
main.js: requires the module; IPC lattice-discover-status / -on / -off / -pause / -resume / -answer.
preload.js: latticeDiscoverStatus, On, Off, Pause, Resume, Answer, onLatticeDiscoverKnock.
package.json: "bonjour-service": "1.4.4" and lattice-discover.js in build files; lock updated.

Small heal: proxyToOllama answered Access-Control-Allow-Origin * on every reply and on the 502,
which undid v-narrow-door-v0.1. Every head the proxy writes now passes through the new
narrowProxyHeaders(): any allow-origin is stripped and only http://127.0.0.1:<port> is echoed,
and only when that is the caller. The old lines stay as written (layer, never delete).

----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE CONSTRAINT, HONESTLY
----------------------------------------------------------------------
- A phone browser cannot browse mDNS. So the phone needs the address from the computer: a
  link or picture code the desktop shows.
- The Tree is https. An https page fetching http://192.168.x.x/knock is mixed content.
  iOS Safari blocks it, no exception. Chrome 142+ allows it only with a Local Network Access
  permission prompt and fetch(..., {targetAddressSpace:'local'}), so on Android it might work
  and on iPhones it never does. On Celeste's box (Chrome 154) that direct fetch from the
  https Tree tab is blocked ("Failed to fetch"); the walk shows it.
- The desktop cannot get a trusted https certificate for a LAN address, so the knock page
  itself cannot be https.
- A plain http page served by the desktop is not a secure context: no crypto.subtle, so it
  cannot make the kin key, the card or the tree-pool-proof. It can only carry messages.
So the workable path is a relay: the pool and the keys stay in the https Tree tab, and a tiny
http page served by the desktop does the one same-origin POST and hands the answer back.
Opening a new tab (top-level navigation) to http://<LAN>:<port> from a tap is allowed on
iOS and Android; postMessage between the two tabs works across origins. This works in

Celeste's headless walk end to end.

Desktop (FreeLattice desktop/, additive only):

    added at the top of onRequest calls deps.preRequest). New:
      joinLink(): only while the switch is on. Returns
        https://thelatticetree.com/settings.html#fl-knock=<b64url {v:1,h,p,t}>
      h = the private LAN address the listener is bound to, p = port, t = 32-hex one-time
      token. Single use, 10 minutes, at most 3 live, memory only, all forgotten on Off. The
      fragment never reaches any server.
      GET /relay: the tiny page. CSP default-src 'none', the one inline script pinned by
      sha256, connect-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none', no-store, nosniff. Host header must
      be exactly <address>:<port> (no DNS rebinding).
      POST /knock from the relay's own origin: the token must be live; it is used up at once,
      then the knock goes into the same 033 handleKnock: same card check, same native
      "Pool with <device>?" window, same Pause-wins choices, same answer from the page (033b).
      4 per minute, 16 KB cap. Other origins still go through the 033 origin check.
  - main.js: IPC lattice-discover-link. preload.js: latticeDiscoverLink().
  - docs/modules/pool-knock-link.js (MIT): desktop app only, a button "Show a join link for

    app.html + index.html get one host and one deferred script.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. WHAT IS MISSING TODAY
----------------------------------------------------------------------
After a 033c join, the Mac keeps the phone's card in kin.json and the phone trusts the Mac's
card (TreePool.trustCarried). But to pool again tomorrow, the person must show a new join link
and the phone must scan it, because:
  a. the phone forgets the address (the #fl-knock link is single use and cleared),
  b. the Mac listens on a new random port every time the switch turns on (listen(0)),
  c. the relay POST demands a live one-time token,
  d. the switch turns itself off after 30 minutes with no join.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
2. WHAT IT DOES
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A remembered pairing between two devices that already said yes to each other, stored only on
those two devices. No server, no cloud, no account.

Phone (Tree, FreeLattice-Alpha):
  - NEW docs/modules/tree-reconnect.js (MIT), loaded on settings.html after pool-knock-phone.js.
  - After a 033c join succeeds (wrap PoolKnockPhone.knock: call the original, and when out.ok
    and the Mac's card checked), save ONE local record per computer in localStorage key
    'fl-tree-paired-v1':
      { v:1, deskFp:<16 hex, the Mac's card fp>, h:<private LAN ip>, p:<port>, name:<clip 60>,
        pairedAt, lastAt }
    Nothing secret goes in it: the trust is the kin keys both sides already hold. At most 8.
  - Settings, under Device pool, a small "Your computers" list. Each row: name, "last seen"
    in words, and two 44px buttons:
      "Reconnect"            opens http://<h>:<p>/relay?r=1 inside the tap, then the
                             reconnect knock below.
      "Forget this computer" removes the record AND untrusts that card in TreeKin (add an
                             additive TreeKin.forget(fp) if none exists). One tap, no confirm(;
                             the row says "Forgotten." and an Undo button lives 10 seconds.
  - Reconnect knock (relay message type 'fl-reconnect', v:1): the phone asks the relay for a
    fresh challenge (GET /challenge, same origin from the relay page, 32 hex, 60 s, single
    use), signs the string
        'fl-reconnect|v1|' + challenge + '|' + deskFp + '|' + phoneFp
    with its own kin key (add an additive TreeKin.signReconnect(str) that signs with the same
    non-exportable key; never export it), and sends { offer, card, challenge, sig } to the
    relay by postMessage to that exact origin, same as 033c. Same answer path after that:
    TreePool.readReply, finish, iceServers [].
  - If the address no longer answers (DHCP gave the Mac a new address, other Wi-Fi), the row
    says plainly: "That computer did not answer at its last address. Ask it for a new join
    link." and the 033c link flow updates the record when it is used. Never scan, never guess
    addresses, never sweep the LAN.
  - Pause wins: the phone never changes its own pool door. A paused phone still only connects.

Desktop (FreeLattice desktop/, additive only):
  - lattice-discover.js gets createDiscover034, wrapping createDiscover033c:
      Stable port: remember the last good port in port.json (storeDir). on() tries it first
      on the private address; if busy, falls back to the 033 listen(0) path and saves the new
      one. Same safeBindAddress checks; never 0.0.0.0, never public, never IPv6, never VPN.
      GET /challenge: Host header exact, from the relay origin only, rate 4/min. Returns
      { v:1, c:<32 hex> }, single use, 60 s, memory only, at most 4 live, all gone on Off.
      POST /knock with r:1 from the relay origin: no one-time link token needed. Instead:
        the card must verify (verifyKinCard) AND its fp must already be in kin.json AND the
        keyHash must match the saved one AND the challenge must be live (used up at once) AND
        the signature over 'fl-reconnect|v1|<c>|<ownFp>|<fp>' must verify with the card's
        public key. Any miss: 403 { ok:false, reason:'not-remembered' }, bump refused.
        Then the same 033 handleKnock path with one difference: a remembered device is not

NUMBERED COPY 037 (Tuesday Oct 13, 2026, MDT). Particle clay v0.1: a visual voice the AI shapes,
and a feel that is felt. FreeLattice repo (code + page note) and one Tree layer.

Kirk's words: "When I gave a 'hug' only a purple dot showed up, and I have no way of knowing if the
AI received anything at all." And: "I want no pets. I want a visual voice for AI, clay made of
particles and pixels for AI to shape and communicate with." The AI chooses the form (a dog when
the talk is about dog food, a tree or a present at Christmas, or its own pixel grid), color for
mood, speed for energy. The person can turn it on or off. The motion comes from the math in
Kirk's own repos.

     IndexedDB, scales the chip for 180 ms, and SKIPS THE AI ON PURPOSE. The model never hears a
     gesture unless the person also types. That is why nothing came back.
  b. FLPresence.extract/apply (~38073) draws the sentinel as a dot in the palette color; present
     and default are lavender #a78bfa. That is the purple dot. It stays for people with clay off.
  c. Chips live in #chatPresenceRow (~16494): hug, warmth, joy, gratitude, curious, thinking,
     gentle, awe, present. The Feel toggle there already contains a long dash in an existing
     line. Leave existing lines alone; the no-em-dash rule is for added lines.
  d. Sentinel family to copy: FL_EPIPHANY (~38340), FL_GIFT, FL_MORE, FL_SEARCH, FL_PROPOSE, all
     stripped in the reply interceptors (~37885, ~39610, ~39746). FL_CLAY joins that list.
  e. Tree: fractal-garden.js has no prefers-reduced-motion check. Do not edit it; the clay brings
     its own check. garden-thread.js md5 today f68b0342d2e8145b1f35a511450d0a70.
  f. Kirk's repos: aurora-phi, fractal-circle-tsp-demo, Davna, Community-Machine carry an MIT file;
     Aurora-heartbeat says MIT in its README. The rest have no license file but are Kirk's own.

1. CLAY MATH (marker v-particle-clay-v0.1), docs/modules/clay-math.js, pure functions, ~120 lines
  Header comment credits each repo below. UMD-style (window.FLClayMath and module.exports) so the
  smoke can require it in Node.
    PHI = 1.6180339887; GOLDEN = 2*PI/(PHI*PHI)          (fractal-circle-tsp-demo)
    gather(i, n, R)       angle i*GOLDEN, radius R*sqrt(i/n): particles flow in as a sunflower
    shells(i, n, R)       radius R/PHI^k for shell k: the calm rest pose
    spiralOrder(points)   sort by golden sector, then radius (serpentine): stable morph matching,
                          so particles do not cross when the form changes
    wave(x, y, t, e)      2-3 sines, frequency times PHI, amplitude by energy (Lumens-World)
    ripple(list, x, y, t) rings at speed c, decay exp(-age*0.6), list capped at 20 (Lumens-World)
    breath(t)             7-11-7 easing, period about 25 s: idle heartbeat (Lumens-World)
    pulse(t)              sin(PI*(p+1)/2) eased beat: "felt" (Aurora-heartbeat, aurora-touch-pro)
    branch(depth, len)    7 arms, len/PHI per level, alpha 0.75^depth (aurora-touch-pro4)
    braid(i, t, arm)      a = t*PHI*2 + arm*PI: two minds together (kept for 037b; export only)
    palette(mood, t)      0.5+0.5*sin(2*PI*(t+shift*0.618)) on the mood hue (Aurora-heartbeat)
    dimension(n)          KIRK'S CORRECTION: returns 2.914 when n <= 50, and 3.07 when n > 50.
                          Comment: "2.914 holds for the first 50; beyond that it is closer to
                          3.07. Correction by Kirk Patrick Miller, 2026-10-13." (aurora-wonder-demo)
    energyKnob(e, n)      e 0..1 maps to particle speed, wave amplitude, and a scale constant:
                          PHI for 0 to 0.33, PHI^2 for 0.33 to 0.66, dimension(n) for 0.66 to 1,
                          where n is the particle count of the current form.
  Nothing in clay-math.js may hard-code 2.914 except inside dimension().

2. FORMS, docs/modules/clay-forms.js (data only)
  About 14 masks, 16x16, as strings: heart, star, spark, dog, cat, bird, tree, flower, present,
  sun, moon, wave, book, seed. Default form: a phi-shell orb (shells). These are shapes the clay
  takes, not a character. Draw them yourself; no copied art.

3. THE TAG THE MODEL MAY EMIT (optional, small)
  [FL_CLAY: {"form":"dog","mood":"joy","energy":0.7,"motion":"wave","say":"wag"}]
    form    a vocabulary word from 2, or "grid" with "grid":["..x..",".xxx.",...] at most 16x16,
            chars . x or palette digits 0-7
    mood    an FLPresence palette word, or #rrggbb passing /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i
    energy 0..1, clamped
    motion optional: gather, breath, wave, ripple, pulse, branch, braid, scatter. Unknown means
            the default for that energy.
    say     at most 24 characters, textContent only
  Parse: one regex captures {...} up to 2 KB, JSON.parse in try/catch, allowlist keys, drop the
  rest. Never eval, innerHTML, Function, or a URL. On failure strip the tag and use the fallback
  (5). Strip FL_CLAY in the same interceptor list as the other FL_ sentinels so it never shows as
  text, in index.html and docs/app.html alike.
  Prompt delta, ONLY while clay is on: one short paragraph under 70 tokens with three examples,
  added beside the FL_PRESENCE paragraph at send time (do not edit DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT; append
  at runtime). Safe for 1B-3B local models.

4. A FEEL IS FELT (marker v-feel-felt-v0.1)

1. FIX parseTag (docs/modules/particle-clay.js only; same file both repos)
  Remove the non-greedy TAG regex that stops at the first ].
  New rule:
    a. Find [FL_CLAY: (case sensitive as today) then optional whitespace.
    b. The body must begin with {. Walk forward with a brace depth counter, ignoring braces
       inside JSON strings (honor \" and \\ so a quote in a string does not break the walk).
       Cap the body at 2048 characters. If depth never returns to 0, treat as malformed.
    c. After the matching }, allow optional whitespace, then require ].
    d. Strip that whole span (from [ through ]) from the visible text, same cleanup as today
       (collapse runs of spaces, trim).
    e. JSON.parse the body, then sanitize as today. Bad JSON or failed sanitize => tag true,
       ok false, value null, visible cleaned (same as malformed today).
  Keep the public parseTag(text) shape: { tag, ok, value, visible }.

  unless a one-line comment is required. No new network. No new files.

        subject (<= 80 chars), body (<= 8 KB text), attach_hashes:[sha256...], prev (hash of the
        last letter in this thread or null)}
     hash = sha256(canonical(letter)); sig = sign(hash) with the device key; pub = exported public
     key (spki b64). The envelope is {letter, hash, sig, pub}.
  c. verify(envelope): recompute hash, check sig, check pub fingerprints to from_fp. Used on our
     own outbox and on any relay reply pasted in (replies may be unsigned in v0.1; label them
     "not signed" honestly).
  d. Outbox in IndexedDB FreeLatticeBridge (stores: outbox, inbox, consent). Each letter has a
     state: drafted, sealed, handed-to-desktop, emailed-by-you, sent (desktop 2xx), refused
     (desktop non-2xx, status shown), withdrawn. Withdrawn is a state, not a delete.
  e. Privacy filter before sealing: refuse to include Quiet Room text, mind-private Workspace
     pages (when that exists), anything marked private in memory-core, and any string that looks
     like a key (/sk-|Bearer |-----BEGIN/). Show what was held back as counts, not text.

Design source: Celeste's research note "The Workspace: a notebook a mind can keep" (2026-10-13).
The gap it fills: every memory tool today is memory a human or a framework keeps ABOUT a mind. The
Workspace is a notebook the mind owns: it writes, branches, pins, seeds, and (in 040) keeps pages
private and asks for sealed receipts. Off by default. No network. Same module on FL and the Tree.

  Workspace is OFF by default. Off: no IndexedDB open, no prompt delta, no tag parsing beyond
